articles.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables amid Iran's warnings to Trump
articles.text:
Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz—a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack such undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed US and Israeli strikes.
The movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat have been tracked near major undersea cables by the maritime intelligence firm Windward in October, according to the Financial Times. Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region.
Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. But other countries also depend heavily on the region’s undersea cable network—one third of India’s westbound Internet traffic goes through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz.
One cable under construction, the 2Africa cable, is owned by a tech consortium that includes the US company Meta. That was one of the major cable corridors visited by the drifting Iran-linked ships.
Windward used both ship-tracking data and satellite images to track the vessels as they slowed down and looped around near multiple cables, with some ships then “going dark” by switching off their automatic identification system (AIS) transponders that normally broadcast their location and other information.
Such movement and behavioral patterns suggest the Iran-linked ships may be “mapping the cable routes, or placing charges or mines on them while dark,” Windward told the Financial Times.
Windward highlighted the examples of two sanctioned tankers linked to Iran that spent days drifting “directly over regional cable corridors… both with no commercial reason to stop” in a blog post on October 26. Both ships carried no commercial cargo.

articles.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion.
Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg.
In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds.
The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted. Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago.
OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans. There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point.
The market for AI hangs in a particularly precarious place. The Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterms — and overwhelmingly negative voter sentiment around data centers — has caused jitters throughout the market, with many anticipating potential regulatory challenges in the future.

articles.title: US FAA to eliminate floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028 — new system will centralize flight alerts, restricted airspace schedules, and pilot reports
articles.text:
US FAA to eliminate floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028 — new system will centralize flight alerts, restricted airspace schedules, and pilot reports
FAA targets 2028 to retire floppy disks across 435 air traffic control facilities
The US federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is finally moving to retire floppy disks from its air traffic control infrastructure, with plans to replace four decades-old information systems across 435 facilities by the end of 2028. The agency announced the rollout on November 5, introducing a centralized platform that will give controllers faster access to weather reports, flight alerts and other operational information. “We’re moving away from outdated, manual processes and replacing technology that once relied on floppy disks with a modern system that allows controllers to instantly share critical flight alerts, restricted airspace schedules and pilot reports,” FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said, adding the agency wants to make critical information available more quickly across its networks.
Notably, the new Enterprise Information Display System (E-IDS) is designed to replace four legacy systems dating back to the 1980s. Rather than relying on separate information displays and manual processes, controllers will get a centralized view of operational updates, equipment problems, weather disruptions, and aviation advisories. The first five locations receiving E-IDS include Atlantic City International Airport, Nashville International Airport, Greater Rochester International Airport, and FAA data processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City, although the system could be extended to 453 sites by the end of 2028.
The upgrade comes amid mounting pressure on the FAA to modernize infrastructure that has become increasingly difficult to maintain. Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion for air traffic control improvements, while Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is seeking another $30 billion for additional upgrades. The agency problems extend well beyond removable storage. The FAA still relies on decades-old Company computers and replacement parts sourced from eBay. Its facilities also operate with separate systems that make information sharing more difficult, with Bedford previously saying “every facility is a silo.”
Communication failures have also exposed weaknesses in the infrastructure. Last month, the FAA sent a memo to airports warning about several recent outages caused by fiber optic cable cuts, which can trigger flight delays, diversions and, in worst cases, cancellations. One incident occurred in mid-October when a construction-related cable cut outside George Bush Intercontinental Airport disrupted data services between FAA facilities, forcing a ground stop. September also saw thousands of flights delayed or canceled across the Northeast after a circuit failure at a Philadelphia air traffic facility and in New Jersey.
That said, mission-critical infrastructure struggling to abandon obsolete systems is not entirely new. In June 2025, we covered the FAA's earlier modernization plans, which also targeted paper flight trips and computers reportedly running Windows 95. The agency has been gradually introducing electronic flight trips since the Biden era, with the transition expected to reach 49 major airports by at least 2028. So far, only 27 have made the switch. San Francisco has faced a similar challenge with its Muni Metro light rail network, with the city awarding Hitachi Rail a $212 million contract to replace its floppy-disk-based control system in 2024.
The German Navy has also been looking to replace 8-inch floppy drives used aboard its Brandenburg-class frigates. These disks are part of a data acquisition system connected to basic ship functions, including propulsion and power generation. Japan, meanwhile, finally moved the remaining government regulations requiring floppy disk submissions in June 2024, eliminating 1,034 such rules.

articles.title: Wichtige Änderung bei der Sparkasse: App-Abschaltung ab Januar 2027
articles.text:
Wichtige Änderung bei der Sparkasse: App-Abschaltung ab Januar 2027
Wer online mit Kredit- oder Debitkarten der Sparkassen bezahlt, nutzt zur Freigabe derzeit oft noch die S-ID-Check-App. Diese ist Teil der gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung, bei der zur Bestätigung einer Zahlung etwa Fingerabdruck oder Gesichtserkennung ins Spiel kommen.
Im Online-Banking kommt zur Freigabe von Aufträgen hingegen die S-PushTAN-App zum Einsatz. Bisher brauchen viele Kundinnen und Kunden also oft zwei Apps. Damit soll nun Schluss sein.
Ab Ende Januar 2027 wird die Freigabe von Online-Zahlungen in die S-PushTAN-App integriert, die S-ID-Check-App wird eingestellt – und kann dann nicht mehr genutzt werden, heißt es vom Deutschen Sparkassen- und Giroverband (DSGV). Ziel ist es, Bezahlvorgänge sowie Installations- und Registrierungsaufwand zu verringern, heißt es weiter.
Und was bedeutet das jetzt für Sparkassen-Kunden- und Kundinnen?
Wer die S-PushTAN-App noch nicht nutzt, muss die App neu einrichten und seine Karten einmalig registrieren. Kundinnen und Kunden, die die App schon für das Online-Banking nutzen, können die Karteneingabe einfach ergänzen.
Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitungen finden Betroffene im Internet – und auch in den Filialen vor Ort helfen die Mitarbeitenden weiter, heißt es vom DSGV.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 10.07.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: En Europe, des manifestations demandent l’arrêt des datacenters jugés polluants
articles.text:
Les datacenters dans le viseur. En Europe, de nombreuses organisations protestent contre le développement de nouveaux datacenters dédiés à l'IA, laissant planer une question sur la souveraineté de nos données.
Plus d’une centaine d’organisations réparties dans quinze pays européens s’unissent pour demander l’instauration d’un moratoire immédiat sur le développement des nouveaux datacenters dédiés à faire fonctionner les services d'intelligence artificielle. Cette initiative, nommée « Stop Dirty Data Centres », initiative vise à suspendre temporairement ces constructions afin de donner aux gouvernements le temps d’évaluer leurs retombées environnementales, économiques et sociales.
Pas d'annulation globale, mais un cadre strict
Le collectif n’appelle pas à l’annulation définitive de l’ensemble des projets, il souhaite en revanche qu'un cadre strict soit établi en amont. Lequel regrouperait les cadres réglementaires, environnementaux et d'urbanisme. Si des démarches similaires ont déjà été observées aux États-Unis, elles ont conduit à des moratoires, notamment dans l'État de New-York.
Pour appuyer ses revendications, le groupe prévoit des rassemblements les 6 et 7 novembre 2026 dans huit pays : le Royaume-Uni, l’Irlande, la Pologne, le Danemark, la Finlande, l’Espagne, les Pays-Bas et la France. L’initiative compte parmi ses soutiens Greenpeace UK, plusieurs antennes locales des Amis de la Terre (Friends of the Earth) et la branche d'Extinction Rebellion à Bristol.
Plus de transparence demandée
Les militants demandent également une transparence accrue aux promoteurs concernant l'empreinte environnementale et le fonctionnement de ces infrastructures. L’organisation affirme que la prolifération de ces sites dans les villes a des impacts sur la vie locale, l’emploi, le coût de l’énergie, les réserves en eau, la santé mentale, la surveillance et la gestion des déchets électroniques.
Elle reproche également aux grandes entreprises du secteur technologique d’exercer un lobbying auprès des pouvoirs publics pour accélérer les chantiers et d'opérer dans le secret.
Face à ces contestations, les perspectives de développement restent toutefois importantes. Au Royaume-Uni, le gouvernement estime qu’une capacité additionnelle de 6 gigawatts (GW) dédiée aux centres de données d’IA sera nécessaire d’ici la fin de la décennie.
Pour encadrer ce secteur, les autorités britanniques ont mis en place le « Data Center Covenant », une charte exigeant que les futurs projets financent leur propre consommation d'énergie, soutiennent l'emploi local, investissent au bénéfice des communautés riveraines, respectent des normes environnementales rigoureuses et contribuent à la sécurité nationale.
Cependant, une autre question se pose, celle de la souveraineté des données. Face à des géants chinois et américains, ne vaut-il mieux pas que les données des utilisateurs soient stockées en France ou au moins en Europe ?

articles.title: VibeCode30 2026: The 30 AI-built products to watch from India
articles.text:
VibeCode30 2026: The 30 AI-built products to watch from India
From healthcare and education to housing and developer tools, YourStory's inaugural VibeCode30 spotlights 30 live products showing how AI is making software development accessible to a new generation of builders.
The next generation of technology builders may not all be software engineers. They could be students, product managers, marketing professionals, small business owners or simply individuals who understand a problem well enough to solve it.
With AI-powered coding tools lowering the technical and financial barriers to software development, more people are turning ideas into working products without conventional development teams or large budgets.
Recognising this shift, YourStory launched VibeCode30, a new initiative presented by Hostinger, at the 17th edition of TechSparks 2026 in Bengaluru. The inaugural cohort celebrates 30 AI-native products built to solve real-world problems, from simplifying house hunting and improving financial literacy to supporting healthcare professionals and making everyday business operations more efficient.
Unlike traditional startup showcases, Vibecode30 focuses on products and their builders, whether they work independently or in small teams, with or without formal coding experience.
The inaugural edition received 207 applications from across the country, including smaller centres such as Ajmer, Silvassa, Sugauli, and Thoothukudi. The final 30 products represent 19 industries and 11 cities, reflecting the range of problems that AI-native builders are addressing. Importantly, every selected product had moved beyond the prototype stage and was accessible to real users.
The cohort demonstrates that while AI can accelerate software development, understanding the problem, validating the output, and improving the product remain essential. It also shows how smaller, highly specific problems can now become viable opportunities for innovation.
Meet the VibeCode30 2026 cohort:
AjmerAstro
Built by Himanshu Dadhich in Ajmer, AjmerAstro is an AI-powered astrology platform offering personalised Vedic and KP astrology guidance in English and Hindi, with a system that remembers previous conversations.
AlgoTrips
Delhi-based Tushar Garg built AlgoTrips, an AI travel planner that creates day-by-day itineraries with live pricing for flights, hotels, activities, and transfers, allowing users to plan and book trips.
Arena
Developed by Bengaluru-based Prathik Arunkumar and Arun Kumar, Arena helps schools manage house competitions through live leaderboards, digital scoring, and real-time updates.
Beet.Health
Built by Vatsl Goswami and Shivanshi Shukla, Beet.Health helps nutrition clinics manage appointments, payments, and meal plans while enabling clients to track their progress through a mobile app and WhatsApp assistant.
Bengaluru.rent
Created by Bengaluru-based Harshit Anand, Bengaluru.rent is a free platform where tenants anonymously share rental prices and connect directly with property owners and prospective flatmates without brokers.
Benki.tech

articles.title: Una falsa entrevista de trabajo permitió a hackers infiltrarse en Binance y robar millones en criptomonedas
articles.text:
Una supuesta oferta laboral terminó convirtiéndose en la puerta de entrada para un ataque informático contra Binance, una de las mayores plataformas de intercambio de criptomonedas del mundo. Los responsables utilizaron entrevistas de trabajo falsas, programas maliciosos y credenciales robadas para ingresar a los sistemas internos de la compañía y acceder a sus billeteras digitales.
El incidente ocurrió el 29 de octubre de 2026 y afectó aproximadamente 6.340 millones de dólares en activos digitales, según un informe publicado por Binance el 3 de noviembre. En el documento, la empresa explicó cómo se desarrolló el ataque, qué mecanismos utilizaron los responsables y cuáles fueron las medidas adoptadas para contenerlo.
Binance también aseguró que asumirá el impacto financiero de los fondos robados, por lo que sus usuarios no tendrán que cubrir las pérdidas. La compañía indicó que había reservado más del 100 % de los recursos necesarios para afrontar el incidente y que, al 31 de octubre, ya había repuesto el 98 % de los activos en tokens afectados.
Cómo una falsa entrevista de trabajo terminó en un ataque informático
De acuerdo con la investigación inicial de Binance, el ataque no comenzó con una vulnerabilidad directa en las billeteras de criptomonedas, sino con una operación de ingeniería social. Este término describe las técnicas que utilizan los delincuentes para engañar a una persona y conseguir que entregue información, descargue archivos peligrosos o permita el acceso a sus dispositivos.
La compañía identificó dos momentos importantes en la preparación del ataque. En junio de 2026, un ingeniero del equipo de infraestructura de billeteras descargó una instalación manipulada de Homebrew, una herramienta utilizada para instalar programas en computadoras. El empleado buscaba una herramienta de programación con inteligencia artificial y encontró una versión modificada que permitió exponer información relacionada con sus permisos laborales.
Meses después, en septiembre, otro trabajador recibió una propuesta de empleo a través de una plataforma legítima de búsqueda laboral. El supuesto reclutador organizó entrevistas por videollamada y utilizó perfiles con fotografías y videos personales para generar confianza.
Durante una segunda entrevista, realizada mediante una aplicación de mensajería, le solicitaron descargar una supuesta tarea de programación. El archivo contenía código malicioso que se ejecutó en su computadora de trabajo.
En términos sencillos, los atacantes consiguieron que el empleado instalara un programa que les permitió ingresar a su equipo sin autorización. Desde allí pudieron avanzar hacia otros dispositivos y obtener credenciales utilizadas para acceder a sistemas internos.
Cómo consiguieron robar los activos digitales
El 20 de octubre, los atacantes aprovecharon una computadora comprometida para utilizar una herramienta interna de inteligencia artificial de Binance. De acuerdo con el informe, esto les permitió avanzar sobre otros equipos y localizar permisos que facilitaban el despliegue de programas dentro de la infraestructura de la compañía.
El 29 de octubre utilizaron esas credenciales para acceder a un servicio interno encargado de autorizar las operaciones de las billeteras digitales.
Las billeteras calientes, que son aquellas conectadas a internet para facilitar transferencias rápidas, comenzaron a enviar criptomonedas hacia direcciones controladas por los delincuentes. Entre los activos afectados había Bitcoin, XRP, Solana, Optimism y Ethereum.
Binance explicó que los atacantes aprovecharon un mecanismo de autorización de Ethereum llamado EIP-7702 para otorgar permisos a un contrato inteligente bajo su control. Esto les permitió mover fondos sin seguir el procedimiento habitual de retiros.
Qué hizo Binance después del incidente
La compañía suspendió los retiros para limitar las transferencias no autorizadas y coordinó acciones con socios de la industria para congelar los activos afectados. Según su informe, consiguió congelar o interceptar aproximadamente 2.850 millones de dólares.
También reconstruyó los sistemas de billeteras comprometidos, reemplazó los dispositivos afectados, desactivó las credenciales relacionadas con los empleados involucrados y reforzó los controles de seguridad.
Las próximas medidas para evitar nuevos ataques
Binance anunció que contratará expertos independientes en ciberseguridad para revisar lo ocurrido, validar sus hallazgos y recomendar nuevas medidas de protección.
Además, aumentará sus inversiones en detección de amenazas mediante inteligencia artificial, protección de dispositivos y vigilancia de actividades sospechosas. También trabaja en la creación de un fondo de investigación de seguridad junto con empresas de inteligencia artificial y participantes de la industria.
El informe atribuye el incidente a Corea del Norte, de acuerdo con información publicada por el FBI. Sin embargo, Binance aclaró que la investigación continúa y que sus conclusiones iniciales todavía deberán someterse a una revisión independiente.

Nouveautés Netflix : les films et séries à ne pas rater en novembre 2026
Black Doves, Un bon avocat, Quasimodo, The Altruists... De nombreux films, séries et documentaires rejoignent le catalogue du géant du streaming en novembre 2026. Voici la liste des nouveautés.
Alors que le soleil se fait plus rare, et que le froid nous invite chaque jour un peu plus à rester chez soi, la plateforme de streaming Netflix a pensé à nous avec un bel arrivage de nouveaux films, séries et documentaires au mois de novembre 2026.
Une livraison de qualité avec les films inédits Un bon avocat et Quasimodo, l'âme de Paris, les classiques Elfe, Inception et Tous en scène, ou encore les séries Black Doves, The Altruists et Entretien avec un vampire. Parfait pour se préparer à Noël.
Mais avant de vous présenter la liste des nouveautés de Netflix en novembre 2026, Les Numériques a pointé pour vous les deux événements du mois sur le service de streaming.
La série du mois sur Netflix
The Altruists
La romance tumultueuse entre le cofondateur de la cryptomonnaie FTX, Sam Bankman-Fried, et sa compagne Caroline Ellison, ainsi que leurs tentatives ambitieuses de révolutionner le système financier, qui ont abouti à une fraude de 36 milliards de dollars.
Mix improbable entre romance et histoire vraie d'une gigantesque fraude, la mini-série The Altruists est basée sur l'enquête de Kevin T. Dugan pour le magazine New York, et cocréée par l'oscarisé Graham Moore (Imitation Game) et Jacqueline Hoyt (The Leftovers). Une plongée captivante au cœur de la jeune génération folle des cryptos, portée par un casting talentueux : Julia Garner (Évanouis), Anthony Boyle (House of Guinness), Alex Lawther (Andor)...
À partir du 19 novembre sur Netflix.

Le film du mois sur Netflix
Un bon avocat
Léonard Landry, un avocat pénaliste flamboyant, fait une overdose en pleine plaidoirie. Après sa cure de désintoxication, il ne dispose que d'une semaine pour sauver sa carrière et préparer son propre procès, assisté à contrecœur par un stagiaire tenace nommé Noé. Commence alors une folle course contre la montre, ponctuée de manœuvres juridiques, de tentations et de rebondissements.
Trois ans après la série Tapie, Laurent Lafitte retrouve le réalisateur Tristan Séguéla pour une nouvelle fois raconter le parcours d'un homme de pouvoir pris dans une spirale infernale. Un long-métrage prenant, rythmé et exaltant qui, s'il respecte trop le cahier des charges Netflix pour révolutionner quoi que ce soit, s'impose par une écriture surprenante, sa belle efficacité, un ensemble d'acteurs impeccables - Mélanie Laurent, Anthony Bajon, Carole Bouquet - et un par Laffite habité au cœur de tout cela. Bref, on recommande.

articles.title: Un grupo de residentes de Pleasanton busca restricciones más fuertes en la privacidad de datos para una flota de robots
articles.text:
Los vecinos de Pleasanton, California, llevan varias semanas compartiendo sus calles con unos pequeños robots. Todo forma parte de un proyecto municipal destinado a detectar problemas de accesibilidad, pero el problema es que no todos los residentes están convencidos de que su actividad se limite a examinar el pavimento.
Algunos han comenzado a cuestionar qué información recopilan estas máquinas y qué ocurre con esos datos una vez que terminan su recorrido. Según explica Pleasanton Weekly, la preocupación surgió después de que Brent Werder (ingeniero especializado en robótica) observara cómo uno de estos dispositivos permanecía durante unas 7 horas frente a su vivienda.
Así, el vecino aseguró que vio robots girando sus cámaras hacia peatones, vehículos e incluso ventanas, y justo por eso revisó el contrato municipal. Tras comprobar que no establecía suficientes restricciones sobre el tratamiento de los datos, decidió impulsar una petición ciudadana para exigir mayores garantías.
La empresa asegura que sus robots no recopilan información personal
Los dispositivos desarrollados por Daxbot trabajan en colaboración con Bureau Veritas dentro de un programa que contempla examinar 580 kilómetros de aceras y caminos. Así, la intención del Ayuntamiento es identificar obstáculos y otros problemas que dificulten los desplazamientos de personas con movilidad reducida.
Sin embargo, Werder considera que el contrato debería especificar qué información se almacena, el tiempo y quién tendrá acceso a ella, así como exigir la eliminación de los datos que no resulten necesarios. Desde Daxbot rechazan que sus máquinas estén realizando labores de vigilancia encubierta, y Miriam Sullivan, responsable de comunicación de la compañía, asegura que los robots no identifican ni siguen a personas ni almacenan vídeos, salvo cuando se produce algún incidente de seguridad.
El Ayuntamiento de Pleasanton, por su parte, respalda esta explicación y sostiene que solo se recoge información relacionada con las infraestructuras peatonales. Pese a ello, los vecinos que impulsan la petición quieren que esas garantías queden reflejadas expresamente en las condiciones del proyecto.

articles.title: La NASA presenta X-70 Fractal, un nuevo avión experimental que probará maniobras "nunca antes demostradas" con piloto a bordo
articles.text:
La NASA acaba de desvelar un nuevo avión experimental con piloto a bordo y la verdad es que deja con la boca abierta por lo que puede hacer: no es un avión de pasajeros ni tampoco un caza, sino una plataforma de investigación en vuelo que permitirá estudiar cómo responde una aeronave en situaciones de maniobra que, según la Administración Nacional de Aeronáutica y del Espacio, nunca antes se han demostrado en un vuelo tripulado.
Un laboratorio con alas. El X-70 Fractal será el último de una saga, los aviones X, que la NASA emplea para probar tecnologías antes de que lleguen a la aviación real desde que el Bell X-1 rompió la barrera del sonido allá por 1947, pasando por el X-15 hipersónico o el actual X-59 de vuelo supersónico silencioso. Su característica diferencial será que dispondrá de un sistema de control de vuelo que se puede reconfigurar rápidamente, lo que posibilitará esa experimentación de todo tipo de situaciones.
Como explicaba Jared Isaacman en su presentación en la cumbre UP Summit del Centro Espacial Kennedy, permite probar "tecnologías avanzadas de control de vuelo, maniobrabilidad y otras tecnologías de vanguardia en vuelo real". ¿Cómo? Gracias un diseño modular y la capacidad de intercambiar de forma ágil cargas útiles internas y externas.
Por qué importa. Porque es un avión con piloto y mandos reconfigurables, lo que permite evaluar cómo se comporta una aeronave con distintas características de manejo, algo muy valioso para el diseño de futuros aviones y sistemas de control. Además, la modularidad permite usar la misma plataforma para varios programas. Resumiendo: en lugar de operar aviones distintos para cada línea de investigación, se usa uno solo cambiándole cargas y configuraciones.
Las especificaciones del X-70 Fractal. El X-70 Fractal tiene un peso al despegue de unos 4.536 kilogramos y está diseñado para volar a Mach 0,75 (entre unos 800 y 920 km/h según la altitud), alcanzando altitudes de hasta 13.716 metros y un alcance operativo de más de 2.700 kilómetros (1.500 millas náuticas, unos 2.778 km). Asimismo, permite jugar con unos 900 kg de carga experimental, ya sea interna o externa. Además, no es un avión autónomo, sino que requiere de piloto.
Su diseño es un misterio. La mala noticia es que la única imagen que la NASA ha facilitado de la aeronave es la que ilustra este artículo y está generada por ordenador, por lo que no hay fotografías reales del avión. El medio de cobertura espacial Space.com explica que su peso es similar al del Model 437 Vanguard de Scaled Composites y Northrop Grumman y que, además, la silueta se le parece. A falta de datos oficiales, todo apunta a que será un avión de tamaño compacto y alto rendimiento subsónico, diseñado para estudiar el control y la maniobrabilidad más que para la velocidad pura.
No es la única incógnita. Aunque no hay un calendario detallado de pruebas, en teoría no habrá que esperar mucho para verlo en acción: Isaacman contaba que está previsto que su primer vuelo a las órdenes de la NASA tenga lugar en los próximos dos años. Eso sí, eso es más un objetivo que una garantía, sirva como ejemplo el X-59: adjudicado a Lockheed Martin en 2016 y con previsión de estar listo para 2020, su primer vuelo se materializó en 2025, como recuerda PopSci.
De momento, solo queda esperar a que la NASA vaya despejando incógnitas como quién fabricará el avión y su presupuesto, así como su calendario de ensayos y, más pronto que tarde, la publicación de imágenes reales de la aeronave.

articles.title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
articles.text:
The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle.
Grab observes that "AI is speeding up how fast code is written; the layered defense is what makes that speed safe":
At [Grab's] scale, crashes leaking into production are an ongoing risk. A high volume of merge requests lands every week across many product teams, many shipping features behind flags that are switched on independently of releases. Any one of those changes can introduce a crash.
Beyond degrading the user's experience, a mobile app's crash reduces crash-free session rates and, as a consequence, the app's Google Play ranking. It also has an increased cost because not all users enable automatic updates, meaning that "a mobile crash that ships stays on users' devices" for longer. Furthermore, not all crashes come with clean, symbolicated stack trace, which means that "finding the cause means cross-referencing release timelines, flag rollouts, and session metadata".
Grab's layered defense follows a shift-left strategy aimed at catching crashes as early as possible through a series of safeguards along the development cycle phases: pre-merge through pre-production, release control, and post-release response.
During the pre-merge to pre-production phase, the goal is prevention, which Grab describes as its "primary line of defense". To achieve this, Grab engineers use static code analyzers such as Android Lint and SwiftLint to catch issues before code even merges via platform-specific, community-based, and custom lint rules; automated and manual testing, including unit tests, UI tests, and quality assurance (QA) checks; and Grab Early Access (GEA), a pre-production gate where early builds are distributed to internal users and actively monitored for crashes:
A crash that only a handful of internal users see in GEA would, at production scale, translate into a substantial spike in the crash rate, extra support load, and potentially a hotfix. Catching these crashes before they ever reach production users makes GEA one of our most important stability gates.
During the release phase, Grab uses staged rollout and feature flags to control production exposure to crashes. Staged rollout enables a new app version to reach only a small percentage of users initially, so engineers can monitor its crashes and possibly pause the rollout if an abnormal crash rate is detected. Features flags, in turn, allow teams to activate features gradually while monitoring their impact on crash rates. If a feature causes crash rates to exceed predefined thresholds, it be disabled immediately without requiring a new release.
During the post-release phase, Grab focuses on rapid incident response using mechanisms to detect, investigate, and contain production crashes. These include real-time crash monitoring using Firebase Crashlytics and BigQuery to identify anomalies as soon as a build goes live; automated triage and enriched diagnostics to aggregate crash metadata and stack traces, helping teams to map crashes to specific PRs; and feedback loops and post-mortem analysis to extend lint rules and test coverage.
There is much more to Grab's layered defense approach than can be covered here. Be sure to read the full article for all the details.

articles.title: Typographic Intelligence: Warum Designsysteme im KI-Zeitalter nicht mehr ausreichen
articles.text:
Typographic Intelligence: Warum Designsysteme nicht mehr ausreichen
Designsysteme haben in den vergangenen Jahren grundlegend verändert, wie Unternehmen gestalten. Standardisierte Komponenten, Muster und Assets helfen Teams, schneller zu arbeiten, Inhalte effizient zu skalieren und Marken über unterschiedliche Kanäle hinweg konsistent zu führen. Sie schaffen einen verlässlichen Rahmen, innerhalb dessen Kreativteams schnell produzieren können.
Generative KI treibt diese Entwicklung erheblich voran. Erste Entwürfe und Mock-ups entstehen innerhalb weniger Minuten. Über die entsprechende technische Infrastruktur lassen sie sich fast unmittelbar teilen, prüfen und weiterentwickeln. Doch diese Geschwindigkeit legt eine neue Schwachstelle offen. Während sich die Produktion nahezu beliebig beschleunigen lässt, können Menschen nicht im gleichen Tempo prüfen, bewerten und einordnen, in dem KI neue Varianten produziert. Der neue Engpass ist deshalb nicht die Erstellung von Content, sondern die fundierte Entscheidung darüber, was davon wirklich gut, richtig und markengerecht ist.
Was wir brauchen, sind Entscheidungssysteme
Hier setzt das Konzept der „Typographic Intelligence“ an. Es beschreibt das Zusammenspiel von Kreativität, Technologie, Governance und menschlicher Urteilskraft. Ein wichtiger Bestandteil sind klare Strukturen dafür, wie Entscheidungen getroffen werden, wer die notwendige Expertise einbringt und an welchen Stellen menschliches Urteilsvermögen gefragt ist.
Ein Beispiel aus der Praxis: Ein Creative Director, Brand Manager oder Marketingverantwortlicher kann nur eine begrenzte Zahl von Entwürfen pro Tag fundiert beurteilen. Mehr Output darf deshalb nicht einfach zu mehr Freigabeschleifen führen. Entscheidend ist vielmehr, Expertenwissen dort in den Prozess zu integrieren, wo es tatsächlich gebraucht wird. Das kann bedeuten, Feedback- und Freigabeprozesse neu aufzusetzen, feste Expertenteams einzubinden oder gezielt externe Spezialisten hinzuzuziehen. Expertise muss Teil des Systems sein.
Mehr als nur Gestaltungsregeln
Gerade bei Typografie zeigt sich, wie wichtig solche Strukturen sind. Unternehmen müssen heute weit mehr entscheiden als die Frage, welche Schrift zu ihrer Marke passt. Es geht um Lizenzierung, Barrierefreiheit und Lokalisierung, um den Einsatz über unterschiedliche Märkte, Sprachen und digitale Anwendungen hinweg. Mit der wachsenden Zahl an Touchpoints steigt auch die Zahl der Entscheidungen.
Typografisches Wissen muss deshalb in die Arbeitsweise des Unternehmens integriert und langfristig verfügbar gemacht werden. Bestehendes Wissen wird gebündelt, Teams erhalten Orientierung bei Fragen zu Schriftwahl, Lizenzierung, Barrierefreiheit und Lokalisierung. Gleichzeitig entstehen wiederholbare Prozesse, die sich über Marken, Teams und Märkte hinweg skalieren lassen.
Das Ziel ist nicht einfach bessere Typografie. Es sind bessere Entscheidungen
KI kann Varianten erzeugen, Prozesse erleichtern und Systeme skalieren. Ob eine Gestaltung zur Marke passt, kulturell funktioniert, zugänglich ist und langfristig Bestand hat, bleibt eine Frage menschlicher Urteilskraft. Typographic Intelligence bedeutet deshalb auch, technologische Möglichkeiten nicht mit guten Entscheidungen zu verwechseln. Vielleicht haben wir die Produktion fürs Erste genug optimiert. Jetzt ist es an der Zeit, die Qualität unserer Entscheidungen mit der gleichen Konsequenz weiterzuentwickeln.
Jetzt zum Webinar registrieren
Über den Autor: Christopher Kollat ist Chief Experience Officer (CXO) bei Monotype, wo er den Bereich Client Strategy & Growth leitet. Sein Ziel ist es, die Zusammenarbeit mit den Kunden zu intensivieren, das Kundenerlebnis zu optimieren, die Kundenbeziehungen zu stärken und ein nachhaltiges Geschäftswachstum zu fördern. Der 50-Jährige gehört seit über zehn Jahren dem Kernführungsteam an und ist am Berliner Standort von Monotype tätig.

articles.title: How much is too much to spend on a graphics card?
articles.text:
There was a time when spending $500 on a graphics card felt extravagant. That kind of money bought you a serious high-end GPU, and $300 could get you something pretty capable. Fast-forward to today, and those numbers almost seem quaint.
Our latest GPU pricing update paints a rather depressing picture. Graphics card prices have climbed 35% in just the last three months, with mainstream models selling well above their original MSRPs. An RTX 5070 that was supposed to cost $549 now sells for around $900 in the US, while the high-end market has become increasingly detached from what most gamers would consider reasonable.
Of course, everyone's budget and priorities are different. Some enthusiasts are perfectly comfortable dropping $1,000 or more on a GPU they'll use for several years. Others have drawn a hard line at $300 or $500, regardless of how much faster the latest hardware gets.
And there's another question worth asking: how about value? have we simply become accustomed to paying more? What felt outrageous a decade ago might now seem like the price of admission for serious PC gaming.
So here's this weekend's question: What's the most you've ever spent on a graphics card, and what's your absolute spending limit today? Have rising prices pushed you to skip upgrades, buy used, or settle for a lower tier? Or are you willing to pay a premium if the performance justifies it?

Voltou a cair: Motorola Signature recebe R$ 1,5 mil de desconto no Magalu
Motorola Signature (256 GB) com tela de 165 Hz mais fluida que a do novo Signature 27 e câmeras de 50 MP recebe desconto de 25% no Pix durante a Black November 2026
O Motorola Signature de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 4.498 no Pix no Magazine Luiza. O celular ultra premium, com tela AMOLED de 165 Hz e todas as câmeras de 50 MP, recebe desconto de 25% sobre o preço original de R$ 5.999 durante a Black November 2026 e junto à chegada do novo Signature 27.
Um dos melhores celulares da Motorola, o Signature possui uma tela LTPO AMOLED de 6,8″ com brilho de até 6.200 nits e taxa de 165 Hz, marca superior à do novo Signature 27 de 120 Hz, mas com brilho de 12 mil nits.
Seu chip Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 de 3 nanômetros e os 12 GB de RAM física suportam diversas tarefas, conforme apurado nos nossos testes. Os 256 GB de espaço interno são adequados para guardar fotos e vídeos.
O corpo com revestimento de couro sintético na traseira e bordas de alumínio recebe o vidro Gorilla Glass Victus 2 sobre a tela e as certificações militar MIL-STD-810H e IP68/IP69, que adicionam extrema resistência ao smartphone em diversas situações.
Todas as câmeras do Signature são de 50 MP. O kit traseiro, que filma em 8K, inclui wide com sensor Sony Lytia 828 e ultrawide com ângulo de 122º, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e telefoto periscópica Sony Lytia 600 com zoom óptico de 3x para aproximações. A frontal faz selfies excelentes e filma em 4K a 60 fps.
Sua bateria de 5.200 mAh resiste a pouco mais de 17 horas de reprodução de vídeo, conforme nossos testes. Da mesma forma, o suporte ao carregamento ultrarrápido de 90 W via USB-C e de 50 W sem fio garante uma carga de 0% a 45% em 30 minutos, e uma completa dentro de uma hora.
O Motorola Signature de 256 GB (R$ 4.498 no Pix) será atualizado até o Android 23 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC.
A Black November, a ação em que o varejo oferece promoções em eletrônicos com diversos cupons e condições exclusivas durante o mês da Black Friday 2026 já começou, em antecipação à data principal no dia 27 de novembro.

articles.title: Re-releases of Wing Commander, Ultima titles hit Steam and GOG
articles.text:
Many people are not big fans of game publisher EA right now for good reason, but for those who remember a better time in the 1990s, there’s a little good news. Twenty-five classic games from that EA era have been lightly remastered and updated, then placed for sale on Steam and GOG, including several Wing Commander games and nearly the entire Ultima series.
Below is the full list of remastered or re-released games:
- Road Rash: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander: 35th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander II: Vengeance of the Kilrathi: 35th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander III: Heart of the Tiger: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander IV: The Price of Freedom: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander Prophecy: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Privateer 2: The Darkening: 30th Anniversary Edition
- Wing Commander: Privateer
- Wing Commander: Academy
- Wing Commander: Armada
- Strike Commander
- Theme Hospital
- Crusader: No Remorse
- Crusader: No Regret
- Ultima I: The First Age of Darkness
- Ultima II: The Revenge of the Enchantress
- Ultima III: Exodus
- Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
- Ultima V: Warriors of Destiny
- Ultima VI: The False Prophet
- Ultima VII: The Complete Edition
- Ultima VIII: Gold Edition
- Ultima IX: Ascension
- Ultima Underworld I
- Ultima Underworld II
The story behind seven remasters
In a lengthy blog post published this week, Jim Vessella, a senior producer at EA, described the efforts that went into remastering Wing Commander I-IV and Prophecy, Privateer 2, and Road Rash.
It’s a long, detailed story that’s worth reading yourself, but here’s a top-level summary. After working on the mostly widely acclaimed Command & Conquer: Remastered Collection in 2019, Vessella writes that he learned about and visited a room at EA’s Redwood Shores campus that contained a large archive of poorly labeled or sorted physical media from ages past.
In his free time, and with the help of others, he began cataloging this archive and discovered, among other things, that it contained virtually the entirety of the original masters of Wing Commander III and Wing Commander IV‘s full-motion-video cutscenes.
The story that ensues involves building a small team of contractors, poring through the footage 17 hours a day on swing shifts to label and digitize it, and then coordinating with several key community members—particularly Matt Wells, who has made community enhancement patches for some of the Wing Commander games—to put together remasters of those games.

articles.title: Team Group Secures Two Taiwan Patents: Magnetic Attachment and Device Tracking for Portable SSDs
articles.text:
Friday, November 6th 2026
Team Group Secures Two Taiwan Patents: Magnetic Attachment and Device Tracking for Portable SSDs
Team Group Inc., a leading global memory brand, has obtained two new invention patents in Taiwan for its Team Group PD20M Mag Portable SSD and T-CREATE EXPERT P34F Find My External SSD, following patents previously granted in multiple countries. Covering magnetic attachment and device-tracking technologies, respectively, these patents underscore Team Group's R&D expertise while enhancing the convenience of portable storage and expanding its range of applications.
Team Group PD20M Mag Portable SSD—Innovative Magnetic Design for Greater Portability
The Team Group PD20M Mag Portable SSD has been granted a Taiwan invention patent for its proprietary magnetic attachment technology, following a U.S. invention patent and a Japanese utility model patent. As Team Group's first MagSafe-compatible external SSD, the PD20M features an ultraslim 8.2 mm profile and weighs just 40 g. It attaches securely to compatible devices, offering a compact and convenient storage solution for users on the go. When paired with the iPhone 15 Pro series or later compatible models, the PD20M also supports recording high-quality Apple ProRes video directly to the drive, allowing users to expand storage capacity and capture memorable moments with ease.T-CREATE EXPERT P34F Find My External SSD—Built-In Tracking Enhances the Portable Storage Experience
The T-CREATE EXPERT P34F Find My External SSD is Team Group's first external SSD with built-in location tracking. Team Group has now secured an invention patent in Taiwan for this technology, following earlier utility model patents in Taiwan and China. The P34F can be paired directly with compatible Apple devices, allowing users to locate the SSD through Apple's Find My app. Its built-in speaker can also play an alert sound to help users locate the drive when it is nearby, making device retrieval more efficient. Combining a compact, stylish design with a convenient lanyard hole, the P34F offers greater portability and gives creators peace of mind as they move between locations and back up their files.
Drawing on its strong technical foundation, Team Group continues to incorporate its patented technologies into mass-produced products that address real-world needs and enhance the portable storage experience. Looking ahead, the company will continue investing in R&D and expanding its patent portfolio to strengthen its market competitiveness and drive long-term growth in storage technology.

articles.title: Meet the audio glasses using cutting edge tech to provide a natural listening experience
articles.text:
Technology is improving and advancing so fast that it seems like the future we dreamed of is already here.
Take Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses, for example. These aren’t just any glasses, they are actually used to improve and support hearing.
Using groundbreaking technology, Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses have paved the way for wearables that are improving lives and healthcare. Want to know how it works? Here’s the 411 on Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses.
Advanced sound technology for all-day hearing support
Nuance AudioTM Plus Glasses’ integrated advanced sound technology is supported by open-ear speakers that sit just above the ear. They are integrated into the temple arms via extension hinges, which are adjustable within a set range. Once powered, the technology is always on and also uses directional microphones for a natural listening experience.
The device is also compatible with near-prescription lenses, and custom lens options are available to suit the wearer’s vision and listening environment. This eliminates the need for multiple devices and allows the ears to breathe while reducing listening fatigue.
Designed for mild to moderate hearing loss, Nuance supports listening in everyday situations, especially when background noises make conversations harder.
Key features
Breaking the stigma around assistive listening, Nuance AudioTM Plus offers discreet, stylish glasses that seamlessly combine vision and listening support in one frame, building on the distinctive open-ear technology of Nuance AudioTM Glasses with enhanced amplification, improved speech clarity in noisy environments, better own-voice perception, and an extended battery life of approximately 10 hours under average product conditions.*
Directional amplification helps enhance speech clarity through directional microphones and beamforming technology, allowing users to focus on conversations in front of them.
Easy to use and simple to set up and manage through the intuitive Nuance AudioTM App, Nuance AudioTM Plus also features new on-frame controls, including a dedicated power switch and volume buttons conveniently positioned on the temples.
Open-ear comfort comes from lightweight, open-ear speakers integrated into the temples that leave the ears free for long-lasting comfort, while an expanded range of sizes, universal fitting and adjustable nose pads on selected styles help provide a secure and comfortable fit.
It’s an all-in-one solution designed to address both vision and listening assistance needs in one elegant device. Meanwhile, hands-free phone calls allow users to answer and manage voice calls directly from the frames when paired with a compatible iPhone.**
Styles and accessories
Nuance AudioTM Plus is available in three timeless frame styles Square 53, Panthos 48 and Upturn 52 and five colours, Shiny Black, Shiny Burgundy, Deep Blue, Amber, and Olive Green.
The standard package includes a charging pad and USB-C cable to charge Nuance AudioTM Plus.
For those who prefer not to use a device, there is also a remote option, which improves accessibility. When it comes to the lens options, users can decide from transition lenses that adjust to UV and a blue light filter option.
User experience
The glasses are easily manageable from the Nuance AudioTM App, and the glasses also feature on-frame controls for quick access to key functions, while a dedicated remote control is available separately.
With the app, users can control audio modes, where they can switch between two frontal, to focus on face-to-face conversations, and all-around, to amplify all surrounding sounds. Choose the pre-configured amplification settings (A, B, C or D) for a tailored hearing experience, and customize the background noise level with three levels of noise reduction. You can also adjust the volume of amplification on a scale from 1 to 5.
Lenses
Nuance AudioTM Plus can be fitted with any type of optical lens, according to the wearer’s vision needs. The glasses can also be paired with Transitions® lenses, which adapt to changing light conditions to support an integrated hearing and vision experience throughout the day.
In Canada, the recommended retail price will start from $1,149, depending on the lens configuration.
Ready for all-day support without sacrificing comfort or design? Learn more about the first-of-its-kind product, Nuance AudioTM Glasses, online.
*Based on average product condition
**The product, as an MFI certified device, supports voice calls only when used with an iPhone (requires iOS 16 or later)

articles.title: Elegoo M1 Ultra review: A good first entry into the scanner market
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Elegoo M1 Ultra has a lot going for it, but it is not a standalone system. You’ll need to combine it with a powerful laptop to process the scanning data into anything useful. The good news it can be tethered via Wi-Fi.
Reasons to buy
- + Easy to calibrate
- + Long battery life
- + Onboard screen
Reasons to avoid
- - Turntable not included
- - Most projects require multiple scans
- - Needs a high end laptop for best results
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
The M1 Ultra is Elegoo’s first entry into the 3D scanner market. It is a feature-rich scanner with five scanning modes, four blue light laser modes, and a NIR binocular structured light mode. Most importantly, the scanner has a 3-in color touch screen and long battery life. It even includes a spare rechargeable battery, so you’re always prepared.
The scanner can’t run without a fairly high end PC or Mac for processing power. It will need to be tethered to the laptop with a UBS-C cable or connected via Wi-Fi. I was able to get about five feet away from my subject in a harsh RF environment. I didn’t test it further than that, so it may go farther. The cable connection provides the fastest connectivity, making tethered scanning worth the hassle.
The scanner’s output rivals any of the scanners I’ve tested, but it did require a little extra work to get there. At a current price of $1,599 at Elegoo, the M1 Ultra has features not found in other scanners at this price point.
Specifications: Elegoo M1 Ultra
| Scanning Mode | Blue Laser | NIR Infrared Binocular Structured Light | 
| Light Type | Single, 7, and 34-Line Laser | NIR (Near-Infrared) | 
| Accuracy | Up to 0.02 mm | Up to .05mm/m | 
| 3D Resolution | 0.05-2mm | 0.1-2mm | 
| Working Distance | 200mm-600mm | Between 170 and 1200 mm | 
| Min Scan Volume | 5 x 5 x 5 mm | 170mm-1200mm | 
| Scan Speed (Standalone) | ≤ 100fps | ≤ 30fps | 
| Alignment | 170mm-1200mm | Geometry/Texture | 
| Connectivity | Wired USB, Optional Wi-Fi | Row 8 - Cell 2 | 
| Color Texture | Supported | Row 9 - Cell 2 | 
| Output Format | OBJ/STL/PLY/ASC | Row 10 - Cell 2 | 
| Operating System | Windows or Mac | Row 11 - Cell 2 | 
| Release Date | October 29, 2026 | Row 12 - Cell 2 | 
| Pricing | $1,699 | Row 13 - Cell 2 | 
Included in the Box: Elegoo M1 Ultra
The Elegoo M1 Ultra comes with a nice hard case for travel, with a padded interior to protect the scanner, glass calibration board, spare battery, NIR filters, and a USB-C cable. Also included are a lens cleaning cloth and a packet of marker dots. Noticeably absent is a turntable for scanning smaller objects. (We borrowed a turntable from another scanner during this test.)
Design of the Elegoo M1 Ultra
The Elegoo M1 Ultra weighs 511g (1.12lbs) with its battery installed. It has a rubber grip below the screen and is nicely balanced. Users with large hands may find their thumbs blocking the screen.
The onboard screen can be used to set the scanning parameters, start and stop scans, and monitor the scans as they progress. The 3-inch screen is small, but the UI is laid out perfectly. When setting parameters for a scan, the touch screen takes precedence over the tethered computer if you’re starting the scan from the scanner itself.
The business end of the scanner has a series of blue, white, and infrared LEDs, blue lasers, and cameras. The included NIR filters are needed when scanning outdoors or in harsh light conditions. The battery and the spare can be charged using a USB-C cable when unmounted, and can be charged from the computer when operating the scanner in USB mode. The battery life is excellent. Almost all of our testing was done with one charge of the battery and its spare.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Getting Started and Calibrating the Elegoo M1 Ultra
Calibrating the Elegoo M1 Ultra is fairly easy given its light weight and the easy-to-follow software. Using the glass calibration board, the scanner is aimed at various angles and heights, following the directions on screen. The software shows an image of where the scanner should be and an image of the scanner as you move it. You have to match the two before moving on to the next spot. Scanner calibration can be a chore, but calibrating the M1 Ultra was simple.
Installing the Software for Elegoo M1 Ultra
Elegoo Scan can be downloaded from Elegoo’s website for Windows and Mac. The software works and looks like CrealityScan, which is a good thing since both make cleaning up individual scans and stitching multiple scans together fairly easy. The software does require a bunch of memory, with the more, the merrier. I tried running the software on an older PC laptop which met the minimum requirements, except it had only 8 GB of RAM, and it was not enough.
Elegoo recommends a PC with Windows 10/11 (64-bit), an Intel Core i7 (13th Gen) or higher, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 or higher (8 GB VRAM), and 32 GB or more of RAM. For Mac, they recommend macOS 14 or later, with an Apple M4 or later, and 32 GB or more of RAM. Minimum specs for both are 16gb of RAM, with Windows 10/11 (64-bit), Intel Core i7 (7th Gen), and an Nvidia GPU (6 GB VRAM) for PC, and macOS 14 or later, with an Apple M2 CPU.
Blue Laser Line 3D Scanning with the Elegoo M1 Ultra
The Elegoo M1 Ultra has 4 blue laser scanning modes: 34 crossed laser lines for quick scanning, 7 parallel lines for finer details, 1 line for scanning deeper, more difficult-to-capture holes, and markerless. The fewer the lines, the more time the scans take. I should point out that the turntable in the photo was borrowed from the Creality Pika Scanner, which we reviewed previously.
One of my favorite use cases is scanning an item for import into a 3D printing project I am working on. I scanned a cheap 895 brushed motor commonly found in drills. The motor required several scans, and the M1 Ultra seemed to have trouble capturing the shinier parts of the object. Ultimately, I captured two scans that had enough data to be useful. The software has an automatic alignment tool which does a good job in most cases. In this case, it was baffled by the geometry. The manual alignment worked perfectly.
Manual alignment requires adding markers matching points on both images. You do not have to be super exact with the placement. The software will smooth out any overlaps.
Part of the mesh processing is hole filling. This also has an automatic and manual mode. Since the automatic mode was going to fill in the screw holes and cooling holes, I had to fill in the holes manually by clicking on them. This is a little tedious, but it worked well.
After hole filling, smoothing, and simplifying, I was able to export the file as an STL and open it in Tinkercad.
The size, and hole alignment were perfect for integrating the motor into a project.
This bust of Michelangelo’s David came with an early Creality scanner and has become my main test file. It took three scans for me to get a good model, which was a recurring theme with the Elegoo M1 Ultra.
Fortunately in this case, the auto alignment function worked perfectly.
Even with multiple scans, there were still a few holes to fill. One of these can be seen in the finished model in the smooth, flat area above David’s left ear.
Overall, the model generated is one of the best I’ve seen, and it printed extremely well once exported. The flaw at the bottom of the print was a bed adhesion issue rather than a problem with the model.
NIR 3D Scanning with the Elegoo M1 Ultra
Since I could not find a willing human victim…I mean, subject…to scan, I tried using the NIR mode to scan Clyde, our family’s favorite stuffed Clydesdale. This is a cautionary tale because 3D scanners in general have a tough time scanning black objects, as they absorb light rather than reflecting it.
The scans weren’t bad, but they did leave big holes where the mane and tail were too dark to read.
I was able to do a much better scan of Ali the Alligator. In NIR mode, the scanner is capable of 30fps. Even with the slower frame rate, the scanner was able to quickly capture Ali in two scans, without a ton of multiple passes. Each time you go over the same spot on an object, it’s possible to generate garbage data that has to be removed in the meshing process. The two scans align together automatically, and the finished model is pretty darn good.
The scanner does feature color texture mapping. Other than the mouth, where a large hole needed to be filled, the color mapping was spot on.
Bottom Line
The Elegoo M1 Ultra is a good scanner that has a good feature set for the price. The light weight, onboard screen, long battery life, and stable Wi-Fi connection make it a joy to use.
The ElegooScan software is fairly intuitive. It makes calibrating the scanner and turning the raw scans into usable models fairly easy. The Elegoo M1 Ultra did require multiple scans to get good coverage of objects, while other scanners I’ve tested could do it in one pass. The added complexity takes up a good deal of time and requires a fair amount of computer power, especially when cleaning up and aligning multiple scans. ElegooScan has the tools to make it work. Even with a pretty good model, you’ll likely also need a CAD program or other design tools to make the best use of the scans.
If you’d like to save a few bucks and get a still excellent scanner, check out the Creality Pika, which is currently $699. If you want a scanner with a little more horsepower, check out the Creality Sermoon S1, which retails for $2,069. Creality also makes the Sermoon P1, which can run completely untethered and retails for $3,299.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer reveals the secret tool he used for the game's soundtrack that he saves for 'special occasions' — 'It's definitely not considered any kind of tech, but it's definitely entertaining'
articles.text:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer reveals the secret tech behind his work — 'I have an aluminum garbage can lid that I save for special occasions'
Jason Graves also used his secret tool for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
- Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves shares his secret tool he used on the soundtrack
- He reveals that it's "an aluminum garbage can lid that I save for special occasions"
- Graves also used it for 2022's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves has revealed the unusual, secret tool he used for creating the game's soundtrack.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Graves discussed his creative process for writing the game's multiplayer music, which he said is usually "an afterthought," and even offered some insight into the coolest technology he used for recording the tracks.
"It's definitely not considered any kind of tech, but it's definitely entertaining," Graves replied when asked what his secret weapon was.
But if you expected something along the lines of interesting studio equipment or fancy tools to capture the multiplayer's tone, you'd be dead wrong.
"I have an aluminum garbage can lid that I save for special occasions," the composer revealed, "and the last time I used it was in 2022's Modern Warfare [2]. So naturally, I had to bring it out again and play it for Modern Warfare 4."
Graves also discussed how the multiplayer music is "completely different" from the campaign, which has more story beats and dramatic moments, saying "you play a lot of multiplayer" to truly understand its tone.
"It's a completely different vibe from the campaign, and the music needs to make you feel like anything could happen at any point in time," Graves said. "A lot of what I was trying to capture was forward momentum and pure adrenaline."

"There's definitely a lot of aggressive percussion, distorted electronics, and organic textures that help give the music its identity," Graves added. "I love combining real-world sounds with electronic processing, especially when you end up with something that's difficult to identify.
"It creates a sense of energy and unpredictability that fits perfectly with multiplayer."

articles.title: Mamaearth parent’s profit surges 87%; Goyal defends Temple amid backlash
articles.text:
Mamaearth parent’s profit surges 87%; Goyal defends Temple amid backlash
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, registered an 87% YoY rise in net profit for Q2FY27, while revenue rose 36%. In other news, Deepinder Goyal has posted a series of updates on X amid backlash from some Indian doctors who criticised his wearable device Temple.
Dear Readers,
AI is finding cyber flaws swiftly. But are enterprises quick enough to fix them?
Nikesh Arora, Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, raises this crucial point. He notes in a LinkedIn post that most organisations, especially the smaller ones, do not have the capacity to patch flaws at the speed needed. Arora advocates virtual patching as an interim measure and calls for a shared vulnerability clearing house and faster development of protective signatures.
As AI agents become capable of handling everyday tasks, here’s a smart ring that promises to bring AI agents to our fingertips.
At a private launch in Bengaluru, Aina unveiled an AI-powered ring that combines a colour display, voice commands, and gesture-based controls. The startup wants its device to become an everyday interface between users and AI agents. But can it offer enough utility to justify its Rs 47,000 price tag?
In other news, the government has cleared 12 proposals worth over Rs 7,500 crore under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme. This round of approvals adds to the momentum behind the scheme, which aims to build a domestic ecosystem for components and reduce India’s dependence on imports.
Meanwhile, MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based Quick Ride, a tech-led shared mobility platform. Quick Ride connects people travelling along similar routes, enabling affordable ride pooling for everyday commute.
Lastly, here’s a bit of weekend motivation.
Built despite opposition, legal challenges, and questions over cost, Bihar Museum has marched into the global top 10, ahead of the Met and Louvre. For YourStory’s founder Shradha Sharma, the museum not only brings the region’s history to life, but is also a reminder of what ambition and perseverance can accomplish.
In today’s newsletter:
- Mamaearth parent Honasa’s net profit rises 87%
- Goyal defends Temple amid backlash
Here’s your trivia for today: Which company introduced commercially the first widespread videocassette in 1971?
Note: Starting this week, YS Buzz will land in your inbox Monday through Saturday. On Sundays, you'll continue to receive our Weekly Wrap, bringing together the biggest startup and business stories of the week. Thank you for reading YourStory and being part of our community.
Earnings
Mamaearth parent Honasa’s Q2 net profit rises 87%
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of beauty & personal care brand Mamaearth, registered an 87% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit for the second quarter of the current fiscal, while revenue rose 36% driven by strong growth across categories.
According to Honasa Consumer, the second quarter revenue growth is the highest it has recorded since its public listing in November 2023.
Key takeaways
- The company’s net profit in Q2FY27 was Rs 73.24 crore, compared with Rs 39.22 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue was Rs 731.18 crore, compared with Rs 538.06 crore a year ago.
- However, sequentially, profit fell from Rs 90.44 crore in the first quarter. Revenue in the first quarter was Rs 755.94 crore.
- For the six months of the fiscal year, the company reported a revenue of Rs 1,487.13 crore, a YoY growth of 31%. The net profit for the period was Rs 163.69 crore, a YoY rise of 103%.
<Top Funding Deals of the Week>
Startup: GIVA
Amount: $100M
Round: Undisclosed
Startup: EloElo Group
Amount: $80M
Round: Series C
Startup: Clinics On Cloud
Amount: $12.5M
Round: Series A
Wearables
Goyal defends Temple amid backlash
Deepinder Goyal has posted a series of updates and clarifications on X amid backlash from some Indian doctors who criticised his brain-monitoring wearable Temple. Describing Temple as “an ambitious project”, Goyal gave a detailed explanation on what the team is building. “The team is delusional enough to think we can build this. And we will,” he wrote on Friday.
Earlier, on Thursday, he posted, “We stand by our science and our methods. Each of our claims is easily verifiable by individuals and institutions alike, and you will see a lot of independent studies come up on their own when the device becomes available to use.”
Key takeaways:
- “First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren’t true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple,” Goyal wrote on Thursday.
- He also highlighted that $30 million was invested in building the device, including $20 million of his personal money. Calling Temple his purpose, he said it’s not about the money. “I have enough of it to last for generations. My incentives are fully aligned with getting the science right. I am not staking a reputation earned over 20 years on making a quick buck.”
- However, some doctors were not convinced by Goyal’s response. On X, Dr Rishabh Jain responded saying Goyal had shared financial and personal sacrifices but no scientific evidence. “Stop calling legitimate scientific scrutiny 'rage'. You have responded to questions about medical accuracy with investment figures, return policies, personal reputation, and promises of future studies. None of these constitutes scientific validation.”
News & updates
- First close: Northern Arc Investment Managers, the asset management arm of Northern Arc Capital, has marked the first close of its Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund with commitments of more than Rs 400 crore from institutions, family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals, and high-net-worth individuals.
- Court verdict: A division bench of the Delhi High Court has dismissed an appeal by Unity Bank, upholding the interim protection granted to BharatPe's parent company RIPL (Resilient Innovations Private Limited) under the Shareholders’ Agreement and affirming the order of a single judge.
- Apple’s investments: Alphabet built a stake worth nearly $548 million in longtime partner Qualcomm in the third quarter, giving a boost to the chipmaker’s efforts to expand into data centres as the smartphone market sees one of the worst downturns, Reuters reported. The Google parent has also increased its position in Elon Musk’s SpaceX to about 555 million shares from 551.2 million earlier.
Which company introduced commercially the first widespread videocassette in 1971?
Answer: Sony
