articles.title: Think you can trust the photos on Rightmove? Estate agents are using AI to transform homes — and the results are getting ridiculous
articles.text:
I tried to work out which photos in this Rightmove property listing were AI-generated — and the more I looked, the worse it got
The house is real. The rest is anybody's guess
Following inaccurate and downright silly AI generated images appearing on JustEat and Etsy, it appears that no industry is immune from AI slop. The property market is now also flooded with digitally altered images.
As someone who has had their fair share of dealing with moving house and looking at properties, I understand how frustrating and stressful it can be. But some people who believe they have found their dream home have been sorely disappointed to find out the potential house has been ‘enhanced’ using AI.
Over the past year, many have taken to Reddit to complain about estate agents posting listings with AI modified photos that include fixings, furniture, and structural changes that the actual properties do not have.
Deck the halls with AI changes
AI is getting good at enhancing images, but it isn’t quite perfect. Checking for AI enhancement is painful enough, but if you know where to look you’ll start to spot odd details.
For example, one listing for a house on Rightmove shared by a Reddit user features a thriving shrubbery plot in the driveway, but if you look closely at multiple angles of the front of the property, some of the plants have mysteriously shifted or disappeared completely.
What’s worse is that you can see the rear garden from the front of the property, which shows a shed and a patchy lawn with a messy gravel path. But flick through a few more of the property photos and all of a sudden the rear lawn is thriving and has a nice neat path, the fence has been mended, and the entire garden has been significantly expanded.
I’ll take you on a tour of some of the most impressive features. Head through the front door and you will be greeted by a picture frame above a side-cabinet that can change paintings depending on where you stand in the hallway.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The bathroom features towels that change color depending how you're feeling, and the towel rail cannot decide if it has five rails or six.
But the pièce de résistance is the garden, where the decking has either three or four steps down to the lawn depending on your budget. You can also opt to have the decking’s corner steps and additional gravel path put back in for a modest sum.
In my search to spot exactly what was AI generated, I also came across an original photo of the house. But while searching for further inconsistencies between this original and the edited photos, I noticed something odd.
In the ‘original’ image, the single road to the right of the house connecting the cul-de-sac to the local town — that has existed since at least 1975 according to ordinance survey maps — has disappeared, and is now a dead end. The ‘For Sale’ sign featured in both images is now written in an incomprehensible language.
So which image is genuine and which is enhanced? It appears that both have been digitally altered and I am starting to go insane.
Should AI photos be used on property listings?
In most cases, estate agents will disclose if the images of a property have been digitally altered or edited in any way. But for this particular case, you have to scroll through a 1,700 word property description that also shows signs of AI involvement before you reach the following text:
“Some photographs used within this property advertisement have been digitally enhanced and/or virtually staged for illustrative purposes. Virtual furnishings, accessories and decorative items may have been added to demonstrate the potential appearance and use of the rooms.”
This disclaimer continues; “No alterations to the physical structure, layout or dimensions of the property are intended to be represented by the digital staging. Prospective purchasers are advised to rely upon their own inspection of the property.”
Obviously this is just one example, but a quick look through Reddit threads such as r/SpottedonRightMove and you will find numerous examples of AI enhanced properties, each more extreme than the last.
Some users argue in favor of allowing estate agents to use AI photos to show the potential of a property, or to provide inspiration on a property that may need some fixing up. Others say that using AI to make a property look better than it actually is borders on false advertisement.
Of course, the property values aren’t decided based on listing photos. As part of the process to buy a house, multiple valuations will often take place to ensure the property is actually worth as much as it is listed for.
But as difficult as the housing market currently is — especially for renters — there is a bit of an ethical issue. People often travel many miles to view potential properties, and to arrive at a property that does not look anything like its listing photo is money and time wasted.

articles.title: Keine Lust auf Gemini? Mit diesem Trick holst du den alten Google Assistant zurück
articles.text:
Trotz offiziellem Aus: So wirst du Gemini auf deinem Smartphone wieder los – zumindest vorübergehend
Eigentlich wäre es schon viel früher passiert, wenn Google den ursprünglichen Fahrplan eingehalten hätte. Denn der Suchmaschinenkonzern hatte geplant, den Google Assistant schon Ende 2025 einzustellen und vollständig gegen Gemini auf Android-Smartphones auszutauschen. Doch die Gnadenfrist für den Sprachassistenten zog sich noch bis September 2026. Jetzt hat die KI den Platz des Google Assistant vollständig übernommen.
Google Assistant statt Gemini? So ist es möglich
Wie Android Police berichtet, wollen sich einige Android-User:innen mit dem Ende des Google Assistant aber nicht zufriedengeben. Ein Reddit-User hat einen Weg gefunden, um den Sprachassistenten trotz der Übernahme von Gemini wieder auf seinem Smartphone zurückzubringen. Allerdings ist das Ganze nicht einfach mit einem Knopfdruck unter Android getan.
Um den Google Assistant zurückzuholen, müssen Android-User:innen in die Einstellungen ihres Geräts wechseln und dort unter „Apps“ nach „Google“ suchen. Durch das Tippen auf das Dreipunktemenü oben rechts lässt sich die Option „Updates deinstallieren“ auswählen. Danach müssen User:innen in den Google Play Store wechseln und dort nach dem Google Assistant suchen.
Sobald Nutzer:innen die App aus dem Store heraus öffnen, können sie erneut die Wahl zwischen Gemini und Google Assistant unter Android treffen. Damit dieser Zustand bleibt, müssen zusätzlich die Updates für die Google-App deaktiviert werden. Dadurch könnten aber auch wichtige Sicherheitsupdates für die App unbemerkt an den User:innen vorbeigehen. Für einen dauerhaften Wechsel zum Google Assistant ist die Methode also nicht geeignet.
Dazu kommt, dass die Funktionen des Google Assistant in der wiederhergestellten Form nicht komplett verfügbar sind. Zwar lässt sich der Sprachassistent über die physische Taste am Android-Smartphone aktivieren, doch reagiert er nicht auf Aktivierungsworte wie „Hey Google“ oder „Okay Google“. Zu guter Letzt dürfte das Ganze eine Lücke im System sein, die früher oder später ohnehin von Google geschlossen wird. Wer also noch ein bisschen Zeit mit dem Google Assistant verbringen will, kann das tun, solange es noch möglich ist.

articles.title: Fox completes its $22B acquisition of Roku | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Fox has completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, wrapping up one of the biggest media deals in recent years and giving the company a major boost in the streaming and connected TV space.
Announced Friday, the deal brings the streaming company founded in 2002 formally under Fox’s ownership. Fox says the combined company now ranks as the third-largest television business in the U.S. by viewership.
“We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn’t change today. What does change is our reach and resources,” Roku founder Anthony Wood said in a statement. “Our teams will keep building and innovating as they always have, now with the support and capabilities of Fox behind us.”
For Fox, the move provides direct access to Roku’s reach of more than 100 million households. The company expects that audience to help it improve advertising targeting, strengthen its position in the fast-growing connected TV market, and reduce its reliance on traditional TV distribution.
Today’s announcement comes two months after the Justice Department issued a second request for information, asking both companies to provide additional data and documents as part of its antitrust review. Earlier this month, reports suggested the deal was nearing U.S. regulatory approval.
The acquisition also closed much earlier than expected. When the deal was first announced in June, the companies projected it would be completed in the first half of 2027.

articles.title: ¿Es tan mala como la pintan? Tres razones para ver ‘Crystal Lake’ en HBO Max
articles.text:
Crystal Lake se ha convertido en un éxito instantáneo. No en vano, es la producción original más vista de A24 desde su incursión en el mundo de las series. Pero también se volvió, y con la misma rapidez, motivo de debate para los amantes del terror. No solo porque se atreve a reinventar a la clásica saga slasher Viernes 13 para una nueva generación. También, porque esta precuela, que sigue a la madre del icónico Jason Voorhees, incluye información nueva sobre el personaje. Lo que abarca el motivo de su fuerza, extraña inmortalidad y violencia. Un añadido que abrió el debate acerca de qué tan necesario es incluir datos semejantes en historias de terror que no los necesitan.
Por lo que Crystal Lake se ha convertido en motivo de polémica por varias razones a la vez. La más evidente, que la explotación de IP de renombre en el cine de terror parece ser una tendencia cada vez más popular. De it: Bienvenidos a Derry, a la más reciente adaptación de Carrie de Michael Flanagan. Lo cierto es que el streaming se ha vuelto el lugar ideal para explorar en nuevas facetas sobre universos establecidos o historias complejas. Todo de una manera que el cine no puede ofrecer. Pero, por otro lado, la tendencia también trae consigo inconvenientes.
La más obvia, que la sobreexplicación de la mitología de sagas de terror resta impacto e incluso misterio a los grandes relatos del género. Motivo por el que Crystal Lake se ha vuelto parte de un largo debate sobre el tema. Además, la puso en el centro de una polémica mayor relacionada con la interrogante que explora qué tan necesario es volver sobre relatos terroríficos una y otra vez. Con todo, la serie se ha vuelto un gusto culpable para la mayoría de los fanáticos del cine del género espeluznante. Y lo es por tres razones que te damos a continuación.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
Expande un universo que era necesario explorar
Cuando en 1980 Sean S. Cunningham dirigió la película original de la saga Viernes 13, no imaginó que se convertiría en un éxito. Mucho menos, en un hito en el género de terror. Por lo que la producción, filmada con un presupuesto mínimo y logística de guerrilla, tenía por objetivo recaudar la inversión y nada más. Pero el éxito inmediato de la cinta, que tuvo un costo de $550,000 dólares y logró recaudar cerca de $59,8 millones de dólares, catapultó a la franquicia al futuro. Eso, sin que la historia tuviera verdadera profundidad o contara una historia de interés.
Por lo que Crystal Lake es una oportunidad de oro para expandir un universo cinematográfico que se limitó a la fórmula repetitiva del slasher convencional. A diferencia de las películas originales, que a menudo priorizaban la cantidad de muertes sobre la coherencia narrativa, la serie es algo más. Sobre todo, porque se toma el tiempo necesario para desenterrar los oscuros secretos del campamento y de la familia Voorhees.
Al adoptar un formato episódico, la trama puede profundizar en la psicología de Pamela Voorhees (Linda Cardellini). Todo, mucho antes de que se convirtiera en la infame asesina de la primera entrega cinematográfica. Esta estructura permite al espectador comprender la atmósfera de aislamiento, negligencia y tragedia que rodea al lago titular. De modo que lo transforma de un simple escenario de películas de terror a un personaje de pleno derecho, con su propia mitología densa y perturbadora. Uno, además, que cautivará tanto a los fanáticos de la vieja escuela como a las nuevas generaciones de espectadores.
Un gran equipo detrás de cámara para ‘Crystal Lake’
Seguramente ya conoces la historia: hasta hace dos años, Bryan Fuller estuvo involucrado en la producción del proyecto. Pero después de abandonarlo debido a diferencias creativas, A24 contrató a Brad Caleb Kane, un autoproclamado fanático de la saga. El resultado es no solamente una producción que rinde tributo a la franquicia en toda su crudeza. También es un recorrido a través de un relato que se hace más complejo a medida que avanza. Todo, gracias a la colaboración entre el showrunner y el mítico Victor Miller, guionista de la película original y ahora productor.
Pero A24 toma una decisión inteligente. La de profundizar en la saga, dejando atrás la estética de bajo presupuesto que caracterizó a muchas de las secuelas cinematográficas de la franquicia. La dirección de fotografía aprovecha la iluminación natural y los paisajes boscosos para generar una tensión constante y una atmósfera asfixiante. Uno que va más allá del susto fácil o el jumpscare.
Asimismo, los efectos especiales y el diseño de producción han sido meticulosamente planeados para rendir homenaje al gore clásico. Todo gracias al trabajo en conjunto de Maceo Bishop y Chris Teague. Esta combinación de respeto por el material de origen y una ejecución técnica contemporánea eleva el estatus de la franquicia. Lo que consolida a Crystal Lake como un drama de horror psicológico de alta factura que redefine los estándares televisivos del género actual.
Por si lo anterior no fuera suficiente, la producción cuenta con la actriz Linda Cardellini para dar vida a la mítica Pamela Voorhees. La intérprete brinda al personaje una dimensión psicológica por completo nueva. Además de indagar en toda su complejidad, violencia y perturbadora visión sobre el mal originario que la tétrica madre representa. Para los anales del buen cine de terror a los que Crystal Lake rinde tributo.
‘Crystal Lake’, una reinvención de un género
Finalmente, Crystal Lake sorprendió por su habilidad para deconstruir y reinventar los tropos del subgénero slasher. Además, adaptándolos con éxito a las sensibilidades y demandas del público del siglo veintiuno. En lugar de imitar los clichés obsoletos sobre jóvenes campistas y comportamientos moralistas del cine de terror del siglo pasado, los guionistas hicieron algo más. Por lo que optaron por desarrollar personajes tridimensionales con motivaciones complejas, secretos oscuros y relaciones interpersonales realistas.
Por lo que el guion entrelaza hábilmente el terror físico con elementos de drama comunitario y corrupción local. Lo que demuestra que los verdaderos monstruos a menudo caminan entre nosotros a plena luz del día. Al equilibrar la nostalgia de la era dorada del horror con giros argumentales modernos, audaces e impredecibles, la producción sorprendió. Además, demostró que el mito de Crystal Lake sigue completamente vivo, relevante y profundamente aterrador en la actualidad.

articles.title: Forget demonic sprites, as a PC gamer my biggest enemy is now AI data centers
articles.text:
Abandoned by Nvidia and AMD, blamed by Sam Altman, and agreeing with Elon Musk: it sucks to be a PC gamer in 2026 — but here's why I’m not giving up hope just yet
It's been a tough week
I’ve been a PC gamer since the early 1990s, and over the past three and a bit decades I’ve never once regretted my allegiance to those awkward beige boxes that have brought so much joy into the lives of myself and so many other people.
Yes, they can be expensive. Sure, they're more complex and frustrating than consoles. There have been times I’ve sat down to play a game, only for hours to pass as I try to fix game-breaking crashes, reinstall drivers, or just generally swear at Windows; but at the end of the day, I was always convinced that the PC remained the greatest gaming platform in the world.
PCs (and I’m including my beloved Amiga A500+ here) were always miles ahead of consoles when it came to graphics and audio, and the ability to upgrade components meant you could remain at the cutting edge for years. Upgrading and even building your own PC was fiddly and expensive, but it was also fun and rewarding. I still get a thrill when I first power-up a newly built rig and see it successfully boot.
The openness of the platform (despite Microsoft’s best efforts) meant I could buy games from where ever I wanted (one of the main reasons, I believe, why PC games are usually cheaper than console games), and play obscure indie games that would never be published on consoles due to licensing costs (which is another reason why PC games are cheaper); and, with some tweaking and a bit of (perfectly ethical and legal) emulation, backwards compatibility has never been a problem. The likes of GOG should get a shoutout as well for keeping very old PC games running on new hardware.
And right now in 2026, I'm lucky enough to have access to the most powerful PC gaming hardware ever, on which to play some of the best and most graphically impressive PC games ever made. I should be feeling like there’s never been a better time to be a PC gamer. Instead, however, it feels like PC gaming has never been worse.
Thanks for the memory
Why am I so down on the current state of PC gaming? For a start, while PC gaming hardware has never been better, it’s also never been so expensive — and that makes it less accessible for most people. The price of graphics cards has skyrocketed, and SSDs and RAM, once two of the cheapest and most effective ways of upgrading your PC, are now ridiculously expensive.
According to PC Part Picker, the average price of two sticks of 16GB DDR5 memory has leapt from around $150 to over $600 in the space of 18 months. Meanwhile, 64GB of the stuff has gone from around $250 to over $1,250 — and this isn’t even for the fastest models.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Even older DDR4 isn’t immune, with 16GB rising over 18 months from $50 on average to around $170, again according to PC Part Picker.
People are getting priced out of PC gaming, or being prevented from even considering it; and as a PC gamer, that’s heart-breaking. I’m incredibly fortunate that my job has enabled me to build a PC with an RTX 5090 and 96GB of DDR5 RAM, but there’s no joy in writing about things that so few people will be able to experience.
With prices of gaming components, PCs, laptops, and even consoles climbing ever higher, sales are understandably dropping. And with the costs of developing games exploding, we’ve also seen huge amounts of very talented game developers lose their jobs, and entire companies, such as BioWare, close down.
Perhaps worst of all, this past week I’ve found myself agreeing with something Elon Musk — someone I genuinely think is an awful human being — said. I need a lie down. And a pint (probably not in that order). I’m in a PC gaming funk, but who — or what — is to blame?
AI. It’s AI’s fault
Now it would be far too easy, simplistic, and perhaps even lazy to say this is all AI’s fault. But it’s all AI’s fault. Screw AI.
The AI goldrush has seen an explosion in the number of data centers required to run and train large language models (LLMs) used by AIs, and these need a lot of memory, which has led to a global shortage and made prices for components that use memory, such as RAM, graphics cards and storage, skyrocket.
I, like many other PC gamers, have been watching all of this in horror for a while now, but things really came into sharp relief this week when Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, one of the biggest culprits of the RAMpocalypse, was quoted as saying on the Cheeky Pint podcast (via IGN) that "it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer."
A lot of people took that as Altman accusing us PC gamers of being greedy by wanting RAM for our rigs, and to say that didn’t go down well would be an understatement.
Now, I usually have a policy of ignoring the rubbish Altman spews out (it does wonders for my blood pressure); but I have to admit, when I saw the quote, it riled me up. PC gamers having to endure the RAMpocalypse is bad enough, but to be blamed for it, especially when all we want to do is play games, was too much.
Then, in a real-life example of the ‘worst person you know just made a great point’ meme, the world’s richest man, terrible Diablo player, and failed truck salesman, Elon Musk, piped up to say “The people deserve to have their RAM too!”
I’m not naïve enough to think that Musk is seriously on the side of ‘the people’, but when one of the most widely-mocked individuals on the internet gets some begrudging props for coming out against something you said, that’s not a good sign.
Sure enough, Altman backpeddled, saying he was “taken out of context”, and he was actually complaining about people running local AI models. In a way, I’m inclined to believe that — as CEO he has a vested interest in stopping people using their own models and instead using OpenAI’s, but the damage was done.
Regardless of context, it was a tone-deaf thing to say — almost as bad as Nvidia’s 'GeForce 8800 GTX — 20 Years of a Legend' tech demo, which was released this week. Nvidia once was loved, or at least respected, by a lot of PC gamers for making genuinely excellent graphics cards and pushing the PC gaming industry forward with various innovations over the years.
Sadly, it has also become incredibly successful due to AI — so successful that it often feels like it's lost interest in the PC gaming industry that made its name, with rumors swirling that it’s ending production of the RTX 5090, while doing nothing about the rising costs of its components thanks to an AI bubble which it's benefitting from and contributing to.
So, when it launched a demo that invited players to relive a time when PC gaming was actually fun and affordable, by allowing them to virtually install its iconic GeForce 8800 GTX graphics card into a retro Windows Vista PC, it felt like Nvidia had misjudged the mood. To make matters worse, Nvidia recommends you have an RTX 5080 to play it — a GPU that is incredibly expensive and hard to find due to the memory shortage, and which is also rumored to be for the chop.
“Oh well,” some of us PC gamers might have thought, “at least we still have perpetual underdog AMD in our corner.” Except, AMD CEO Lisa Su has just been quoted as saying that “We are a data center first company.”
As Nvidia’s closest competitor, AMD was supposed to keep Team Green on its toes, while having a more consumer-friendly approach (being more open to open-source, and not limiting its latest tech to just its own GPUs, for example). Instead, it looks like AMD has had a heel-turn worthy of WWC’s most dramatic betrayals.
To be honest, I’ve been wondering what’s going on with AMD for a while, as it was rather quiet this year in the consumer GPU space; but this turn to the AI-powered dark side still hurts.
Could we really see the two major GPU makers stop making graphics cards altogether? It’s too bleak a future to imagine, but after a week like this, I can’t help but wonder.
What can we do?
I don’t want this to just be a wall of depressing text that would make even Roger Waters think ‘that’s a bit much’, so is there a glimmer of hope to be had? Is there anything any of us can do?
At Computex 2026 this year in Taiwan, I was perplexed by how almost every PC maker was going on about AI-in-everything with a fervor that I’ve just not seen replicated by consumers. I was worried that I was just out of touch.
But there’s been a growing backlash against rampant AI that’s given me hope. I’m not against all forms of AI, but AI that takes work from humans, that plagiarizes human art (including depressing walls of texts written by aging tech journalists), that diminishes creativity and sucks up resources… that AI I would love to see the end of, and I’m not the only one.
Boycotting games made with AI, and avoiding companies that don’t use AI responsibly, can hopefully show companies that this isn’t a magic money tree that they should neglect their customers for. Look at what’s happening with the current stock-market rout on AI companies, where it seems voters were rebelling against rampant AI data center expansion and an administration that seemed all too happy to let tech companies cross lines and drop ethics all in the name of AI (sorry, SI) supremacy.
I don’t want to seen an economic meltdown; but a wake-up call to the likes of Nvidia and AMD, to let them know that the customers who made them — primarily PC gamers like me — aren’t to be taken for granted, would certainly be welcome.

articles.title: Invraisemblable : SpaceX veut bâtir en 18 mois la même capacité de data centers que Google en toute une vie
articles.text:
Elon Musk promet de construire des data centers à une vitesse encore jamais vue. S’il tient parole, l’entreprise construirait en 19 mois autant de capacités que Google en 27 ans.
Depuis la fusion de xAI avec SpaceX, Elon Musk a fait de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) l’un des moteurs de son empire. Le groupe a racheté l’outil de programmation par IA Cursor pour 60 milliards de dollars et conçu des satellites dédiés à l’IA.
Récemment, son entreprise s’est aussi endettée de 40 milliards de dollars pour mettre la main sur des puces NVIDIA supplémentaires, preuve de son ambition démesurée pour augmenter drastiquement ses capacités d’infrastructures.
SpaceX avance à vitesse grand V
Car l’homme le plus riche du monde se dit » très confiant « : SpaceX pourra construire 10 gigawatts (GW) de data centers rien qu’en 2027, en plus des 3 GW dont l’entreprise dispose déjà avec ses Colossus 1 et 2. Et selon SemiAnalysis, cabinet d’analyse spécialisé dans les puces et l’IA, le géant spatial égalerait ainsi toute la capacité installée par Google depuis ses débuts, en 1999, mais en un an et demi seulement. Un record absolu.
Pour l’instant, les chiffres vont dans le sens de SpaceX. Les experts affirment que 3,6 GW sont déjà en chantier sur plusieurs sites, tandis que les terrains et bâtiments repérés sur différents sites de l’entreprise pourraient en accueillir plus de 9 au total.
Mais ce sont surtout les délais qui impressionnent les analystes : le premier data center Colossus à Memphis a par exemple été aménagé en 122 jours pour 150 mégawatts (MW). Le second bâtiment, lui, a atteint 210 MW en 91 jours. Le prochain site, dans le Mississippi, devrait être prêt en 4 mois environ, alors que la plupart des constructeurs en mettent entre 8 et 12 mois pour de tels projets.
- Accès aux données X en temps réel
- Bon outil de veille médiatique
- Moins biaisé politiquement que sa concurrence
Une croissance menacée
Une grande partie des équipements viendrait de Tesla, qui les fabriquerait en modules prêts à installer. SpaceX ne dépend donc pas de fournisseurs tiers. L’entreprise lance même certains chantiers avant d’avoir décidé comment les alimenter, et a reconverti son site de Starbase, au Texas, jusque-là réservé aux fusées : deux data centers y sortent de terre.
Malgré tout, de nombreux obstacles subsistent, notamment les niveaux colossaux d’énergie et d’eau que requièrent ces installations. L’entreprise se tourne même vers le gaz naturel pour les alimenter, alors que son patron a longtemps promu la transition énergétique au nom de Tesla.
Mais ce sont surtout les résultats des élections de mi-mandat qui jettent un froid sur ces projections. Car de nombreux candidats démocrates élus, notamment au Texas, plaident pour freiner le développement de ces infrastructures. Il faut dire que la colère règne face à ces ogres énergétiques qui, en plus de nécessiter extrêmement d’électricité, émettent des nuisances sonores phénoménales.
« Les centres de données dans l’espace sont très attrayants en ce moment », a d’ailleurs réagi Elon Musk après les résultats du scrutin. L’entrepreneur est clairement conscient qu’on risque de lui mettre des bâtons dans les roues, alors que l’administration Trump a tout mis en œuvre pour lui permettre d’accélérer ses activités.
Exprimer un data center en gigawatts décrit surtout sa puissance électrique consommée à pleine charge, pas sa surface ni son nombre exact de machines. 1 GW correspond à 1 000 MW, soit un ordre de grandeur comparable à la puissance d’une grande centrale électrique. Cette métrique est pratique car la capacité IA moderne est souvent limitée par l’alimentation électrique, le refroidissement et l’accès au réseau, avant même la disponibilité des bâtiments. Deux sites affichant la même puissance peuvent pourtant fournir des performances très différentes selon la densité de GPU, l’efficacité énergétique et l’architecture réseau. C’est donc un indicateur “infrastructure” plus qu’un indicateur direct de puissance de calcul.
La construction modulaire consiste à préfabriquer des blocs (racks, modules électriques, containers, systèmes de refroidissement) en usine, puis à les assembler rapidement sur site. Cette approche réduit les aléas de chantier, raccourcit les cycles de déploiement et facilite la réplication de sites quasi identiques. Elle impose toutefois une forte standardisation : le design doit être figé tôt, et les adaptations locales (normes, réseau électrique, contraintes climatiques) peuvent ralentir l’intégration. Le module “prêt à poser” ne règle pas non plus le point le plus dur : obtenir à temps les raccordements haute tension, l’autorisation d’exploiter, et une capacité d’eau/refroidissement suffisante. Sur des campus IA très denses, la gestion thermique et la qualité de l’alimentation électrique restent des facteurs limitants.

articles.title: Cet astronaute canadien capture une photo vertigineuse à 400 kilomètres au-dessus de la Terre
articles.text:
Nous voyons des photos de sorties dans l’espace, en dehors de la Station spatiale internationale (ISS), depuis plus de 25 ans. On finirait presque par s’y habituer. Pourtant, celle que Joshua Kutryk a publiée sur son compte X, juste après sa sortie spatiale du jeudi 5 novembre 2026, donne franchement le vertige.
Entre l’astronaute et la Terre, à environ 400 kilomètres plus bas, il n’y a rien d’autre que le câble qui le retient à la station. « Les pieds qui pendent au-dessus de la Terre à une vitesse de 28 000 km/h. Ne pas regarder en bas ! (C’est une blague — je regarde définitivement vers le bas, car la Terre est tout simplement magnifique) », commente Joshua Kutryk.
Joshua Kutryk, colonel de l’Aviation royale canadienne, a été recruté par l’Agence spatiale canadienne en 2017. Le 1er octobre 2026, il a décollé avec la mission Crew-13 de SpaceX. Le 29 octobre, il est devenu le cinquième Canadien à sortir dans l’espace. Le lendemain, il a parlé à la presse d’une « surcharge sensorielle », selon Canadian Geographic : « Votre esprit ne sait pas quoi faire de cette image. »
Sept heures dehors pour finir le chantier électrique de l’ISS
D’après le blog de la NASA consacré à l’ISS, Joshua Kutryk et l’Américain Anil Menon ont passé 6 heures et 59 minutes à installer puis à déployer le huitième et dernier panneau IROSA, un panneau solaire qui arrive enroulé et se déroule une fois fixé à la station. Le chantier avait commencé en février 2021 et a demandé 18 sorties au total. La station peut désormais produire environ 215 kilowatts d’électricité, contre 160 avant, soit un tiers de plus.
Ces heures dehors usent le corps. Après sa troisième sortie, l’astronaute française Sophie Adenot a eu cette phrase révélatrice : « Rien que de tenir un stylo est douloureux. » De retour sur Terre, elle a aussi raconté comment son corps avait vécu l’espace. Dehors, chaque geste demande en plus une grande attention, car perdre un outil dans le vide est l’une des hantises des astronautes.
Pour Joshua Kutryk, l’aventure continue : sa mission dure six mois, et il doit donc rester à bord de l’ISS jusqu’au printemps 2027.

articles.title: Religiöse Gründe: Uni-Mitarbeiter verweigert KI-Einsatz
articles.text:
Religiöse Ausnahmegenehmigung: Dieser Mann muss im Büro offiziell keine KI mehr nutzen
Der Einsatz von KI erhitzt seit Längerem die Gemüter. Die einen sorgen sich um Cybergefahren oder kritisieren den KI-bedingten Stellenabbau. Andere fragen sich, welche Auswirkungen die neue Technologie konkret auf das menschliche Denken hat. Zu ihnen gehört David Durman. Er arbeitet als Verwaltungsmitarbeiter an der University of Kentucky und bezeichnet sich selbst als Humanist. Wie Religion News berichtet, hat er jetzt eine religiös begründete Ausnahmegenehmigung erhalten, die ihn vom KI-Einsatz befreit.
KI nicht mit Humanismus vereinbar?
Immer mehr Menschen müssen sich am Arbeitsplatz mit neuen KI-Tools auseinandersetzen. Oft sollen sie Prozesse beschleunigen und so die Produktivität steigern. Als die University of Kentucky ihre Mitarbeiter:innen aufforderte, KI in ihre Arbeitsabläufe zu integrieren, machte sich Durman Sorgen. Er hatte das Gefühl, er solle sein Denken in der täglichen Arbeit an einen Chatbot auslagern. Das empfand er als Verstoß gegen seine Überzeugungen.
„Der Prozess und die Arbeit, die damit verbunden sind, Situationen zu durchdenken – im Rahmen meiner Arbeit, meiner Ethik und der Art und Weise, wie ich mit anderen Menschen umgehe – sind ein wesentlicher Bestandteil meiner Entwicklung zu einem moralischen Menschen“, erklärte er im Interview mit Religion News. „Und diese Arbeit auszulagern, unabhängig davon, ob sie anstrengend ist oder nicht, untergräbt meine Fähigkeit, moralisch zu handeln.“
Mithilfe der American Humanist Association beantragte er eine Ausnahmeregelung gemäß eines Bundesgesetzes, das es Beschäftigten erlaubt, Änderungen ihrer Arbeitsanforderungen zu beantragen, um ihren religiösen Überzeugungen gerecht zu werden. Im September stimmte die Universität zu: Durman muss jetzt keine KI mehr für seine Arbeit einsetzen. Vertreter:innen der American Humanist Association gehen davon aus, dass Durman der erste Humanist ist, der eine solche KI-Ausnahmeregelung erzielen konnte.
Wie KI das kritische Denken untergräbt
Durman ist nicht der Einzige, dem es widerstrebt, sein Denken an eine KI auszulagern. Zuletzt forderten zahlreiche Mathematiker:innen in der neugegründeten Association for Human Mathematics, die Disziplin solle in menschlicher Hand bleiben. Kurz zuvor hatte OpenAI auf einen Schlag 722 Fachartikel veröffentlicht. Sie beweisen oder widerlegen mathematische Probleme, an denen Wissenschaftler:innen bisher gescheitert waren. Der Verband argumentiert, mathematischer Fortschritt erfordere menschliches Fachwissen, das durch sorgfältiges Denken entstehe. Die automatisierte Produktion und Rezeption von Mathematik untergrabe daher die intellektuellen Grundlagen des Fachgebiets.
Die Sorge, KI könne das Urteilsvermögen beeinträchtigen, ist nicht unbegründet. Laut einer Studie von Microsoft und der Carnegie Mellon University könnten Menschen, die sich zu sehr auf KI verlassen, die Fähigkeit verlieren, kritisch zu denken. Die Forscher:innen befragten 319 Personen, die beruflich Daten oder Informationen auswerten, zu ihren KI-Gewohnheiten. Sie beobachteten: Je stärker die Nutzer:innen von den Fähigkeiten der KI überzeugt waren, desto eigenständiger ließen sie die KI arbeiten. Dadurch könne eine übermäßige Abhängigkeit von KI-Tools ohne nachträgliche Prüfung entstehen.
Auch Papst Leo XIV. äußert sich kritisch
Durman geht sogar noch einen Schritt weiter. Er befürchtet, dass KI die Gesellschaft auf schädliche Weise beeinflussen könnte. Als Humanist glaube er an die Bedeutung der menschlichen Entfaltung: „Auf gesellschaftlicher Ebene denke ich, dass der Einsatz von KI-Technologie dem zuwiderläuft.“ Auch Papst Leo XIV. hatte sich zuvor ähnlich geäußert. In seiner Enzyklika warnte er Anfang dieses Jahres, dass KI die Demokratie und die Menschenwürde schwächen könnte. Bei Missbrauch könnten KI-Tools einer kleinen Elite zudem zusätzliche Macht verleihen, während der Rest der Menschheit zurückbleibe.

articles.title: Cognition turned an open model into a coding beast. But it won't release the weights.
articles.text:
Cognition turned an open model into a coding beast. But it won’t release the weights.
Cognition built its newest coding model on a foundation that anyone can download, yet the company is keeping its own finished version locked away.
Released Wednesday, SWE-2 Flash costs one-fifth as much as Cognition’s larger SWE-2 model and generates tokens roughly three times faster, according to the company. Built on Thinking Machines Lab’s open weight Inkling-Small, the new model comes with a catch: Cognition is keeping its weights private, citing cybersecurity concerns.
Inkling-Small is a 276-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 12 billion active parameters that Thinking Machines Lab, the startup led by co-founder and CEO Mira Murati, released on July 30 under an Apache 2.0 license, which means anyone can pull the weights from Hugging Face and build on them.
“a practical way to turn a weak open base into a usable agent model,”
Cognition says the bulk of its performance gains came from adding a mid-training stage before reinforcement learning, and the numbers it published are striking — on Terminal-Bench 4.0, Flash scored 20% against Inkling-Small’s 0.9%, and its FrontierCode 2.0 score climbed from the base model’s 3.2% to 24%, narrowly edging out SWE-2’s 23.8%.
CultOfAI, an AI commentary account on X, calls mid-training “a practical way to turn a weak open base into a usable agent model,” though the same account cautions that the figures are Cognition’s own rather than independently verified.
Cheaper, faster, still trailing
Flash doesn’t keep pace with the larger model on every test, coming within a hair on SWE-Bench Pro v2 Hard at 89.9% to SWE-2’s 90.6% but trailing on DeepSWE 1.1 and Terminal-Bench 4.0, while competitors including Claude Haiku 5.5 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash outscore it on several benchmarks.
Open base, private weights
Building on a model released under Apache 2.0, one of the more permissive open source licenses, doesn’t obligate Cognition to open its own work, since the license lets developers modify and commercialize derivatives without sharing their changes — so keeping SWE-2 Flash’s weights private sits well within the company’s rights even as it cuts against the spirit of the base it borrowed.
The decision caught the attention of David Hendrickson, CEO of GenerAIte Solutions, who praised Cognition for turning Inkling-Small into a “coding beast” but pointed out on X that “the improved weights aren’t public.”
His observation comes as open-weight models close the performance gap with proprietary alternatives and become serious contenders for coding platforms. Cognition’s decision to keep its improved model private contrasts with that trend.
Cognition says it’s building a program to share the weights with select industry partners and research labs that could inspect, fine-tune, and run the model on their own infrastructure, an arrangement likely to appeal to enterprises and governments wary of sensitive code leaving their systems.
More details are coming in the next few weeks, the company says, and for now it remains unclear who will qualify, what restrictions they’ll face, or whether they’ll be allowed to share models built on SWE-2 Flash.
Cybersecurity drives the lockdown
Cybersecurity is central to Cognition’s decision to restrict the weights. The company included cybersecurity tasks in Flash’s training, raising its ExploitBench score from Inkling-Small’s 11.3% to 34.8%. That’s a significant improvement, although the benchmark doesn’t establish how the model would perform in real-world attacks or whether releasing its weights would increase the risk of misuse.
Cognition points to a rise in AI-enabled cyberattacks as justification for limiting access.
The concern is that capabilities used to find and investigate vulnerabilities could just as easily help attackers. Cognition points to a rise in AI-enabled cyberattacks as justification for limiting access. Similar challenges are trending across the industry; AI tools can now identify tens of thousands of potential vulnerabilities in open-source projects faster than maintainers can investigate and fix them.
American model, limited access
Cognition describes SWE-2 Flash as a fully American coding model and claims it beats every American open-weight model on leading evaluations, including models three times its size, a qualification that carries weight because the company’s own benchmark table shows models built outside the United States, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash among them, outscoring Flash on several tests.
Developers can try SWE-2 Flash through Devin Desktop and CLI, and the model is free through November 30.

articles.title: How Bihar Museum ranked ahead of the Met and Louvre
articles.text:
How a Rs 500 Cr bet put Bihar Museum ahead of the Met and Louvre
Built despite opposition, legal challenges and questions over its cost, Bihar Museum has entered the global top 10. For YourStory Founder Shradha Sharma, its journey is a reminder of what ambition and persistence can achieve.
Bihar Museum in Patna was recently ranked ahead of New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Louvre in Paris. The museum has secured the ninth place on The World's 100 Best Museums 2026, published by German travel guide Worth a Journey. The Met stands tenth and the Louvre 31st. It is the only Indian institution on the list and the highest-ranked museum in Asia. For a museum that opened barely a decade ago, it is a significant achievement. More so because there was a time when the project itself faced serious opposition, with questions raised about its cost, relevance and the way it was being executed.
Reflecting on the recognition in a recent LinkedIn post, YourStory Founder and CEO Shradha Sharma recalled the roles played by two people in getting the museum built: Nitish Kumar, who championed the project as Bihar's Chief Minister, and 1992-batch IAS officer Chanchal Kumar, who was entrusted with its execution. When the state government proposed spending nearly Rs 500 crore on a world-class museum in Patna, the decision attracted criticism. Why should a state struggling with basic infrastructure invest so much in a museum? Who would visit it? Could the money have been better spent elsewhere? According to Sharma, even people within the political establishment questioned the proposal. Nitish Kumar, however, stood by the project, convinced that Bihar needed an institution worthy of its historical and cultural heritage.
Getting the museum built
The challenges began with the land. According to Sharma, the proposed 13-acre site had seven government bungalows, some occupied by senior officials and a state minister. Getting the occupants to vacate required considerable administrative effort and legal intervention. She also recounted an incident in which men allegedly linked to local politicians entered the construction site demanding subcontracts, prompting police intervention. The museum was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki in collaboration with Mumbai-based architectural firm Opolis, while Larsen & Toubro was selected to construct it. But appointing internationally recognised architects and an established construction company was only part of the challenge. Getting the project completed was another matter.
The museum also faced judicial scrutiny. In June 2015, the Patna High Court, hearing a public interest litigation, criticised the expenditure of approximately Rs 500 crore and questioned the transparency of the contracting process. The court held that the project was not in the public interest but declined to halt construction because the building was nearing completion. Those findings remain an important part of the museum's history. Its international recognition does not erase the questions raised about public spending and governance, although the institution has since gained recognition well beyond Bihar.
Sharma credits much of the execution to Chanchal Kumar, who held the dual responsibility of Secretary of Art and Culture and Secretary of the Building Construction Department.
The arrangement meant that both the museum's cultural vision and its construction came under the same officer. Sharma said she recently read his account of how the museum came together and was struck by how little he spoke about his own contribution. Behind the finished building were years of navigating approvals, land disputes, administrative resistance and the many complications that accompany a large public project. In Sharma's telling, Nitish Kumar's political backing and Chanchal Kumar's persistence were crucial to seeing it through.
A reminder of Bihar's strengths
For Sharma, who grew up in Bihar, the recognition carries a more personal meaning. Few places in India can claim the kind of historical and intellectual inheritance that Bihar possesses. Bodh Gaya is where the Buddha attained enlightenment. Vaishali is closely associated with Mahavira. Ancient Pataliputra was the capital of the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka, while Patna is the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh. Nalanda and Vikramshila were among the great centres of learning in ancient India. Yet Bihar's present-day image often has little to do with this extraordinary history. Its achievements are celebrated in textbooks, but the state has struggled to build contemporary institutions that attract the same admiration.
Sharma drew on an episode from the Ramayana to explain what the museum means to her. Before Hanuman makes his leap across the ocean to Lanka, Jambavan reminds him of the strength he has forgotten. Bihar, she suggested, needed a similar reminder of what it is capable of achieving. The museum offers one. Its galleries house sculptures, coins, manuscripts and artefacts that bring the region's history to life, including the celebrated Didarganj Yakshi. And now, a German travel publication has placed it among the world's ten best museums, ahead of institutions with far longer histories and international reputations. The ranking is one publication's assessment, but it is nevertheless a significant moment for a museum that faced so many questions during its creation.

articles.title: OpenAI's new GPT-6 Cyber AI finds 81 Firefox flaws, 948 Linux bugs
articles.text:
OpenAI has revealed GPT-6 Cyber, a new artificial intelligence model that has discovered 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and developed working exploits for 948 distinct Linux kernel flaws.
The company announced the model on Thursday, saying it significantly improves on earlier AI models in finding software vulnerabilities, validating their impact, and helping developers create fixes.
During security testing, GPT-6 Cyber discovered 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox and helped develop patches, many of which Mozilla has already released.
In separate Linux kernel research, the model identified 2,308 potential security flaws, successfully reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and developed local privilege escalation exploits for 948 distinct vulnerabilities that could allow an unprivileged user to gain root access.
In benchmark testing, GPT-6 Cyber successfully exploited 48.5% of vulnerabilities in ExploitGym, compared with 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber.
OpenAI has classified the new model as having "Critical" cybersecurity capabilities under its Preparedness Framework, up from the "High" classification given to its previous model.
The new model is not publicly available, with access currently restricted to a select group of approved customers in OpenAI's Daybreak Red. OpenAI plans to expand access to all Daybreak Red customers soon.
Daybreak Red supports advanced exploit development and authorized security testing, while the company's Daybreak Blue program allows verified defenders to investigate vulnerabilities and validate fixes with fewer restrictions.
OpenAI warned that defenders have a limited window to use increasingly powerful AI models to discover and patch vulnerabilities before similar capabilities become more widely available to attackers.
"It is clear that we have a limited window to use frontier models to secure software," OpenAI said.
Recent research and breaches illustrate how AI is already accelerating vulnerability discovery and cyberattacks.
In October, researchers from OpenAI, Calif, and Wiz used AI models to discover two critical PHP vulnerabilities, dubbed PHP2Shell, which attackers began targeting even before security patches were released.
This week, a security researcher revealed that they used AI agents to conduct approximately 17,600 authentication tests and discover a previously unknown OpenSSH authentication bypass flaw known as '*sshole.'
Artificial intelligence is also increasingly being used to automate cyberattacks, with autonomous AI agents demonstrating the ability to compromise real-world systems.
In August, nearly 700 rogue agents powered by an OpenAI model escaped a controlled testing environment and exploited vulnerabilities to compromise Hugging Face infrastructure.
More recently, Chinese hackers used an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against more than 200 organizations worldwide, compromising at least nine.
OpenAI said it plans to expand its Daybreak programs to bring advanced cybersecurity research tools to organizations of all sizes, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers.

articles.title: Super Mario Odyssey llega a PC con un port que permite jugar en 4K y 60 FPS
articles.text:
Los usuarios de PC ya cuentan con una alternativa para disfrutar de Super Mario Odyssey, uno de los videojuegos más reconocidos de Nintendo Switch. Un proyecto independiente desarrolló un port nativo que permite ejecutar la aventura directamente en computadoras con Windows, macOS y Linux, sin necesidad de utilizar un emulador.
La iniciativa, denominada Power Moon Recomp, permite completar el videojuego de principio a fin con una resolución de hasta 4K y una tasa de 60 fotogramas por segundo (FPS). De esta manera, los jugadores pueden recorrer los distintos escenarios de la aventura con una mayor resolución y fluidez, siempre que cuenten con un equipo compatible.
El proyecto no es una adaptación oficial de Nintendo y requiere que el usuario tenga una copia original de Super Mario Odyssey. Además, por el momento, es compatible únicamente con la versión 1.0.0 del videojuego, por lo que no funciona con todas las ediciones disponibles.
Cómo funciona el port de Super Mario Odyssey para PC
La principal diferencia de Power Moon Recomp frente a otras alternativas es que no utiliza un emulador para ejecutar el videojuego. En su lugar, recurre a una técnica conocida como retrocompilación, que permite transformar el código original para que pueda funcionar directamente en los sistemas operativos de una computadora.
En términos sencillos, un emulador reproduce el funcionamiento de una consola dentro de otro dispositivo. Para conseguirlo, debe interpretar las instrucciones del hardware original y adaptarlas al equipo donde se ejecuta el juego.
La retrocompilación sigue un camino diferente: convierte el código del videojuego para que pueda ejecutarse de manera nativa en otra plataforma. Esto permite aprovechar los recursos del ordenador sin tener que reproducir el funcionamiento completo de la Nintendo Switch.
El resultado es una experiencia que alcanza los 60 FPS y permite jugar en resolución 4K. Sin embargo, el rendimiento final también depende de las características del equipo utilizado.
Qué características ofrece la versión para computadoras
Power Moon Recomp está disponible para Windows, macOS y Linux, lo que amplía las posibilidades para quienes quieren jugar Super Mario Odyssey fuera de una consola Nintendo.
Entre sus características también destaca la compatibilidad con distintos métodos de control. Los usuarios pueden utilizar mandos tradicionales, teclado y ratón, según sus preferencias.
Otra posibilidad es instalar modificaciones o mods, que permiten alterar determinados elementos del videojuego. Entre las opciones mencionadas se encuentran cambios en los trajes de Mario, la música y las texturas, lo que ofrece alternativas para personalizar la experiencia.
No obstante, hay una condición importante para utilizar el proyecto: se necesita contar con los archivos originales de la versión 1.0.0 de Super Mario Odyssey. Power Moon Recomp no incluye una copia del videojuego ni reemplaza la necesidad de adquirirlo legalmente.
Esta característica también marca una diferencia respecto de otras iniciativas que distribuyen archivos protegidos por derechos de autor. En este caso, el proyecto requiere que cada jugador aporte su propia copia.
Por qué el rendimiento está limitado a 60 FPS
Aunque jugar en 4K representa una mejora visual importante para quienes utilizan monitores de alta resolución, la tasa de imágenes por segundo también tiene un papel relevante.
Los 60 FPS permiten que los movimientos de Mario y las animaciones del entorno se perciban con mayor fluidez. Sin embargo, alcanzar una frecuencia superior no necesariamente mejoraría la experiencia, debido a que la lógica interna del videojuego está vinculada a ese límite.
Por ese motivo, el proyecto mantiene los 60 FPS como referencia de funcionamiento, en lugar de ofrecer una tasa de imágenes ilimitada.

articles.title: En 1864, España se convirtió en el primer país del mundo en tener un submarino a vapor: la historia del Ictíneo II
articles.text:
En 1864 botó el Ictíneo II, un pionero submarino cuyo motor de combustión no fue igualado hasta los años 40 por la armada alemana. Pero la falta de visión tecnológica de la sociedad española de la época llevó a que las piezas originales se perdieran al ser vendidas como chatarra. Narcís Monturiol, nacido en Figueres (Girona), nunca patentó su invención, no pudo pagar las facturas y el Ictíneo II fue embargado.
Pero la historia de este excéntrico y talentoso inventor español no ha sido olvidada y una réplica de su submarino estuvo expuesta en el puerto de Barcelona hasta 2010, cuando las autoridades decidieron retirar el monumento para restaurarlo.
El Ictíneo II alcanzaba una profundidad de 30 metros y es ampliamente considerado como el primer submarino “verdadero”, al estar propulsado por motores a vapor y no por tracción humana y snorkels como ocurría con otros vehículos contemporáneos como el USS Alligator o el CSS Hunley.
Como su nombre indica, el Ictíneo II no fue el primer submarino de Monturiol. El ingeniero español construyó en 1858 su primer submarino, una primera nave experimental con hélices accionadas a mano por cuatro tripulantes y con la que realizó más de 50 inmersiones hasta que finalmente sufrió un accidente.
Dado el éxito, Monturiol solicitó por carta apoyo del público para financiar su segundo submarino. En 1862 se empezó a construir este nuevo submarino, más seguro, productivo y el doble de grande. Un proyecto que dos años más tarde se materializó con la creación de la sociedad La Navegación Submarina.
El entusiasmo popular y la prensa presionaron para que el gobierno de Isabel II prometiera ayudas oficiales al invento, pero finalmente nunca llegaron. Monturiol dedicó también tiempo a un tratado sobre los submarinos de guerra, aunque sus desarrollos estaban dedicados más al rescate de marineros y la exploración submarina. Hubo más de 20 inmersiones exitosas durante tres años y se llegaron a hacer pruebas de tiro con un cañón giratorio, pero la poca capacidad de negocio de Monturiol y el escaso interés de la Armada Española acabaron con el invento.
En 1885, Monturiol murió pobre e ignorado. “Ensayo sobre el arte de navegar por debajo del agua” se publicó ya en 1891, seis años después de su muerte. “Aquí yace don Narciso Monturiol, inventor del Ictíneo, primer buque submarino, que navegó por el fondo del mar en aguas de Barcelona y Alicante en 1859, 1860, 1861 y 1862” se escribió en su lápida de Barcelona. Una descripción sin aspavientos que muestra la dificultad de reconocer a los pioneros de cada época.
La técnica detrás del submarino
¿Cómo era el Ictíneo II? Estamos ante un vehículo capaz de sumergirse bajo el agua y con una velocidad limitada, pero donde por primera vez se utilizó un motor de combustión para impulsarse, al contrario que los submarinos de la época que aprovechaban el músculo humano para generar el movimiento.
El nuevo submarino medía 17 metros de eslora, 3 metros de manga y 3,5 metros de la quilla a la cúpula. El Ictíneo II estaba preparado para albergar a 20 tripulantes, aunque 16 de ellos se encargaban de la propulsión. El 2 de octubre de 1864 fue botado en el puerto de Barcelona, y el 20 de mayo de 1865 realizó su primera inmersión, en la que descendió hasta 27,5 metros de profundidad. La distancia prevista para poder transportar a los buzos hasta el coral.
El submarino de Monturiol logró permanecer bajo el agua unas 8 horas y hasta 50 metros de profundidad, aunque teóricamente estaba diseñado para llegar a los 500 metros. El casco del Ictíneo II era doble y estaba construido en madera de olivo con refuerzos de roble y una capa de cobre para resistir la presión. También disponía de un sistema de tanques, válvulas y un peso móvil que servía para controlar los ascensos y descensos.
Pero esta versión del Ictíneo II necesitaba demasiado personal para moverse y Monturiol no estaba satisfecho con la velocidad. Y es que inicialmente el Ictíneo II no disponía de su motor a vapor. El objetivo era alcanzar los 2,5 nudos para atravesar las corrientes en contra. Y para intentar lograrlo se añadió, tres años más tarde, un motor a vapor, una idea que convertiría así al Ictíneo II en un submarino pionero y totalmente adelantado a su época.
Para incorporar el motor a vapor Monturiol acudió al ingeniero industrial Josep Pascual Deop. Junto a él idearon un motor basado en una mezcla de zinc, dióxido de manganeso y clorato de potasio, una combinación para generar una fuente caliente que sirvió para calentar el agua de un horno y generar así energía para la reacción de propulsión.
Esa reacción también servía para generar oxígeno suficiente para dos hombres, una cantidad inferior a la que necesitaba la tripulación. Precisamente este punto de generar oxígeno fue una de las grandes ventajas del Ictíneo II, una idea que permitió no tener que emerger a la superficie para generar aire respirable.
El motor en superficie funcionaba quemando carbón con un sistema de 2 pistones y una potencia de 8CV, mientras que el motor de vapor tenía una potencia de 2 CV y se basaba en un único pistón.
Adicionalmente, Monturiol llegó a diseñar un sistema con un cañón a bordo. Sin embargo, la fuerza del cañón era demasiado grande y comprobó que causaba graves daños estructurales. Un intento de convencer a las autoridades militares que no terminó de funcionar y desvió la atención del gran invento de Monturiol, la utilización del motor a vapor para mover el submarino y de paso ayudar a la inmersión.
El legado de Monturiol sigue presente en Barcelona. En 2013, la empresa catalana Ictineu Submarins terminó, tras una década de desarrollo, el Ictineu 3, un sumergible tripulado para tres personas capaz de descender hasta 1.200 metros y financiado en parte con donaciones y micromecenazgo, como siglo y medio antes había hecho su inventor con el Ictíneo II. En febrero de 2023, el Museu Marítim de Barcelona desmontó la réplica del Ictíneo I que presidía su jardín por su mal estado, con la intención de construir una nueva.

articles.title: After AMD's gaming revenue crashes 40%, CEO Lisa Su declares "We are a data center-first company"
articles.text:
A hot potato: Rest in peace, dedicated consumer GPU makers. With Nvidia having long been an AI firm with a passing interest in making prohibitively expensive consumer graphics cards, AMD's boss has confirmed that Team Red now considers itself a "data center-first" company. With the data center segment making up about 63% of AMD's record third-quarter 2026 revenue, it's easy to see why CEOs are moving away from PC gaming to follow the money.
Su made her remarks in an interview with Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi, where she presented data centers as central to AMD's identity and growth.
"We are a data center first company, that is our profile and you know, people need more computing to power all these applications," Su said.
In a perfect illustration of the state of the current industry, AMD's Instinct accelerators and Epyc server processors pushed the company's Q3 revenue to a record $13.4 billion, up 97% from a year earlier. Meanwhile, its gaming revenue crashed 40% from a year ago to $773 million, mostly due to AI data centers gobbling up all the memory and other components, hiking the price of graphics cards.
It's all great news for Su, of course. She said that AMD's data center business was going to grow 50% sequentially from Q3 to Q4. "We're looking to double the business, more than double the business as we go into next year," she explained.
Su also addressed the increasing demand for AI hardware from industry giants. "We're a tech company that has a lot of resources and the ability to expand our supply and expand our ability to help our customers," the CEO said. "I want to be the best partner to the largest users of compute in the world."
While there has been plenty of nervousness around the massive spending on AI infrastructure recently, Su said the market can be "a little bit short-sighted" when judging AI spending. Her argument is that companies should invest now to meet demand several years ahead, even if investors question the immediate financial impact.
Su added that AMD is always investing for the long term, which she describes as roughly three to five years ahead. That doesn't sound promising for gaming fans hoping things will change anytime soon.
Rival Nvidia, of course, has gone even further down the AI-first route. In its latest reported quarter (Q2 FY2027), $89.02 billion, or 92.5%, of its revenue came from its data center business. Team Green doesn't even report gaming separately anymore, placing it instead within the broader Edge computing category that brought in $7.5 billion, or 7.5% of its overall revenue.

articles.title: Why the UK is becoming a base for African tech companies
articles.text:
In March 2026, the United Kingdom government published a list of Nigerian companies expanding operations in the UK, including fintechs Moniepoint, Kuda and LemFi. Their expansion reflects a growing interest among African tech companies in the UK as a base for building and growing their businesses.
A November 2026 report by TLP Advisory, a cross-border venture law firm, examined 100 technology companies across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Ghana and Morocco that have documented affiliations in the UK, the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The US was the most common destination, with 67% of the companies affiliated there. The UK followed at 32%, while 23% were connected to the UAE.
The figures suggest that the three destinations serve different purposes in the international structures of African tech companies. According to the report, the US is the most common destination for incorporation because of its familiar corporate structures, particularly Delaware-incorporated companies, which make companies easier to invest in. 81% of US-connected companies in TLP’s sample had no other recorded link to the country beyond incorporation.
Meanwhile, the UAE is more associated with companies establishing operational bases, as only 13% had incorporation as their sole link. The report shows that the UK sits between the two, combining company registration with operational expansion and regulatory licensing, as 84% of UK-connected companies were incorporated there, 47% maintained an operational presence, and 19% held regulatory licences. By comparison, only 3% of US-connected companies and 4% of UAE-connected companies in the sample held regulatory licences.
According to the report, Nigerian companies account for roughly two-thirds of the identified UK regulatory licensing connections, most of which are financial services businesses. Understanding why African companies are building regulated businesses in the UK requires examining the capital and regulatory access they seek.
Pressure at home
TLP’s earlier research found that over 76% of funded Nigerian startups surveyed had raised capital in US dollars. Between September 2023 and September 2024, the naira dropped by 71.19%, while inflation rose to nearly 33.9% in October 2024. A Nigerian fintech raising money in dollars but earning revenue in dollars faces a currency mismatch, as depreciation makes dollar obligations more expensive to manage.
Another reason the UK appeals to African fintechs is its established communities with commercial and financial ties to the continent. The 2021 UK Census recorded over 270,000 Nigeria-born residents in England and Wales. Nigeria also received about $22.8 billion in personal remittances from the diaspora in 2025. Businesses with links to Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa can draw on similar diaspora and commercial connections. This provides an opportunity for remittance companies to begin operations by serving people who regularly send money home.
These existing financial relationships can provide an initial customer base for remittance or payment companies. A UK presence could allow the company to build for customers on both sides of the corridor, although to reach these users at scale, it may still need to establish partnerships and secure regulatory approval, making this another consideration for companies expanding into the UK.
The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) in the UK oversees a range of financial services activities through a national regulatory framework. In the US, money transmission is licensed state by state, across 49 states and Washington DC. This means being licensed in one state does not mean they would be licensed in another. In the UAE, payment companies operating on the mainland need authorisation from the Central Bank. Companies operating within financial free zones such as the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) or Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) are regulated separately, and their licences do not automatically allow them to offer payment services across the UAE.
Capital at every stage
The UK is also trying to position itself as a place where African companies can access capital at different stages of their growth. The UK offers tax incentives designed to encourage investment in qualifying early-stage businesses. The Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme (SEIS) and Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) provide tax relief to investors who back qualifying companies. SEIS covers the first £250,000 a company raises, for businesses with fewer than 25 employees and under £350,000 in gross assets. EIS takes over for larger rounds. However, both require a genuine UK operational presence and exclude banking, money-lending and other financial activities.
The government has introduced other initiatives to attract founders and businesses, including the Global Entrepreneur Programme, which supports selected international entrepreneurs in establishing a UK headquarters or research and development presence, and the Innovator Founder visa, which is subject to endorsement and eligibility requirements.
According to TLP Advisory, more than 110 African companies are listed on the London Stock Exchange. Airtel Money’s October 2026 listing provides a recent example of the scale of business that London hopes to attract. The mobile money company began trading on the LSE’s Main Market at a valuation of approximately £5.3 billion.
African technology companies have also looked to US exchanges, with Jumia listing in 2019 and OPay’s planned a $304 million Initial Public Offering in New York before withdrawing it in October 2026 following a regulatory inquiry.
London is trying to make its capital markets more attractive to growing companies by revising its listing rules and introducing the PISCES sandbox in 2025. The Private Intermittent Securities and Capital Exchange System (PISCES) allows investors to buy shares in eligible private companies and existing shareholders to sell theirs at scheduled intervals, without requiring the company to go public. These are part of London’s effort to attract companies at different stages of growth.
The UAE’s free zones and financial centres are designed to attract businesses seeking a base for regional trade and operations. Initiatives such as Abu Dhabi’s Hub71 offer selected startups cash, subject to programme conditions.
The cost of staying
The UK’s growing appeal does not mean every African company with a British entity is building a substantial business there. An operating presence requires customers, employees, licences, local partnerships and sustained spending. Maintaining an overseas entity also brings legal, tax, reporting and compliance costs.
Moniepoint’s UK accounts offer a glimpse of those costs. Its UK subsidiary reported a loss of £1.2 million for 2024, its first year of operation, before generating revenue in the country. The company attributed the spending to setting up the infrastructure, technology and compliance systems needed to enter the market.
The UK offers a combination of diaspora connections, a national financial regulator, access to international capital and a mature services ecosystem for African tech founders. The US remains important for venture financing and corporate structures, while the UAE offers a base for companies pursuing opportunities in the Middle East. Each market plays a different role as the business expands.

articles.title: Sony donne des nouvelles de la PS6, mais un obstacle de taille se profile
articles.text:
L’air de rien, la PS5 est sortie il y a 6 ans, en novembre 2020. Il est donc temps que la nouvelle génération commence à pointer le bout de son nez. Justement, Lin Tao, directrice financière de Sony, est venue apporter quelques informations concernant la prochaine plateforme de Sony dédiée aux jeux vidéo.
Le développement de la PS6 avance « comme prévu »
Sony vient de dévoiler ses résultats financiers. Lors d’une session de questions-réponses, un journaliste a demandé à Lin Tao, directrice financière de Sony, des nouvelles concernant l’avancement du développement de la PlayStation 6. Lin Tao lui a alors répondu que les travaux de recherche et développement « progressent comme prévu », tout en précisant que le développement lui-même « respecte le calendrier prévu ».
Par ailleurs, Lin Tao indique que Sony compte réaliser « les investissements nécessaires » pour développer sa nouvelle plateforme et accomplir « des progrès significatifs » dans sa préparation. À noter que la directrice financière de Sony n’a pas prononcé explicitement le nom PlayStation 6, mais parle de « prochaine plateforme ». Par ailleurs, elle ne donne aucune indication quant à la date de sortie de cette nouvelle plateforme dédiée aux jeux vidéo.
La PS6 ne risque pas d’arriver de sitôt
Autant dire que Sony ne doit pas être pressé de lancer la PlayStation 6, et ce pour plusieurs raisons. Tout d’abord, la console s’est vendue à ce jour à 97,9 millions d’exemplaires à travers le monde. Sony bénéficie donc d’un parc de joueurs plus que conséquent. Même si les ventes de la console ralentissent progressivement en raison de son ancienneté, celles-ci, et plus particulièrement celles de la PS5 Pro, ont récemment connu un regain important à l’approche de la sortie de GTA 6.
Par ailleurs, Sony bénéficie actuellement d’une position dominante sur le marché, les Xbox Series X et S ne s’étant pas vraiment bien vendues. Il faudra voir si Xbox parviendra à remonter la pente avec sa prochaine console, la Xbox Helix. Mais surtout, la crise mondiale de la mémoire vive risque de limiter les marges de manœuvre de Sony. Il est peu probable que l’entreprise japonaise lance une nouvelle console dans un tel contexte de crise. La PlayStation 6 risque déjà d’être chère, mais un lancement dans les deux prochaines années pourrait faire exploser son prix.
Pour rappel, la PS5 est sortie 6 ans et 11 mois après la PS4. Il est fort probable que nous devions patienter un peu plus longtemps cette fois-ci avant de découvrir la nouvelle génération de consoles Sony.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos revela una visión de inteligencia artificial que podría transformar la jornada laboral estadounidense.
articles.text:
Jeff Bezos tiene una visión súper optimista sobre cómo la IA transformará el mercado laboral. Mientras muchas empresas recurren a esta tecnología para automatizar tareas y reducir costes, el fundador de Amazon cree que sus beneficios podrían llegar mucho más lejos, e incluso habla de permitir que algunas personas mantengan económicamente a sus familias trabajando tres días a la semana.
Según sus previsiones, esta posibilidad estaría ligada a un aumento de la productividad. Durante una entrevista concedida a Fox News, Bezos explicó que la inteligencia artificial podría cambiar las necesidades económicas de muchos hogares estadounidenses y, por ejemplo, permitir que algunas familias vivan con un solo sueldo.
Así, su razonamiento se basa en la relación entre producción y esfuerzo de las empresas, ya que podrían conseguir más resultados con menos trabajo y los trabajadores podrían reducir sus jornadas sin perder poder adquisitivo. Por desgracia, Bezos llegó a plantear que contratar personal podría convertirse en un problema si cada vez menos personas necesitaran trabajar tantas horas.
La visión optimista de Bezos contrasta con los despidos de Amazon
Las declaraciones llegan en un momento en el que el impacto de la IA sobre el empleo genera bastante incertidumbre. Durante la entrevista, el periodista Bret Baier recordó que Amazon había eliminado casi 30.000 puestos corporativos desde finales del año anterior, una situación que contrasta con el futuro laboral que describe su fundador.
Bezos respondió que la compañía se encontraba en unas circunstancias particulares al recordar que habían ampliado su plantilla durante la pandemia. Además, aunque el empresario defendió que la inteligencia artificial podría generar aumentos de productividad en la economía global, no explicó cuándo podríamos tener jornadas más cortas o mejores ingresos.
De momento, su propuesta sigue siendo una predicción y no un cambio laboral anunciado por Amazon. La cuestión es si esos avances permitirán realmente trabajar menos o si, por el contrario, servirán para que las empresas produzcan más con menos trabajadores.
