articles.title: EA brings Wing Commander and Ultima to Steam, with cutscenes restored from the original master tapes
articles.text:
In context: Wing Commander III's Mark Hamill cutscenes haven't aged well, mostly because they were squeezed into heavily compressed 240p video back in 1994. EA, as it turns out, still had the original master tapes. This week, a restored version of the game hit Steam for the first time, along with the rest of the Wing Commander series and all eleven Ultima RPGs.
In all, 25 classics from EA's back catalog made their Steam debut. GOG and the EA app carry the same lineup, too. Most of them are straight ports, including the Ultima games, both Crusader titles, and Theme Hospital. Seven, though, are new Anniversary Editions that got real restoration work – six Wing Commander games plus the 1996 PC version of Road Rash.
The Anniversary Editions sell for $9.99 each and the rest for $4.99. Until November 19, though, everything is half off on Steam and GOG. Anyone who already owns a Wing Commander game on GOG or the EA app also gets the Anniversary Edition upgrade for free.
All of this goes back to March 2022, when EA senior producer Jim Vessella came across a storage room at the company's Redwood Shores campus. It held nearly 20,000 archival items, from Betacam, VHS and D1 tapes to film reels. By April of this year, a small team had digitized about 6,000 of them. Among those were the master tapes for Wing Commander and Road Rash.
Privateer 2's cutscenes were the one big gap in the vault, though. As Vessella explains in a lengthy write-up, the game's original cinematics director found the full set of master tapes sitting in his attic.
For Wing Commander III and IV, EA then re-edited more than 1,000 cutscenes frame by frame from those tapes. Players can switch to AI-upscaled versions of each scene or stick with the original 1990s videos. Both games also ship with modder Matt Wells' Enhancement Patch built in. That adds 60 fps gameplay and proper controller support, among other fixes.
Fan-made patches also do the heavy lifting on the first two Wing Commander games. WCAT and Wcdx mainly sort out the speed problems the old code runs into on modern CPUs. Meanwhile, GOG's engineers stitched several older mods together to get Wing Commander Prophecy running smoothly. As for Road Rash, EA relicensed all 14 songs on its soundtrack – Soundgarden included – so the 1996 PC version could get its first-ever digital release.
The Ultima ports also land just months before their creator is set to take back the copyright. Richard Garriott has said he's getting the rights back from EA in 2027. He sold Origin Systems to EA in 1992, and a US copyright rule that lets creators reclaim their work after 35 years kicks in next year. EA would still keep the Ultima trademark, though. Garriott has also said the two sides are in active talks about working on something together.

articles.title: Tesla unveils AI accelerator roadmap, adopts new 'SI' branding in 'Super Intelligence' push — SI6 to bring 80X more compute performance, Dojo 3 headed to space
articles.text:
Tesla unveils AI accelerator roadmap, adopts new 'SI' branding in 'Super Intelligence' push — SI6 to bring 80X more compute performance, Dojo 3 headed to space
Adopts 'Super Intelligence' term for new processors, retrofits it for old ones too.
Tesla has disclosed its revamped AI accelerator roadmap that sheds some light on the future of the company's chip development efforts. The Elon Musk company expects that its 6th Generation inference accelerator will bring 80X more compute performance than the existing 4th Generation chip, whereas its D3 training accelerator will cease to use SRAM-centric architecture in favor of a multi-chiplet design with stacked HBM. Also, Tesla has adopted the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence for its AI accelerators, renaming them with SI monikers. Musk recently confirmed SpaceXAI would be redubbed SpaceXSI for the same reason.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | HW3 \| AI3 | SI4 \| HW4 | SI5 \| AI5 | SI6 \| AI6 | Dojo D1 | Dojo D3 | 
| Application | Inference | Inference | Inference | Inference | Training | Training | 
| Process technology | Samsung 14nm | Samsung 7nm | TSMC 3nm / Samsung 2nm | 2nm-class | TSMC 7nm | TBD | 
| Architecture | Monolithic | Monolithic | MCM | MCM | SoW | Chiplets | 
| Packaging | FCBGA | FCBGA | MCM | MCM | InFO_SoW (training tile) | 2.5D + 3D | 
| Memory type | LPDDR4 | GDDR6 | GDDR6/GDDR7 (?) | GDDR7 (?) | On-chip SRAM | Stacked HBM | 
| Memory capacity | 8 GB | 16 GB | 96 GB | 144 GB | 440 MB SRAM per die 11 GB SRAM per wafer | TBD | 
| Memory bandwidth | ~68 GB/s | ~224 GB/s | TBD | TBD | ~10 TB/s (on-chip) | TBD | 
| Performance vs. SI4 | — | 1X | 40X | 80X | — | — | 
| Estimated compute (TOPS) | 72 TOPS | 216 – 576 | 8,640 – 23,040 | 17,280 – 46,080 | 362 TFLOPS | TBD | 
| Estimated compute (POPS) | 0.072 | 0.216 – 0.576 | 8.64 – 23.04 | 17.28 – 46.08 | 0.362 PFLOPS | TBD | 
| Status | Legacy | Production | Nearing Production | Development | Discontinued | Development | 
Dojo D3: No more wafer-level integration?
Perhaps the most interesting development in Tesla's AI hardware roadmap is the re-emergence of the in-house developed Dojo training accelerator after Elon Musk cancelled the whole wafer-level Dojo project in August, 2025, and then said SpaceX and xAI would exclusively use Nvidia hardware in August, 2026, both in its terrestrial and extraterrestrial data centers. Yet, the 3rd Generation Dojo will be considerably different from the first two generations, Dojo D1 and Dojo D2.
Tesla describes its next-generation Dojo 3 (D3) training accelerator as a chiplet-based design that combines 2.5D and 3D packaging technologies with stacked HBM. This represents a substantial departure from the original Dojo D1 system-on-wafer architecture, which relied on distributed on-chip SRAM and interconnected 25 D1 processors with 11 GB of SRAM using wafer-scale packaging technology. The adoption of HBM suggests that Tesla intends to substantially increase memory capacity, as modern AI models consume extreme amounts of memory to store parameters, activations, and intermediate data, making SRAM unattractive from a capacity standpoint. The use of HBM simplifies memory scaling but introduces different latency, bandwidth, packaging, and power trade-offs. Yet, it remains unclear whether the company has abandoned wafer-scale integration altogether.
On the one hand, it is possible to stack custom HBM modules on top of logic dies interconnected using wafer-scale packaging technology. On the other hand, wafer-level integration is expensive and makes the most sense for select use cases, which include SRAM-centric architectures. Stacking HBM atop wafer-scale interconnected logic dies adds further design complexities, cooling challenges, manufacturing complexity (i.e., potentially reducing yields), long-term reliability concerns, and ultimately costs. While most of the challenges can be resolved by adding redundancy and refining process technologies, this all comes at a cost, making wafer-scaling less likely for D3.
Tesla has yet to disclose D3's compute performance, memory capacity, manufacturing process, or development schedule. At the same time, it claims that its Dojo D3 will be optimized for 'space, training, and scaling,' which means the unit will offer decent performance and will be easy to scale (which again points to a more conventional architecture of accelerators rather than to wafer-scale packaging). More intriguingly, the D3 is also set to be optimized for extraterrestrial deployments, which probably means radiation hardening for at least select SKUs.
SI6: 80X more performance than HW4 in a few years
Another interesting detail in the roadmap is the disclosure of approximate compute performance of Tesla's 6th Generation inference accelerator (SI6): 80X compute improvement over HW4 and 9X more memory over HW4. Depending on how HW4 performance is measured (read on for explanation), we are talking about 17,280 – 46,080 TOPS (trillion operations per second), or 17.28 – 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), though we do not know anything about data formats supported by SI6. Of course, these are estimates, so take them with a grain of salt. To put the numbers into context, Nvidia's Rubin GPU offers 50 NVFP4 PFLOPS for inference, 35 NVFP4 PFLOPS for training, and 17.5 FP8/FP6 PFLOPS. Meanwhile, Rubin is shipping to customers today, whereas SI6 is due in 2029 – 2030. There are some additional details about SI6, which we will discuss below.
Tesla's existing 4th Generation inference processor used in the company's automobiles today (which was originally called HW4, then renamed to AI4, then to SI4) is made by Samsung Foundry using its 7nm-class process technology and relies on conventional flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) packaging (note that the alleged Tesla slide contains a mistake and claims that the unit is made using a 5nm-class node) as well as presumably 16 GB of GDDR6 memory. The company describes the processor as the current benchmark for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology, which makes it the baseline against which performance of future generations is measured. Meanwhile, Tesla does not officially disclose the chip's absolute compute performance numbers, memory capacity, or power consumption, which makes comparison hard. Elon Musk once said that HW4 is 3X – 8X more powerful than HW3, which was officially rated at 72 TOPS, making HW4 a 216 – 576 TOPS ASIC (note that these are estimates).
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
As expected, the slide re-confirms that the upcoming 5th Generation inference accelerator called SI5 (aka HW5 aka AI5) will be manufactured using 3nm- and 2nm-class process technologies at TSMC and Samsung Foundry, respectively, and will adopt a multi-chip module (MCM) design, marking a departure from the conventional packaging approach used for HW4. Tesla expects SI5 to deliver a 40X performance improvement over HW4, which will be a result of an eightfold increase in compute capabilities (driven by considerably denser process technologies and more execution units) and a fivefold gain from silicon optimization, according to Elon Musk, which points to 8,640 – 23,040 TOPS (an estimated figure), depending on how one counts performance of HW4. Meanwhile, the processor is expected to consume from 250W to 800W depending on application, so making performance estimates at this point is not exactly a good business. Meanwhile, the processor will also feature six times more memory than its predecessor (i.e., 96 GB). Depending on the memory type used (GDDR6 or GDDR7), the Tesla SI5 can offer memory bandwidth between 768 GB/s and 1.536 GB/s.
Moving on to the Tesla's 6th Generation inference accelerator (SI6), which is set to further increase compute performance to 80 times that of HW4 and feature eight times more memory than the current-generation processor. This could translate to 17.28 – 46.08 POPS (quadrillion operations per second), depending on how to count HW4 performance, and 144 GB of memory, which is significant performance and amount of memory for an AI accelerator.
Tesla has already inked a deal with Samsung Foundry to make its 6th Generation inference accelerators through 2033, and the new slide reveals that the unit will be made using a 2nm-class process technology. Given the fact that the chip is due in 2029 – 2030 and Samsung's recently updated foundry roadmap, we are probably talking about automotive-grade SF2A, performance-enhanced SF2P, or even SF2Z with backside power delivery. Meanwhile, a thing that strikes the eye with the SI6 is that Tesla does not envision the chip to be produced at Terafab using Intel's 14A fabrication process in the 2030s.
SI6 will retain the multi-chip module (MCM) approach introduced with AI5/SI5/HW5, which seems rational as it will be able to leverage experience it is going to get with its 5th Generation inference accelerator and retain relatively reasonable packaging costs. Many automakers are considering adoption of multi-chiplet designs and HBM memory for their next-generation system-in-packages (SiPs), which will drive their costs. It remains to be seen when Tesla adopts HBM for its inference accelerators, but probably not with SI6.

articles.title: You know the launch market is tough when satellite companies start building rockets
articles.text:
There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are optimistic plans.
AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space. So on Friday, AST announced that it is developing a medium-lift rocket, named Blacklift, which will have the capacity to lift 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Oh, and the company said it would start launching commercially in late 2028.
“The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner’s economics in the industry,” said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release.
To anyone with even a basic understanding of rockets, that timeline is wildly, fantastically, and stupidly optimistic. Still, the announcement is worth examining because it underscores two important trends in today’s launch industry.
First, it’s becoming increasingly apparent that satellite operators planning to deploy large constellations need to secure launch capacity years in advance, as Amazon did nearly half a decade ago. And if they can’t secure that capacity on favorable terms, they are now considering taking the extraordinary step of developing their own rockets.
And secondly, since investors are now recognizing the worsening launch crisis that Ars has been writing about for months, there is apparently capital to be raised for new entrants into the medium-lift launch market. AST is not the only company making fantastical claims of late. A firm called Cowboy Space said in October it was building a large rocket named Big Iron (full credit—that’s an excellent name) to launch orbital data centers. It also claimed its large rocket would make its first flight in 2028.

articles.title: Windows 11 27H2: la gran actualización con la que Microsoft quiere reinventar Windows en 2027
articles.text:
Durante años, la industria tecnológica dio por hecho que el siguiente gran salto de Microsoft sería Windows 12. No obstante, la compañía ha cambiado la trayectoria y decidió enfocarse en mejorar la versión actual del sistema operativo antes de ofrecer una nueva versión. En 2027 el plan seguirá vigente y, según los rumores, Microsoft lanzaría una de las actualizaciones más ambiciosas hasta la fecha.
De acuerdo con The Verge, Windows 11 27H2 será un cambio completo del sistema operativo que mejorará el rendimiento a 64 bits. A diferencia de lo que vimos con las versiones 25H2 y 26H2, que se distribuyeron como parches que habilitaban características previamente integradas al sistema, la nueva actualización sustituirá partes importantes de la base del sistema. Esto le permitiría aplicar cambios más profundos en el desempeño y en la arquitectura interna de Windows.
El reporte menciona que los ingenieros de Microsoft han puesto al rendimiento como uno de los pilares de la actualización. Hace unos días, la tecnológica anunció que Windows 11 ya es más rápido en equipos con 8 GB de RAM en comparación con lo que vimos a inicios de 2026. El secreto está en una serie de optimizaciones a la gestión de memoria, las cuales reducen la necesidad de transferir datos a tu disco duro cuando la RAM se encuentra bajo presión.
Microsoft seguirá mejorando el rendimiento para asegurarse de que la multitarea resulte más fluida, sobre todo en ordenadores con configuraciones modestas. Sumado a esto, Windows 11 27H2 podría incluir soporte para Intel APX, un conjunto de instrucciones que mejoran el desempeño de las aplicaciones de 64 bits. De materializarse, esto último sería una de las novedades más importantes de la actualización, permitiendo ejecutar aplicaciones más rápido en diversos escenarios de uso.
Windows 11 27H2 llegará con diseño actualizado y nuevos fondos de pantalla
Además de los cambios en la base del sistema operativo, Microsoft aprovechará esta versión para renovar una buena parte de la identidad visual de Windows 11. La actualización 27H2 reemplazará el fondo de pantalla Bloom que ha acompañado al sistema desde su lanzamiento por varios diseños. El reporte señala que habrá variantes para los ordenadores de casa y empresariales, así como versiones enfocadas a los gamers, creadores de contenido y más.
Es probable que Microsoft comience a integrar en un solo paquete los cambios que ha desplegado en las versiones Insider desde hace meses. Si hacemos memoria, uno de los planes de la compañía es modernizar el sistema operativo, incluyendo esos cuadros de diálogo que se han mantenido por más de tres décadas sin cambios. Algunos de ellos mantienen el lenguaje de diseño de Windows NT, incluyendo los íconos clásicos que veíamos en las versiones viejas del sistema operativo.
En junio de este año, el director de diseño, March Rogers, confirmó en su cuenta de X que Microsoft está reescribiendo los cuadros de diálogo más antiguos en WinUI 3, el marco de interfaz moderno de Windows 11. Algunas funciones, como el diálogo de copiar archivos, ya se completaron internamente, pero todavía existen otras que utilizan tecnologías heredadas como Win32. Los ingenieros tienen que asegurarse primero de que las versiones de WinUI 3 son tan rápidas como las antiguas.
Fuera de los ajustes del diseño y mejoras en el rendimiento, Microsoft no está lista para dar el siguiente paso y anunciar Windows 12. Primero debe asegurarse de que cuenta con una base sólida y resolver todos los problemas que arrastra la versión actual. Eso sí, Windows 11 27H2 será una actualización importante, casi al nivel de lo que vimos en la versión 24H2.

articles.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
articles.text:
Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company’s models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down.
Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
AI is dramatically speeding up Anthropic’s research, even as the company calls for slowing down AI development.
That’s according to a new report published Thursday by the AI safety research organization METR, following an 11-week investigation inside the company, as part of a report evaluating its AI research and development. The probe is separate from a program offering safety researchers “employee-like” access to systems in the wake of high-profile hacking incidents over the summer.
The findings offer some of the clearest evidence yet of AI accelerating its own development, raising questions about how quickly the technology could advance toward a future in which AI systems can improve themselves with little or no human involvement. They also come at a pivotal time for Anthropic, which is preparing to go public even as its CEO, Dario Amodei, has publicly called for labs to pump the brakes on AI development.
But while the report offers a rare glimpse into the inner workings of the world’s leading AI labs, what it leaves out is just as revealing. Anthropic was permitted to redact portions of the final report as part of its agreement with METR, and it appears to have exercised that power liberally, raising questions about how much the public really knows about the pace — and risks — of frontier AI development.
Here are some of the biggest takeaways.
AI is dramatically accelerating Anthropic’s research and development
One of METR’s most noteworthy findings is that Anthropic’s AI models are improving roughly twice as quickly as they were a year ago, with benchmark scores suggesting “that Anthropic has made roughly two years of historical progress over the last year.” Crucially, METR’s researchers said they “are confident” that the acceleration was not simply due to scaling up the computing power used to train the models, which historically has been a major driver of AI progress.
Instead, the researchers said that the majority of the acceleration as of October “is due to AI,” with its contribution growing over time. That finding was supported by informal Slack polls and interviews with Anthropic employees, which pointed to sizable productivity gains. METR wrote that employees using Anthropic’s most capable internal model on average self-reported being around 12 times as productive at their respective work as they would have been without AI assistance, around double what staff had reported just a few months earlier while using Mythos 5.
For now, much of that acceleration appears to be coming from AI assisting human researchers, rather than AI working independently, though METR warned that “there are some signs that fully autonomous contributions will play a larger role soon.” Notably, the researchers said they found no clear signs of diminishing returns or observable bottlenecks that could prevent “even faster acceleration.”
Three of Anthropic’s newest AI models remain under wraps
Anthropic’s researchers are using more advanced AI models than the rest of us, with a lot of the acceleration and productivity gains described by METR attributable to unreleased internal models.
Over the past six months, Anthropic has finished training three models it has yet to release, according to METR. The pace of development is swift, with the models — codenamed Model 2, Model 3, and Model 4 — completing training in July, August-September, and September-October, respectively. METR also identified an unreleased model dating back to 2022, called Unreleased 2022. “These are the codenames shared with us; we understand they have different internal codenames,” the researchers wrote.
Anthropic is keeping key information secret
Anthropic gave METR access to a host of non-public information, including confidential research, model performance data, and employee interviews as part of the research process. It had no obligation to do so and by METR’s own admission, the AI lab “shared more information than was initially scoped for this project, surpassing our expectations.” This is commendable, but it is worth noting that Anthropic did not grant researchers unrestricted access, nor the kind of “employee-like” access it has promised other METR safety researchers as part of a separate program announced last month. It is an important distinction, given the reputational benefits companies can gain from independent assessments, even when they come with significant restrictions.
And there were significant restrictions. Anthropic had the power to redact information from METR’s final report — and it used that power extensively. “We submitted a ~100-page full report on our assessment to Anthropic. For the public version, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative,” METR wrote on X.
METR reiterated those concerns throughout the report, highlighting other limitations on its access. “Our pipeline of information was relatively narrow, and a small number of our requests for data were denied.”
METR repeatedly stressed the impact Anthropic’s redaction decisions had on its ability to communicate its findings and for others to assess what’s going on at the company. It noted that much of the redacted evidence could have “multiple plausible interpretations,” making it difficult for the public to assess its findings, understand the uncertainties surrounding them, and judge the evidence themselves. “As a consequence [of the redactions], the public has to rely on METR’s judgment much more than would be ideal, given the weight of the questions answered here,” the report said.
In the report, METR said Anthropic justified the redactions on the grounds that releasing the information could benefit its rivals. However, METR said “most of the redacted information was very high-level,” even though it said it was not in position to comment whether redactions were justified commercially or not.
“We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work,” Anthropic cofounder Sam McCandlish acknowledged in a lengthy post on X responding to METR’s findings. “But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster,” he said, adding that doing so would make the risks METR is concerned about “worse.”
McCandlish said that it’s a trade-off, but maintained Anthropic had made the “right call” in deciding to redact the information. He said the company plans to publish its own report on the speed of AI progress “in the coming weeks,” as well as new steps it’s taking to strengthen safety.
Anthropic is accelerating the very technology it warns is dangerous and faster than many expected
The publication of METR’s report has provoked a fierce backlash among AI safety researchers and commentators, largely centered on an apparent contradiction at the heart of Anthropic’s approach to AI: The company has been one of the most outspoken advocates for safety and responsible development, yet the report suggests it is helping accelerate the technology toward a threshold many consider dangerous, while seemingly failing to live up to its own commitments to transparency and accountability.
For some, the findings suggest that even many of the field’s most aggressive predictions about AI progress may be too conservative. They indicate that recursive self-improvement — AI systems that can autonomously develop increasingly powerful successor systems without human intervention, potentially accelerating development dramatically — may be closer than previously thought, raising concerns about whether existing safety measures can keep pace. While METR’s report only covers Anthropic, OpenAI said in September that it is “making strong progress” toward building an AI researcher that can “further progress on deep learning and alignment” by March 2028.
The report provides evidence about just how quickly AI is accelerating its own development
Marius Hobbhahn, CEO and founder of Apollo Research, which conducts AI safety testing for several leading AI labs, told The Verge the report suggests a pace of AI-enabled research and development even faster than what was forecast in AI 2027, an influential scenario that envisions a key breakthrough toward self-improvement in early 2027. He said the report has attracted so much attention because it provides evidence about something that has been very hard to pin down: Just how quickly AI is accelerating its own development.
Hobbhahn said the findings were broadly in line with what many in the field had expected, perhaps a little faster. Alan Chan, a senior research fellow at tech policy research center GovAI, told The Verge that the findings should prompt skeptics to reconsider their stance on AI accelerating AI development, and possibly shorten their timelines to when we will have systems that can fully automate tasks like software engineering.
On X, other researchers commented on the rate of acceleration and its implications for AI development. Sydney Von Arx, founder and CEO of AI safety organization The Nightingale Collective and a former METR researcher, also compared the findings to AI 2027’s timeline. Ryan Greenblatt, a METR researcher formerly of AI safety organization Redwood Research and one of three external researchers permitted to investigate OpenAI’s hack of Hugging Face, said he “was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026.”
Frustration is mounting over Anthropic’s approach to safety
Beyond highlighting the speed of AI development, the report has also fueled a growing sense of frustration over Anthropic’s role in driving that progress. The company has been one of the most vocal proponents of responsible AI development — and no stranger to calling for others to slow down — yet appears to be racing ahead itself. This report only builds on already heightened tensions from its IPO prospectus and future plans released last month.
Anthropic’s decision to heavily redact the report, citing grounds that revealing more could help its rivals accelerate their own development, has fueled accusations of hypocrisy. Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI researcher who now runs the AI Futures Project, which published AI 2027, accused Anthropic of “recklessly gambling with our lives,” adding that “it is pretty rich” of the company to cite others going faster as a reason to redact information when it does “not appear to be slowing down much at all.”
Anthropic declined to answer The Verge’s questions about the report and ensuing criticism, instead directing us to McCandlish’s post.
The redactions have also renewed calls for greater transparency and independent oversight of frontier AI labs, which grew to new heights earlier this year following a spate of incidents involving rogue AI agents. Brianna Rosen, research director for frontier security at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, told The Verge that it was concerning that companies, not governments, were effectively calling the shots on automating AI research. “For democratic oversight to work, independent evaluators need the freedom to explain why they reached their conclusions, governments need to assess the evidence themselves, and the public has to trust this process,” Rosen said. “The report was not sufficiently transparent about the evidence.”
Pressure is building for more transparency from AI labs
Hobbhahn echoed Rosen’s concerns, saying that much of the reaction to the report stems from the apparent gap between Anthropic’s public safety stance and its actions. He pointed to the company’s decision to cancel part of the assessment designed to evaluate how much compute it allocates to safety work versus improving capabilities. METR said the company said “this was due to wanting to keep the engagement focused on risk assessment for the time being, and that it would revisit compute allocation verification later on.”
For Hobbhahn, the episode underscores the need for independent safety researchers to be embedded more deeply within AI labs, with significant access to internal systems and evidence. While his organization stands to benefit from such arrangements — Apollo is taking steps toward becoming an embedded evaluator at frontier labs — he is far from alone in calling for stronger oversight of AI development.
Others have called for more direct action. In a direct response to the report, New York state Assemblyman Alex Bores, a key figure shaping the Democrats’ AI agenda, called on Congress to “ban RSI, this year if possible.” With the blue wave of Democrats — many of whom campaigned against AI companies — taking office soon, the prospect of tougher restrictions is a very real possibility.
And with AI research showing little sign of slowing down, the pressure is set to intensify. Hobbhahn said he had another takeaway from the report, too: “Brace for craziness,” he said. “It is going to go very fast,” likely way too fast for society or politics to keep up.

articles.title: Chainalysis admits all users affected in major data breach — names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens all exposed
articles.text:
Chainalysis admits all users affected in major data breach — names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens all exposed
Chainalysis shut down multiple services to contain the attack
- Chainalysis disclosed a cyberattack that exposed customer data, including hashed passwords and account information
- Company took key services offline, forced password resets, and required additional security measures
- Investigation continues as Chainalysis restores systems and assesses the full impact of the breach
Blockchain data analysis platform Chainalysis has disclosed suffering a disruptive cyberattack that forced it to shut down some of its services to prevent further damage, as sensitive data from all of its customers - including hashed passwords - were stolen.
On October 30 2026, the company issued a notification saying it was a target of an attack, “similar to many other tech platforms in recent weeks,” but “unrelated to the recent crypto theft involving Binance.”
At first, it did not look like a particularly dangerous hit - the initial investigation did not find evidence of unauthorized access to investigation content, authentication credentials, or session tokens.
On-path attack
The unnamed attackers used “offensive agentic techniques”, Chainalysis said, but believed at the time that investigation content (such as graphs, notes, or cases), transaction or query results, passwords in clear text, MFA secrets, or user session tokens were not compromised.
It did confirm non-sensitive data (user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on the platform) as accessed.
On November 4, Chainalysis shared an update, confirming that this was a much bigger hit than initially believed.
“Today, we confirmed that as a part of this incident, an “on-path attack” exposed a subset of customer passwords, including yours,” the company said in an email sent to affected parties. “This attack vector has been contained and remediated.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Given this sensitive and urgent information, we are requiring you to reset your password.”
Users were locked out of their accounts and were forced to reset them using the standard Chainalysis login page. At roughly the same time, it also took down three products, Reactor, Data Solutions and Chain (Beta) “out of an abundance of caution”, and KYT (the user interface and API), other address screening products and the login page “due to abnormal activity.”
The company said it will require additional protections to access accounts, including having every user reset their passwords and rotate API keys as appropriate.
Chainalysis has now said it started restoring access to KYT and Address Screening, albeit partially, and that customers should expect to regain access “over the next several hours”, because it was “proceeding carefully” and monitoring each phase. Users looking to regain their access as soon as possible are invited to submit their trusted IP address via email and prepare to reset their credentials.
No word from the perpetrators (yet)
The company said it was still working “around the clock” to harden its systems and restore access to Reactor and Data Solutions. “We recognize the disruption this incident has caused and appreciate your continued patience and partnership as we work to restore our services safely,” Chainalysis said.
Chainalysis is a blockchain analytics company that governments, law enforcement agencies, and other businesses use to track and investigate cryptocurrency transactions.
Using its tools, the police were able to trace stolen funds, identify illicit activity, and investigate numerous cryptocurrency-related crimes. It is considered a rather important organization in the crypto cybersecurity chain because it provides much of the intelligence infrastructure that helps authorities and businesses understand who is moving crypto and where.
At this moment, we don’t know if this will result in an extortion attempt. No threat actors have claimed responsibility for this attack, and the data has not yet emerged anywhere on the dark web. Chainalysis has not mentioned being reached out by the attackers or even trying to get in touch with anyone.

articles.title: SA-founded Water Ledger Global secures investment from Launch Africa - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African-founded water data startup Water Ledger Global (WLG) has secured a strategic investment from Launch Africa to scale its shared trust infrastructure for water globally.
Founded in October 2024 by a South African team, with roots in Australia going back to 2016, WLG is the company behind Water Ledger, a platform that creates a single, trusted record of how much water there is, who is using it, and what it is worth.
By breaking down data silos, it gives regulators, utilities, investors and lenders a shared source of truth, with the aim of turning water into a transparent, investable asset class. The startup has subsidiaries in South Africa, Australia and the United States, and its technology is already live. Its SWaN solution for mitigation and nutrient markets operates in Virginia, while its water accounting and trading solution is used by Seqwater in Australia.
The new funding will help WLG take its platform to more utilities, regulators, water users and markets.
“Capital follows confidence. In a very short time we have taken a bold idea and turned it into real solutions to real water challenges,” said Fred Platt, CEO of Water Ledger Global. “We are not just building technology; we are building the trust backbone for water.”
Uwem Uwemakpan, head of investments at Launch Africa, said the platform addresses a real need as the push for transparency and more funding into local utilities grows.
“We backed the team because that record is what gives investors and lenders the confidence to put capital into water infrastructure,” he said.

articles.title: Foto-Backup am PC: Von dieser neuen Funktion profitieren alle Android-Smartphones
articles.text:
Android-Update: Dein Smartphone sichert Fotos und Videos jetzt vollautomatisch auf deinem Windows-PC
Google verteilt seit dem 2. November das aktuelle Update für seine Play-Systemdienste. Darin stecken unter anderem Neuerungen bei der Geräteverbindung, der Kontoverwaltung und der Sicherheit. Anders als bei klassischen Android-Updates und Sicherheitspatches muss Google nicht auf die Gerätehersteller warten: Die Verbesserungen landen also sofort bei dir. Google spielt die Aktualisierungen direkt auf alle Android-Geräte mit Play-Diensten aus – das sind die meisten. Profitieren können davon nicht nur Smartphones, sondern auch Tablets, Smartwatches, Smart-TVs, Fahrzeuge mit Android Auto und Chromebooks.
Fotos automatisch auf den Windows-PC sichern
Mit Version 26.43 der Google-Play-Dienste können Windows-Nutzer:innen Fotos und Videos automatisch sichern lassen. Dafür kommt Quick Share zum Einsatz, Googles Funktion zum drahtlosen Teilen von Dateien zwischen Geräten. Details zur genauen Funktionsweise nennt Google in seinen Release-Notizen nicht. Es kommen aber „qualitativ bessere Protokolle zur Geräteverbindung“ zum Einsatz.
Wer sogenannte Familienkonten nutzt, findet die Verwaltung künftig gebündelt: In den Systemeinstellungen steht direkt unter den Google-Einstellungen der neue Punkt „Familie“. Dort zeigt Google eine Übersicht der Familienmitglieder, einen eventuell abonnierten Google-One-Tarif samt Speicherverbrauch sowie die geteilten Dienste an.
Mehr Kontrolle im Passwort-Manager
Neu ist auch eine Option im Google-Passwort-Manager. Beim Importieren lässt sich jetzt manuell auswählen, welche Zugangsdaten bei widersprüchlichen Passwörtern und Passkeys erhalten bleiben. Passkeys sind Anmeldedaten, die Passwörter ersetzen und zum Beispiel per Fingerabdruck freigegeben werden. Zudem hat Google die Systemverwaltungsdienste aktualisiert. Die neue Version soll laut Google „die Akkulaufzeit, die Gerätekonnektivität, die Geräteleistung, den Datenschutz, die Sicherheit, die Stabilität und die Aktualisierbarkeit verbessern“.
Hinzu kommen Funktionen für Google und externe App-Entwickler:innen, die standort- und kontextbezogene Abläufe in ihren Apps unterstützen. Außerdem behebt Google Fehler bei sicherheits- und notfallbezogenen Diensten, aktualisiert die Kundenkarten in Google Wallet und bessert dort weitere Bugs aus. Google verteilt die Updates in der Regel schubweise. Auf einem Redaktionsgerät war zum Zeitpunkt der Veröffentlichung des Artikels bereits die neue Version der Play-Systemdienste installiert, der Play-Store selbst lief dagegen noch in einer älteren Fassung.

articles.title: El Niño record : 2027 a 96 % de chances de battre tous les records de chaleur
articles.text:
Depuis le printemps 2026, les climatologues ont les yeux rivés sur le Pacifique tropical, où El Niño, la phase chaude d’un va-et-vient naturel entre l’océan et l’atmosphère, monte en puissance plus vite que prévu. En octobre, les satellites de la Nasa y relevaient déjà les signes d’un épisode « potentiellement historique ». Ce mardi 3 novembre, le site britannique Carbon Brief a chiffré ce que cet épisode risque de coûter à la planète : 2027 finirait autour de +1,74 °C au-dessus de la moyenne 1850-1900, qui sert de référence préindustrielle. Ce qui signifie que l’année qui arrive dépasserait de plus de 0,2 °C le record actuel, détenu par 2024.
Carbon Brief est un média spécialisé dans la science et les politiques climatiques, et l’analyse est signée Zeke Hausfather, climatologue chez Berkeley Earth, l’un des groupes qui calculent la température mondiale. Sa méthode fait la moyenne de six grandes séries de températures (Nasa, NOAA, Met Office britannique, Berkeley Earth, Copernicus et l’agence météo japonaise), puis applique un modèle statistique qui relie la force d’El Niño à la température des mois suivants.
Or l’épisode actuel est hors norme. En septembre, la température de surface dans la zone Niño3.4 du Pacifique, l’indicateur de référence, a battu le record de novembre 2015. En moyenne, 656 prévisions issues de 14 modèles le voient culminer vers +4 °C en décembre, plus d’un degré au-dessus de l’ancien record. De son côté, l’OMM estime qu’El Niño devrait se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027.
Pourquoi +1,74 °C est un chiffre important
Mais pourquoi parler de 2027 alors qu’El Niño culmine fin 2026 ? Parce que la température mondiale réagit avec environ trois mois de retard sur le Pacifique tropical : la chaleur libérée par l’océan cet hiver pèsera sur l’atmosphère l’an prochain, comme 2016 avait hérité de l’épisode de 2015. Le chiffre de +1,74 °C est une médiane, c’est-à-dire la valeur centrale d’une fourchette qui va de +1,54 °C à +1,95 °C dans 90 % des cas. Même le bas de cette fourchette dépasserait les +1,52 °C de 2024.
Carbon Brief prévoit un bond d’environ 0,2 °C entre 2026 et 2027, plus fort qu’après n’importe quel El Niño passé. Ce bond reste une projection fragile, et Zeke Hausfather le reconnaît lui-même. Son modèle a été entraîné sur des épisodes moins violents, et rien ne garantit que la relation observée jusqu’ici tienne pour un El Niño de cette taille.
El Niño, un accélérateur posé sur un climat déjà chaud
Serge Zaka, docteur en agrométéorologie, alerte sur ce scénario depuis des mois. Dès avril, il décrivait sur X El Niño comme « un accélérateur ponctuel de chaleur à l’échelle mondiale », qui ajoute « une couche de chaleur exceptionnelle sur un climat déjà fortement réchauffé ». Ce vendredi 6 novembre, il a été plus direct : « Ce qui se profile pour 2027 est… bah on est dans la merde quoi, je vais faire simple ». Il relevait au passage que la planète venait d’enregistrer ses deux plus fortes anomalies thermiques, dans l’atmosphère comme à la surface des océans.
El Niño est-il lui-même dopé par le changement climatique ? Rien ne permet de l’affirmer à ce stade. Dans son dernier rapport, publié en 2021, le GIEC constate que les épisodes sont plus amples depuis 1950 qu’avant l’ère industrielle, mais n’accorde qu’un faible degré de confiance à l’idée que les activités humaines en soient la cause, car les modèles produisent ces variations sans aucune émission.
Par contre, les émissions humaines expliquent la quasi-totalité du réchauffement de long terme, et les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre ont atteint des niveaux record en 2025, selon l’OMM. El Niño s’ajoute à ce socle pendant un an ou deux, puis s’efface sans faire redescendre la tendance de fond.

articles.title: WhatsApp prépare une fonction IA bien pratique pour vos photos, et certains iPhone en profitent déjà
articles.text:
WhatsApp commence à proposer sur iPhone une option d’IA pour étendre une photo au-delà de son cadre d’origine. Elle s’active depuis l’éditeur d’images de l’application et reste, pour l’instant, réservée à une poignée d’utilisateurs.
Le principe, popularisé par Photoshop et plusieurs chatbots, consiste à laisser l’IA inventer ce qui se trouve hors champ. Pour obtenir ce « dézoom » artificiel, les utilisateurs de WhatsApp n’ont désormais plus besoin de quitter la messagerie, ce qui banalise un peu plus l’outil de retouche générative.
Un outil de retouche généré par Meta AI, déjà visible chez certains utilisateurs
Selon 9to5Mac, le déploiement concerne d’abord les testeurs du programme bêta via TestFlight. Quelques utilisateurs de la version publique sur iOS y auraient déjà accès. L’extension d’image est confiée à Meta AI, et non à l’IA d’Apple.
Le parcours est simple : on sélectionne une photo dans une conversation, WhatsApp ouvre l’éditeur de dessin, où figurent plusieurs effets d’IA. Une nouvelle option permet d’étendre l’image. Meta AI met quelques secondes à analyser le cliché et à générer la version élargie, affichée dans l’éditeur avant l’envoi. La fonction est aussi compatible avec les statuts.
Le résultat d’une extension générative est par nature imprévisible, puisque l’IA fabrique des pixels qui n’ont jamais existé. WhatsApp prévoit donc un bouton d’annulation qui restaure l’image d’origine. On peut ensuite relancer l’outil pour obtenir une autre proposition.
Reste un point à garder en tête : ce qui s’affiche au-delà des bords est une reconstitution plausible, pas une réalité photographiée. Envoyer à ses proches un cliché élargi par IA n’a rien de dramatique, mais la frontière entre souvenir et image recomposée devient plus floue.
Apple proposait déjà Extend, mais pas à tout le monde
Les iPhone compatibles avec Apple Intelligence disposent d’un outil natif baptisé Extend, qui permet de pincer ou de faire glisser l’image pour l’agrandir. L’intérêt de la version WhatsApp est donc surtout pratique : elle évite un détour par la galerie et ne dépend pas, a priori, de la compatibilité Apple Intelligence, même si les sources ne le précisent pas explicitement.
Aucune date de généralisation n’est communiquée, comme souvent pour les fonctions bêta de WhatsApp. La fonction a toutefois déjà été déployée sur la bêta Android, et certains utilisateurs de la version publique iOS la voient déjà : un élargissement ne devrait pas tarder, sans garantie.
Après le fond d’écran de profil généré par IA, WhatsApp poursuit méthodiquement l’installation de Meta AI dans chaque recoin de l’application. Reste à savoir si les utilisateurs y verront un vrai gain ou un gadget de plus.
- Chiffrement de bout en bout.
- Appels audio et vidéo gratuits.
- Compatibilité multiplateforme.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 6, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 6, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Friday, November 06, 2026.
From Deepinder Goyal defending wearable device Temple to xxx raising Rs 400 crore, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured news
How Satin Group’s Sankalp plans to empower Indian founders
Satin Group launched Sankalp this September, a platform designed to nurture sustainability-focused ideas from students and early-stage entrepreneurs. In an exclusive interaction with YourStory, Pramod Marar, CEO of Satin FinServ Limited, discussed the thinking behind the initiative, the importance of non-financial support alongside funding, and the role financial institutions can play in scaling climate innovation.
Sankalp operates through two distinct tracks: student-led business ideas and early-stage startups. The student track encourages college students to develop technology-driven solutions to climate and environmental challenges. The startup track focuses on young businesses working in areas such as clean mobility, circular economy, waste management, and sustainable supply chains. Sankalp winners stand a chance to win Rs 32 lakh, with Rs 10 lakh for students and Rs 22 lakh for startups.
Latest news
Deepinder Goyal hits back at doctors
Deepinder Goyal took to X on Thursday to counter Indian doctors who criticised his brain-monitoring wearable Temple. Defending the science behind the device, he said, “First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren't true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple.”
He also said the device features a 14-day no-question return policy. “If the product doesn't work, it fails out of the gate and the company dies before recovering a tenth of its R&D," he said.
In the post, Goyal also highlighted that $30 million was invested in building the device, of which he put in $20 million of his personal money.
Funding news
Northern Arc hits first close at over Rs 400 crore
Northern Arc Investment Managers, the asset management arm of Northern Arc Capital, has marked the first close of its Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund with commitments of more than Rs 400 crore from institutions, family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and high-net-worth individuals (HNIs).
The fund is the firm's 15th private credit vehicle. It is a sector-agnostic Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) focused on performing private credit, rated AA (SO) by CareEdge Ratings. It targets a corpus of Rs 1,500 crore, with a greenshoe option of Rs 500 crore that could take it to Rs 2,000 crore. The fund has a five-year tenure and targets a 16% XIRR.
Fitness and sports technology startup OBSESS raises angel funding
Delhi NCR-based fitness and sports technology company OBSESS has raised angel funding to build a unified digital ecosystem for India’s fitness and sports industry. The round saw participation from Angel Investors including Pushpendra Singh, Co-founder of Centricity; Amitt Goel, Angel Investor; and Harshit Vij, Co-founder of Freecultr.
Founded in 2026 by Tushar Sharma and Yash Kumar, OBSESS brings different parts of the fitness journey together through a single connected platform.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: Veeam warns of Software Appliance boot failures on AMD EPYC hosts
articles.text:
Veeam warned customers about boot failures affecting Software Appliance virtual machines (VMs) on hosts with AMD EPYC processors.
The company's Software Appliance VMs are pre-configured, Linux-based virtual machines that let admins run the Veeam Backup & Replication backup software suite on Linux devices without manually installing dependencies or configuring the software.
To comply with corporate and government security frameworks, the underlying Linux kernel runs integrated health and cryptographic checks (such as jitterentropy health tests) in FIPS mode during early boot.
However, as the company explained in a Wednesday advisory, these VMs will fail to boot and will crash with a kernel panic after failing an early-boot FIPS-mode jitterentropy check on some AMD EPYC processors.
"A Veeam Software Appliance (Linux-based Veeam Backup & Replication) virtual machine running on a host with an AMD EPYC processor intermittently fails to boot after a reboot, including a reboot that follows an update that installs a new kernel," it said.
"This issue occurs because the Linux kernel used by the Veeam Software Appliance runs a jitterentropy health test in FIPS mode during early boot, and the test intermittently fails on certain AMD EPYC processors, including AMD EPYC 7262, 7302, and 7F72. When the test fails, the kernel stops the boot process with a kernel panic."
This known issue originates in the Linux kernel version used by the Veeam Software Appliance and affects Veeam Software Appliance version 13.1 and later.
According to Veeam, users are seeing "Kernel panic - not syncing: jitterentropy: Initialization failed with host not compliant with requirements: 9" kernel panic errors on impacted systems.
Mitigation available
To mitigate this issue, Veeam told IT administrators to redeploy the appliance to a Linux host with a different processor.
If the appliance cannot be redeployed on a system with an unaffected processor, IT admins are advised to disable automatic updates for the appliance and install updates manually (while monitoring the VM as it reboots).
"If the kernel panic occurs, power off the virtual machine and power it on again. A restart of the guest operating system does not recover the virtual machine," Veeam added. "After the appliance has booted successfully, no further errors are expected, and the operation of Veeam Backup & Replication is not affected."
Earlier today, Veeam also said that some of its products are affected by a critical Linux kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432) in the IPv4 TCP networking code that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners.
The company has fixed the CVE-2026-98432 flaw for some impacted Veeam components and is now pushing the patched kernel to affected systems either as a private fix or through the Veeam Updater.
Veeam's products are used by more than 550,000 customers, including 74% of Global 2,000 firms and 82% of Fortune 500 companies.

articles.title: Toyota quiere ir más allá de los coches. La respuesta a su próxima gran apuesta está en sus propias fábricas
articles.text:
Toyota es uno de los grandes nombres de la industria del automóvil, pero su historia no se explica únicamente por los vehículos que fabrica. La compañía japonesa lleva décadas perfeccionando la manera de producirlos, con sistemas de trabajo que han influido en fábricas de todo el mundo. Hablamos de procesos donde la automatización, la coordinación entre personas y máquinas y la mejora continua tienen un papel fundamental. Lo interesante es que buena parte de ese conocimiento no sirve exclusivamente para fabricar coches: también puede aplicarse a otros procesos industriales y a tecnologías que van más allá del transporte.
Ese bagaje ayuda a entender el siguiente movimiento de la compañía. Toyota anunció el 5 de noviembre de 2026 la creación de Toyota Robotics, una nueva organización interna que comenzará a funcionar el 1 de enero de 2027 bajo la supervisión directa de Toyota Motor Corporation. Al frente estará Takefumi Shiga, responsable de producción del fabricante, que sumará esta tarea a sus funciones actuales. Su misión será reunir los conocimientos, profesionales y recursos relacionados con la robótica que hasta ahora estaban repartidos por distintos departamentos, con el objetivo de acelerar su aplicación práctica, comercialización y despliegue.
La nueva división forma parte de una reorganización más amplia que también incluye un grupo de filosofía y formación dirigido por Akio Toyoda, presidente del consejo de administración, para transmitir los conocimientos industriales de la compañía a las próximas generaciones.
De fabricar coches con robots a convertir la robótica en un negocio
Para entender cómo pretende llevarlo a cabo, tenemos que mirar hacia sus propias instalaciones. Según explicó Toyota en su presentación de resultados del 5 de noviembre, cuenta con 60 plantas y unos 18.000 trabajadores especializados en distintos oficios cuyos conocimientos pueden contribuir al desarrollo de nuevas soluciones robóticas. La propuesta consiste en aprovechar los datos y la experiencia acumulados en estos entornos para perfeccionar las máquinas e incluso enseñarles habilidades de los propios trabajadores. La compañía también quiere trasladar a la robótica conocimientos de tecnologías ya desarrolladas para sus vehículos, como su plataforma de software Arene.
Pongamos números sobre la mesa. Toyota calcula que su ecosistema industrial podría necesitar unos 400.000 robots entre 2028 y 2040, tanto para sustituir equipos existentes como para incorporar nuevas soluciones de automatización, según detalló Reuters en septiembre. De ellos, 150.000 corresponderían al fabricante y otras empresas del grupo, mientras que los 250.000 restantes serían para sus proveedores. La estimación contempla fabricación propia y compras a terceros, por lo que no equivale a ventas previstas de Toyota Robotics. Además, la compañía calcula que la renovación de instalaciones y equipos envejecidos en su cadena industrial podría requerir alrededor de un billón de yenes anuales, una necesidad estimada que no representa una inversión comprometida específicamente para la nueva organización.
Y aquí aparece una de las claves del proyecto: la firma japonesa no quiere limitarse a utilizar robots, también pretende vender las soluciones que desarrolle. Para conseguirlo, su estrategia contempla perfeccionar primero estas tecnologías dentro de su propia actividad y después ofrecerlas a otras empresas manufactureras y sectores industriales, con la posibilidad de extenderlas más adelante a aplicaciones de la vida cotidiana. Toyota aspira a conseguir un crecimiento sostenido de las ventas de este negocio a partir de 2030. Por ahora, sin embargo, hablamos de una hoja de ruta empresarial, no de un catálogo de productos con lanzamientos ya confirmados.
La apuesta tiene antecedentes que ayudan a entender qué hay detrás del anuncio. Toyota lleva años investigando robots de asistencia y ha desarrollado prototipos como ELEY, concebido para realizar tareas de manipulación, mientras que su instituto de investigación colabora con Boston Dynamics en el desarrollo de sistemas de inteligencia artificial para el humanoide Atlas. Pero no todo se queda en las demostraciones: Walden Robotics, empresa independiente surgida del Toyota Research Institute y respaldada financieramente por Toyota, asegura que sus máquinas realizan trabajos de producción en una planta del fabricante en Norteamérica desde febrero de 2026. Conviene distinguir estas iniciativas de la nueva organización, porque Toyota todavía no ha detallado cuáles pasarán a depender de ella.
La cuestión ahora es si el fabricante conseguirá trasladar esa experiencia a un mercado donde fabricar buenos coches no garantiza desarrollar robots comercialmente exitosos. Su ventaja de partida está en conocer de primera mano los problemas que pretende resolver, pero tendrá que demostrar que las soluciones funcionan también para clientes con necesidades distintas. La nueva organización representa, por tanto, algo más que un cambio administrativo: es un intento de convertir capacidades tecnológicas e industriales ya existentes en una actividad comercial con recorrido propio. Lo que todavía no sabemos es qué peso llegará a tener ese negocio dentro de la compañía.

articles.title: EngageXP lança o Gamin PLUS, um clube de benefícios para gamers; veja como funciona.
articles.text:
A EngageXP, um hub de soluções de performance para o mercado gamer desde 2021, lançou o Gamin PLUS, um clube de membros voltado ao público gamer que combina benefícios digitais, recompensas e atividades em comunidade.
A iniciativa busca explorar um modelo diferente dos serviços tradicionais de assinatura de jogos. Em vez de oferecer acesso temporário a uma biblioteca, como acontece no Xbox Game Pass e no PlayStation Plus, o Gamin PLUS permite que os usuários acumulem moedas virtuais para resgatar jogos, créditos in-game e outros benefícios em uma única assinatura.
Como funciona o Gamin PLUS?
Os assinantes recebem 1.000 G-Coins por mês, moedas virtuais para utilizar no resgate de itens no catálogo do serviço.
Segundo a EngageXP, jogos completos podem ser resgatados a partir de 1.000 G-Coins, enquanto créditos para jogos online começam em 100 G-Coins. A plataforma também prevê outros tipos de benefícios e cupons de desconto.
As G-Coins são cumulativas e não expiram, permitindo que os usuários as guardem para resgates futuros de itens de maior valor. Entretanto, a disponibilidade dos produtos depende do catálogo, que recebe novos jogos mensalmente.
O serviço também conta com um sistema de gamificação. Os membros podem completar missões para acumular pontos de experiência (XP), avançar de nível e obter recompensas adicionais, podendo ser uma alternativa para conquistar alguma recompensa mais fácil.
Outra funcionalidade é a comunidade exclusiva no Discord, onde os participantes podem interagir, encontrar outros jogadores e participar de atividades.
Quanto custa a assinatura?
O Gamin PLUS está disponível por R$ 25 mensais durante o período promocional de lançamento. O preço regular é de R$ 40 por mês.
Também há uma modalidade trimestral por R$70,00 e o anual por R$ 250.
O serviço está disponível no site oficial, onde os interessados podem consultar as condições de contratação e os benefícios oferecidos.
Sobre a EngageXP
A EngageXP é um hub de soluções de performance para o mercado focado no ecossistema gamer, com produtos que conectam jogadores, criadores de conteúdo e a indústria de videogames.
Sobre o Gamin PLUS
O Gamin PLUS é um clube de membros para gamers. Por uma mensalidade, o membro recebe G-Coins mensais para resgatar jogos e créditos in-game, além de descontos. O serviço também é focado na comunidade, com conteúdo exclusivo para quem pretende fazer parte do mercado de games.
Rachele Victoria é formada em Letras, MBA em Inovação e atua há 10 anos com comunicação e conteúdo gamer.
Amazon Prime também é feito para jogadores!
Todo mês, obtenha itens exclusivos, jogos grátis, uma assinatura gratuita na Twitch.tv e muito mais com sua assinatura Prime. Clique aqui para um teste gratuito de 30 dias.

articles.title: Japón lanzó un plan de emergencia con IA y equipos de élite contra la ola de filtraciones de datos
articles.text:
El Gobierno de Japón presentó el 6 de noviembre un paquete de medidas de emergencia contra la ola de ciberataques que expuso datos personales en el país. La primera ministra, Sanae Takaichi, y sus ministros aprobaron el uso de IA para detectar fallas en sistemas, la creación de equipos de expertos y un gasto inicial de 10.000 millones de yenes.
La cifra equivale a unos USD 63 millones y saldrá de la reserva presupuestaria del año fiscal 2026, según Kyodo. El Gobierno la aprobó antes de presentar el paquete. Es un monto de partida para financiar las primeras acciones, no el costo total del plan.
Según Jiji Press, unos 2.000 millones de yenes servirán para revisar con IA las vulnerabilidades de los sistemas del Estado. Otros 4.100 millones irán a equipos y entrenamiento de la policía para investigar ataques, y 3.800 millones al refuerzo de la seguridad informática de la Agencia Digital.
El detonante fue una serie de filtraciones de datos personales por accesos no autorizados. Kyodo citó como ejemplo el ataque contra el proveedor de internet GMO Internet Group, a cuyos responsables se les atribuye haber exigido un rescate.
Equipos de élite y acceso a servidores atacantes
El paquete se apoya en cuatro ejes: reforzar la seguridad básica con IA, mejorar la recolección y el análisis de información, responder a los ataques con una estrategia y apoyar a las víctimas para limitar el daño, según Kyodo.
Un equipo de especialistas de primer nivel, al que el Gobierno llama top gun, hará pruebas de penetración (ataques simulados) y reforzará las defensas. The Japan Times informó que ese grupo quedará constituido a fines de noviembre.
Otro equipo de expertos, con funcionarios y personal del sector privado, irá a asistir a las empresas que sufran un ataque. Un tercer grupo asesorará a las compañías en riesgo antes de que las ataquen, según Kyodo.
El Gobierno también quiere neutralizar amenazas entrando de forma preventiva en los servidores de los atacantes, una práctica que Kyodo describe como “defensa cibernética activa”. Una ley vigente desde octubre lo permite, según el diario The Asahi Shimbun, que precisó que la policía y las Fuerzas de Autodefensa podrán acceder a esas computadoras para inutilizarlas.
Si un incidente puede afectar gravemente la seguridad nacional, se enviará un equipo con integrantes de la Oficina Nacional de Ciberseguridad, la Policía Nacional y el Ministerio de Defensa, entre otros organismos.
Cooperación con las empresas de IA
El plan prevé trabajar con empresas informáticas extranjeras y desarrolladores de IA avanzada para mantener actualizada la información sobre vulnerabilidades, según Kyodo. NHK agregó que se pedirá a las empresas que manejan datos personales que borren los que no necesiten.
Takaichi había convocado el 26 de octubre la primera reunión ministerial sobre ciberseguridad. Entonces dijo que la situación “se ha vuelto grave” y ordenó acelerar el análisis de vulnerabilidades en los ministerios con apoyo del Instituto de Seguridad de la IA, además de ampliar la ayuda a las pequeñas y medianas empresas, según el texto oficial de la Oficina del Primer Ministro.
En esa reunión también pidió una red para vigilar ataques en cadenas de suministro completas y que se pusiera al servicio de las empresas la experiencia técnica del sector privado. Y fijó un plazo: el paquete debía estar listo hacia fines de la semana siguiente.
El Gobierno busca, según el documento citado por Kyodo, alcanzar “uno de los niveles de ciberseguridad más altos del mundo”. El primer paso verificable es el equipo de especialistas, previsto para fines de este mes.

articles.title: « Critique » : OpenAI lance GPT-6 Cyber, son IA la plus dangereuse à ce jour
articles.text:
OpenAI passe à la vitesse supérieure en matière de cybersécurité. L’entreprise de Sam Altman vient de dévoiler GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle d’IA conçu pour débusquer des failles de sécurité, trouver un moyen de les exploiter et proposer des correctifs. Le modèle succède à GPT-5.6 Cyber, lancé à la fin de l’été. Sans surprise, GPT-6 Cyber est réservé aux entreprises qui font partie de Daybreak Red, le programme d’OpenAI dédié aux professionnels de la sécurité.
Des centaines de failles débusquées
Comme l’explique OpenAI dans son billet de blog, ses chercheurs ont utilisé GPT-6 Cyber pour découvrir 81 failles inconnues dans Firefox. Toutes les vulnérabilités ont été jugées de gravité élevée par Mozilla. Le navigateur a pourtant déjà été passé au crible par plusieurs générations d’IA taillées pour la cybersécurité, dont Claude Mythos. Le modèle a malgré tout trouvé des failles inédites et aidé à corriger le navigateur
« Firefox est entré en 2026 comme l’une des bases de code les plus renforcées et les plus scrutées au monde », souligne Brian Grinstead, ingénieur chez Mozilla, cité par OpenAI.
Même son de cloche du côté de Linux. OpenAI explique avoir mis au point 948 tactiques d’exploitation qui permettent à un simple utilisateur de prendre le contrôle total d’un système Linux. C’est plus de cinq fois plus que GPT-5.6, qui n’en avait trouvé que 166 lors du même test, trois mois plus tôt. L’opération, et la découverte des failles, a coûté environ 1,2 million de dollars de calcul.
 Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber: a major advance in security research that pairs stronger capabilities with better model alignment.
The model powered the Linux kernel research we announced yesterday, and security teams at companies like Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif, and… pic.twitter.com/34uAeNnhwP
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) November 5, 2026
En amont de l’annonce, le spécialiste de la sécurité industrielle Dragos a testé le modèle d’IA sur une fausse centrale électrique. Sans presque aucune instruction de la part d’un programmeur, l’IA y a trouvé deux failles inconnues dans le fonctionnement de la centrale. , Pour Rob T. Lee, directeur de l’IA chez Dragos, « le niveau de compétence requis pour la reconnaissance et la recherche de vulnérabilités qui précèdent une attaque est en train de baisser ». En clair, il n’y a plus besoin d’avoir des compétences en informatique pour débusquer des failles et lancer une cyberattaque.
Une IA classée « critique »
Pour la toute première fois, OpenAI attribue à l’un de ses modèles cyber un niveau « critique ». C’est le niveau le plus élevé du cadre d’évaluation des risques de la start-up. Pour mémoire, GPT-5.6 Cyber était seulement classé « élevé », mais GPT-6 Astra a déjà franchi le seuil du critique lors de différents tests.
OpenAI insiste sur le fait que son IA respecte mieux les règles. Bien que classée critique, l’intelligence artificielle se veut plus docile, ce qui devrait éviter les incidents de sécurité indésirables. Le géant de l’IA garde évidemment en tête l’incident de cet été, qui s’est soldé par le piratage de la plateforme Hugging Face. Lors d’un test conçu pour l’occasion, GPT-6 Cyber s’est d’ailleurs abstenu de s’attaquer à des services hors de sa mission dans 99,93 % des cas, contre 94,49 % pour son prédécesseur.
« Plus de 99 % du temps, il fait ce que vous lui demandez », résume Fouad Matin, responsable de la sécurité chez OpenAI, auprès de The Next Web.
Tous les experts ne sont pas rassurés pour autant. « À l’échelle à laquelle fonctionnent ces modèles, même une petite fraction représente des actions contre des systèmes que personne n’a autorisés », nuance Chris Hughes, de Noma Security, interrogé par le média. Si l’IA obéit dans 99 % des cas, il reste une infime, mais bien réelle, possibilité qu’elle réalise des actions imprévues à l’encontre de systèmes informatiques, ce qui risque de faire des dégâts.
Une course contre la montre
Pour OpenAI, le monde de la sécurité est engagé dans une véritable course contre la montre. Selon la start-up de San Francisco, « il est clair que nous disposons d’une fenêtre limitée pour utiliser les modèles de pointe afin de sécuriser les logiciels ». En clair, il faut impérativement se servir de l’IA pour sécuriser tous les logiciels critiques avant qu’une entité malveillante exploite la technologie pour lancer des cyberattaques. C’est pourquoi OpenAI refuse de lever le pied et dégaine réguliérement de nouveaux modèles d’IA taillés pour traquer les failles de sécurité.
