articles.title: Northern Arc's diversified debt fund hits first close at over Rs 400 crore
articles.text:
Northern Arc's diversified debt fund hits first close at over Rs 400 Cr
The 15th private credit fund from Northern Arc Investment Managers targets a Rs 1,500 crore corpus and a 16% XIRR, as its India Impact Fund matures after deploying Rs 1,398 crore.
Northern Arc Investment Managers, the asset management arm of Northern Arc Capital, has announced the first close of its Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund with commitments of more than Rs 400 crore from institutions, family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and high-net-worth individuals (HNIs).
The fund is the firm's 15th private credit vehicle. It is a sector-agnostic Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) focused on performing private credit, rated AA (SO) by CareEdge Ratings. It targets a corpus of Rs 1,500 crore, with a greenshoe option of Rs 500 crore that could take it to Rs 2,000 crore. The fund has a five-year tenure and targets a 16% XIRR.
The announcement coincides with the maturity of the Northern Arc India Impact Fund, which channelled global capital into financial inclusion opportunities across India. Over its tenure, the fund supported 60 businesses across credit cycles, with gross deployment of over Rs 1,398 crore at the fund level, backed by UHNIs, family offices, and domestic and global institutional investors.
Commenting on the announcements, Ashish Mehrotra, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Northern Arc Capital, said, "The first close of the Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund reflects continued investor interest in private credit and its evolving role in sophisticated investment portfolios. The maturity of our Northern Arc India Impact Fund further demonstrates our experience in managing private credit investments across credit cycles. Together, these milestones reinforce our focus on disciplined credit selection, portfolio diversification and risk management.”
He added, “Over the past decade, we have built a diversified private credit platform that has deployed over Rs. 16,500 crores across 15 AIFs and two PMS offerings and served more than 1,500 investors across institutional and wealth segments. As private credit becomes an increasingly strategic allocation for investors, we remain focused on connecting capital with businesses across sectors while creating opportunities for risk-adjusted returns."
Since its inception in 2014, Northern Arc Investment Managers has launched 15 funds, of which seven have fully matured, delivering returns at a weighted average XIRR of over 14.5%, in line with targeted returns, without any extension or principal loss to investors, the company said. It has cumulatively distributed over Rs 10,000 crore of principal and coupon since inception.
Separately, Northern Arc Capital reported a 41% year-on-year growth in consolidated profit after tax to Rs 129 crore in Q2 FY27, while net interest income rose 32% to Rs 425 crore. Lending assets under management grew 34% to Rs 19,003 crore, supported by a 64% rise in direct lending AUM to Rs 12,502 crore, which now accounts for 66% of the overall portfolio. Credit costs improved by 11 basis points to 2.66%."

articles.title: IMSI vs IMEI: What Your Phone Broadcasts and Who Can Read It
articles.text:
In April 2026, BleepingComputer reported that Canadian authorities arrested three men for operating an “SMS blaster,” a device that pretends to be a cell tower to send phishing texts to nearby phones.
It’s a close cousin of the IMSI catcher, the fake-tower device used for surveillance. Both work by tricking phones into connecting to the strongest signal and sharing information before anything is authenticated.
One of the main things a fake tower can collect this way is your IMSI, the identifier tied to your SIM, but it’s far from the only thing your phone gives away.
What information does your phone actually broadcast?
Your phone has several radios that connect to different kinds of signals and share different information.
The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios share hardware addresses, which modern phones randomize or rotate to reduce tracking.
The cellular radio reveals two identifiers that typically never change: the IMSI, which is tied to your SIM card, and the IMEI, which is tied to your device.
IMSI vs IMEI
The IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) is a unique number assigned by your mobile carrier when you sign up for your service. It lives on your SIM card, and is used by the network to look you up and authenticate you. For the most part, your IMSI never changes.
The IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) is a unique number tied to your physical phone. Unlike the IMSI, the network doesn’t authenticate it, so it names a device without proving anything.
How well each is protected depends on the cellular generation in use. The standards come from 3GPP, the industry body that writes mobile network specifications. Newer generations protect identifiers better, but phones fall back to older ones, which is where fake towers come in.
| Network | IMSI | IMEI | 
| 2G/3G | Sent in plaintext (unencrypted) | Transmitted in plaintext and allowed to be sent without secured channel | 
| 4G (LTE) | Sent in plaintext the first time a phone connects, then replaced by a temporary ID (a GUTI) to reduce the exposure of the IMSI. | Sent only after mutual authentication | 
| 5G standalone | Encrypted (as a Subscription Concealed Identifier, or SUCI). | Sent only after mutual authentication | 
How your IMSI can be leaked
- IMSI catchers/fake base stations: In 4G, a phone will send its IMSI in plaintext to a tower that hasn’t proven who it is, which is what an IMSI catcher exploits. 5G’s SUCI encryption is meant to close that gap, but because 5G coverage isn’t universal, an IMSI catcher can still downgrade your device to 4G or below.
- Paging attacks: An idle phone saves battery by sleeping and waking only at set moments, called paging occasions, to check for incoming calls, texts, or notifications. In 4G, that slot is calculated from the IMSI with a publicly documented formula, so while the IMSI never changes, neither does the slot. (5G calculates it from a temporary ID instead.)
In a 2019 paper, researchers showed how to exploit this.
An attacker who knows your phone number can trigger “silent calls” (calls cut off before your phone rings), texts, or app notifications, and uses a nearby radio receiver to watch which slot sees activity.
After about eight tries on average, the pattern confirms you’re in that area, with no fake tower needed. It worked against all the US carriers tested.
This paging attack is a stepping stone to a more serious one: using a fake tower, an attacker can link your phone number directly to your IMSI. Some carriers, when normal pages to a phone’s temporary ID fail, fall back to broadcasting the raw IMSI in paging messages. Knowing your paging slot, an attacker can trigger that fallback.
A fake tower hijacks your paging channel to block the network’s pages, and a single silent call then makes the carrier send your IMSI over the air where the attacker captures it. The researchers validated this against one major US carrier.
Once an attacker has your IMSI, they can track your location or intercept your calls and texts through signaling attacks, which we covered in an earlier article.
What about the IMEI?
Think of an IMSI catcher as a license plate reader for phones: the IMSI is the plate, which follows your SIM, and the IMEI is the VIN, which stays with the device. In 4G and 5G, a basic fake tower gets the plate but not the VIN, because a phone sends its IMEI only after authenticating with the network.
An attacker generally has to downgrade the phone to an older network first, or use authentication data obtained earlier through SS7 or Diameter attacks, which themselves start with an IMSI. The IMSI rather than the IMEI is used to route a call or look up your location through signaling.
However, if your mobile carrier itself is compromised, whoever has access would be able to track you by your IMEI.
Protect yourself with private cell service.
Cape is America's privacy-first mobile carrier providing unlimited talk, text, and 4G/5G data, built from the ground up with privacy and security at its core.
Most carriers track everything: where you go, who you call, what you do. Cape collects the minimum amount of information required to provide you with service, deletes call and text metadata after 24 hours, rotates your network ID to prevent tracking, defends against SIM- and network-based attacks, and more.
Privacy shouldn't cost more. Switch today and get $29 off for life.
Learn More
Why rotating the IMSI helps
Cape’s Identifier Rotation changes your IMSI every 24 hours, or on demand, cycling through seven IMSIs a week drawn from a shared pool that’s constantly reassigned among customers, so each IMSI carries a tangled history of many people’s activity.
Here’s what that does:
- Harvested IMSIs go stale. Signaling attacks start by harvesting a target’s IMSI, which on a typical carrier stays useful for years. A rotated one stops pointing at you within a day. An attacker can still ask for your current IMSI in real time, which is why rotation is layered on top of Cape’s signaling protections.
- The paging fingerprint moves. In 4G, a new IMSI means a new paging slot, so any pattern an attacker builds no longer matches.
- IMSI catchers lose the thread. A catcher can still grab today’s IMSI, but it can’t match it to yesterday’s, so it can’t build a history of you or confirm you’re nearby using an IMSI it learned earlier. Cape plus GrapheneOS adds LTE-only mode, which blocks downgrades.
For most people, the tracking that matters is the long-term kind built on a stable identifier, which is what rotation breaks.

articles.title: Après Fiat, Opel veut aussi sa petite voiture électrique à moins de 15 000 euros
articles.text:
Le groupe Stellantis a fait une offensive importante au Mondial sous le signe du néo-rétro, notamment avec la 2CV chez Citroën. Si la 2CV a cristallisé toute l’attention, les autres marques du groupe Stellantis pourraient profiter de sa plateforme pour produire un véhicule électrique très abordable. Après Fiat, c’est Opel qui semble être intéressé par la plateforme e-Car.
Opel pourrait avoir sa citadine électrique abordable
Actuellement, la gamme Opel n’a que la vieillissante Corsa en citadine électrique. En revanche, l’Opel Frontera est plus récent et figure parmi les SUV électriques les plus abordables. Toutefois, il reste à plus de 20 000 euros, ce qui n’est pas à la portée de toutes les bourses.
Opel serait alors intéressé par l’utilisation de la plateforme e-Car introduite avec la 2CV pour proposer une citadine électrique abordable dans sa gamme, à moins de 15 000 euros. D’après les informations publiées par le média italien Quattroruote, Opel profiterait de cette plateforme pour faire renaître l’Agila. Une citadine du segment A disparue en 2015, avant d’être remplacée par la Karl jusqu’en 2019 et de voir Opel se retirer du segment A.
Un retour sur le segment A avantageux pour Opel
On dirait que Renault a réussi, avec la Twingo, à relancer une véritable course au segment A avec des motorisations électriques en Europe. Il y a déjà la Dacia Spring et la Nissan Pixo, qui s’appuient sur la base technique de la Twingo, mais c’est maintenant Stellantis qui prépare des voitures du segment A avec la Citroën 2CV, la Fiat Koala, la Leapmotor T03 et certainement l’Opel Agila. Volkswagen a confirmé préparer une citadine du segment A pour la fin 2027 découlant du concept ID.1. Il y a aussi la BYD Dolphin Surf, qui va bientôt être produite en Europe.
Ce segment, qui a failli disparaître, reprend peu à peu de la couleur. La motorisation électrique a remotivé les constructeurs, qui ont pu faire augmenter légèrement les prix de ces voitures au profit d’une meilleure rentabilité du segment A. Mais surtout, pour Stellantis, c’est la catégorie M1E que prépare l’Europe qui intéresse le groupe. Cette catégorie sera avantageuse dans le calcul du bilan CO2. Commercialiser ces petites citadines électriques profitera à toute la gamme, y compris aux voitures hybrides.
Aussi, multiplier les voitures utilisant la plateforme permet de réduire la répartition des coûts de développement et de vendre des voitures moins chères au client. C’est exactement la stratégie qu’adopte Volkswagen avec la plateforme MEB+ utilisée pour l’ID. Polo, l’ID. Cross, le Skoda Epiq et la Cupra Raval.

articles.title: Ola Källenius, CEO de Mercedes: “no existe una estrategia en la que puedas dejar a China de lado”
articles.text:
Mercedes-Benz se está replanteando cómo hace negocios en China, pero desde luego no tiene intención de marcharse. Y es que la marca alemana afirma que presentará un plan más amplio para el país en 2027, todo mientras sus ventas allí continúan cayendo.
Por qué es importante. China es donde Mercedes ha construido buena parte de su rentabilidad, y ahora precisamente es donde se concentran sus problemas. Según el último informe financiero de la compañía, en el tercer trimestre, las ventas de vehículos de Mercedes en el país cayeron un 31 % interanual. Los beneficios ajustados en la división principal de automóviles se redujeron a más de la mitad, hasta los 560 millones de euros, y el margen se contrajo del 4,8 % al 2,5 %. Tal y como comparte Bloomberg, las acciones de Mercedes han perdido más de un tercio de su valor este año.
El mensaje del CEO. En declaraciones durante la presentación de resultados, Ola Källenius, CEO de la compañía, dejó claro que dar marcha atrás no es una opción. “No hay ninguna estrategia en la que se pueda dejar de lado a China,” afirmaba. Para Källenius China es uno de los pilares de la estrategia de la compañía y, argumenta, que además de su tamaño, China importa debido a su ecosistema tecnológico de rápido movimiento y al creciente alcance internacional de los proveedores y fabricantes de automóviles chinos.
Qué salió mal. Källenius admitía que las condiciones en China estaban “deteriorándose más de lo que habíamos pensado que ocurriría este año”, según comparte Bloomberg. El daño es mayor en la gama alta del mercado, donde Mercedes tradicionalmente ha obtenido sus mayores márgenes. El medio señala entre las causas una menor demanda de artículos de lujo vinculada a la crisis inmobiliaria en China, una feroz competencia de precios y rivales locales que ahora compiten en software, tecnología eléctrica y, cada vez más, en diseño. Un día antes de la conferencia sobre los resultados, Mercedes ya había rebajado sus previsiones para el año.
El nuevo enfoque. La compañía está revisando su gama de productos, ventas, producción, aprovisionamiento y tecnología en China, según informa Bloomberg. El primer ejemplo es el próximo Clase E eléctrico, del que Källenius dijo que se había desarrollado partiendo prácticamente de “una hoja de papel en blanco” para los compradores chinos. Se construirá casi en su totalidad en China, lo que debería reducir significativamente los costes variables.
Los límites. Källenius descarta seguir a otros competidores rebajando el precio de sus vehículos para ganar cuota de mercado, según explicaba durante la presentación. Esto deja a Mercedes el objetivo de tener que proteger una marca de lujo mientras compite en una de las guerras de precios más agresivas del mundo. El director financiero, Harald Wilhelm, declaraba que la compañía quiere depender menos de los beneficios de China y está trasladando su cadena de suministro hacia un abastecimiento totalmente local, según comparte Reuters.
Entre líneas. Mercedes ahora parece ver a China como un desafío estructural más que como un bache temporal. Y esto es importante porque la estrategia de Källenius se ha centrado en vender menos coches pero más caros, confiando en las gamas Clase S, Maybach, Clase G y AMG. Dicha fórmula es más difícil de mantener cuando el gasto en artículos de lujo en China es débil.
Y Mercedes no es la única que está haciendo frente a este problema, pues BMW y Volkswagen también han advertido de que China está perjudicando sus beneficios, y precisamente el CEO de Volvo Cars, Håkan Samuelsson, declaró hace unas semanas que el mercado de los coches desarrollados en Occidente en China no va a volver.
Las otras apuestas. Mientras piensan que hacer en China, la compañía busca crecimiento en otros lugares, como Estados Unidos. En este país, Källenius afirma que la compañía planea más inversiones y ve margen para elevar las ventas anuales de más de 300.000 vehículos a cerca de 400.000, según comparten desde Reuters. También señalaba que los costes laborales en EEUU, a pesar de los elevados salarios del país, se sitúan en torno al 80 % de los niveles en Alemania. Audi, de hecho, ha dado un paso similar al anunciar una planta de ensamblaje de 4.000 millones de dólares en EEUU, generando 4.500 empleos.
Más cerca de casa. En Alemania, las cosas también apuntan a un cambio pues, según comparten desde Reuters, la marca relanzará un programa de bajas incentivadas para el personal indirecto a partir de diciembre, y se espera que la mayor parte del impacto en los beneficios se produzca en 2027. Källenius también aseguraba que las nuevas inversiones en Alemania dependen de una mejor productividad y de unos costes más bajos, y señala opciones de producción de menor coste en Hungría, Rumanía y Polonia, donde Mercedes ya tiene presencia.
Qué pasa ahora. Mercedes tiene previstos más de 40 modelos nuevos o renovados de aquí a finales de 2027, según compartían desde Bloomberg, incluidos el CLA y el GLC eléctricos, que ya se están desplegando, y las nuevas versiones de las clases C, S, GLE y GLS. La compañía también aspira a conseguir un ahorro en los costes de materiales de alrededor del 8 % en comparación con 2024, con recortes más profundos en China.

articles.title: Os 7 jogos mais caros da história: o ranking de orçamentos que GTA 6 deve liderar
articles.text:
Quanto custa desenvolver um videogame? Para grandes produções, a resposta pode ultrapassar centenas de milhões de dólares. Equipes com milhares de profissionais, tecnologias de ponta, campanhas de marketing e anos de desenvolvimento fizeram os orçamentos dos chamados jogos AAA crescerem consideravelmente.
Com a chegada de Grand Theft Auto VI, a expectativa é que a Rockstar Games estabeleça um novo recorde. Embora o orçamento oficial do título não tenha sido divulgado, estimativas que circulam na indústria apontam para investimentos bilionários.
Mas quais jogos já alcançaram os maiores custos de produção?
Os sete jogos mais caros da história
A lista considera valores divulgados por empresas, documentos e estimativas de mercado. É importante destacar que os números não seguem uma metodologia única: alguns incluem marketing, outros consideram apenas desenvolvimento, enquanto jogos como serviço acumulam investimentos ao longo de vários anos.
| Jogo | Orçamento divulgado ou estimado | 
| 1. Genshin Impact | Mais de US$ 900 milhões | 
| 2. Star Citizen | Mais de US$ 800 milhões em financiamento e investimentos estimados | 
| 3. Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War | US$ 700 milhões | 
| 4. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare (2019) | US$ 640 milhões | 
| 5. Call of Duty: Black Ops III | US$ 450 milhões | 
| 6. Cyberpunk 2077 | Mais de US$ 440 milhões, incluindo expansão e custos posteriores | 
| 7. Battlefield 6 | Mais de US$ 400 milhões, segundo estimativas | 
Os valores são nominais, não corrigidos pela inflação, e não representam um ranking auditado de custos diretamente comparáveis.
Por que esses jogos custaram tanto?
Entre os títulos da lista, Call of Duty chama atenção por aparecer três vezes. A franquia da Activision utiliza uma estrutura de produção que envolve diferentes estúdios, equipes de desenvolvimento e investimentos contínuos em tecnologia, multiplayer e novos conteúdos.
Já Cyberpunk 2077 representa outro tipo de custo. Além do investimento no lançamento de 2020, a CD Projekt Red precisou dedicar recursos a atualizações, melhorias técnicas e à expansão Phantom Liberty, lançada em 2023.
Em Genshin Impact, o principal diferencial é o modelo de serviço contínuo. Desde 2020, a HoYoverse adiciona personagens, regiões, eventos e sistemas, o que faz os investimentos se acumularem ao longo dos anos.
Star Citizen também apresenta uma situação particular. O projeto da Cloud Imperium Games arrecadou centenas de milhões de dólares por meio de financiamento coletivo, mas dinheiro arrecadado não equivale necessariamente ao custo efetivamente gasto no desenvolvimento.
Por isso, embora apareçam frequentemente em listas de jogos mais caros, esses projetos não podem ser comparados diretamente com títulos de campanha tradicional.
GTA 6 pode se tornar o jogo mais caro já produzido?
O desenvolvimento de GTA 6 envolve um dos projetos mais ambiciosos da Rockstar Games, com um mundo aberto inspirado na Flórida, múltiplos protagonistas e um longo ciclo de produção.
Rumores sobre o orçamento do jogo mencionam cifras que chegam a US$ 2 bilhões. Entretanto, a Rockstar e a Take-Two não confirmaram publicamente esse valor, e não está claro quanto corresponderia ao desenvolvimento, marketing ou investimentos de longo prazo.
Mesmo sem números oficiais, a escala do projeto indica que GTA 6 pode figurar entre as produções mais caras da história dos videogames.
A discussão também revela uma mudança importante na indústria: desenvolver grandes jogos deixou de ser apenas uma questão de criar mundos maiores ou gráficos mais realistas. Atualmente, os custos envolvem manter equipes por anos, desenvolver ferramentas próprias, produzir conteúdo e sustentar operações depois do lançamento.
Se GTA 6 realmente estabelecer um novo recorde, o resultado será mais um exemplo de como os orçamentos dos games se aproximaram — e, em alguns casos, ultrapassaram — os de grandes produções cinematográficas.

articles.title: Esta herramienta gratuita te muestra por fin qué está consumiendo la GPU de tu PC
articles.text:
La GPU es uno de los componentes que casi nunca recibe atención dentro de las herramientas para medir el rendimiento en Windows. Fuera de la temperatura o la carga de trabajo, los usuarios no saben con exactitud qué servicio o aplicación está consumiendo recursos, lo que sí ocurre con la memoria o el procesador. Un ingeniero de Microsoft ha decidido resolver el problema a través de gputaskman, una herramienta que te dice qué hay dentro de tu tarjeta gráfica y qué programas la utilizan.
Scott Hanselman, vicepresidente y miembro del equipo técnico de Microsoft, publicó un repositorio en GitHub que ofrece un programa gratis para monitorear tu GPU. De acuerdo con Neowin, gputaskman muestra información detallada por proceso, uso de la GPU y memoria VRAM. También se incluyen valores como el consumo energético, temperaturas, velocidad de reloj, actividad de codificación y decodificación de video e incluso tráfico PCIe.
A diferencia de las herramientas tradicionales, gputaskman no se limita a indicar que tu tarjeta gráfica está usando cierta cantidad de memoria. La herramienta muestra un listado similar al que vemos en el Administrador de tareas de Windows, con los programas que tienes ejecutándose en ese momento, la cantidad de memoria que consumen y el porcentaje total de uso de la GPU. La aplicación también revela información detallada de lo que pide cada proceso, aunque esta información está dedicada más a entusiastas y desarrolladores.
Si ejecutas modelos de IA en tu ordenador, gputaskman también monitorea su uso
Otra de las funciones interesantes de gputaskman es una que permite ver las cargas de trabajo de la IA. La herramienta detecta los procesos asociados con los modelos de lenguaje y ofrece detalles sobre los pesos, niveles de cuantización, estimaciones de caché KV y otros datos relacionados. El programa puede generar archivos de texto plano y JSON, en caso de que necesites compartir la información para llevar a cabo un análisis posterior.
Si bien Windows 11 ya implementó algunos ajustes en el Administrador de tareas en agosto, gputaskman va un paso más lejos. La versión de Microsoft que se ofrece en el sistema operativo solo ofrece información general sobre el uso de memoria y gráficas de consumo que pueden personalizarse para diversas tareas, como 3D (juegos), video, etc. Esta función no incluye una división por procesos, como sí lo hace la herramienta externa.
Por ahora, gputaskman se encuentra en una fase de desarrollo temprano, por lo que podrías encontrarte con algunos fallos. Hanselman no ha mencionado si existen planes de integrarla de forma nativa en alguna actualización oficial de Windows 11, aunque puedes descargarla gratuitamente desde el repositorio de GitHub. La herramienta es compatible con GPUs de NVIDIA y AMD, así como también con Linux y Mac con chip Apple Silicon.

Score a huge $600 saving on this RTX 5070 Ti gaming laptop from HP, now under $2,100 — HyperX Omen Max 16 machine is fully customizable, base model ships with 16GB DDR5 and a 512GB SSD
Smash through games with high frame rates with these specs
There's a seriously good price on a HP gaming laptop right now with an RTX 5070 Ti and a top spec AMD Ryzen CPU. HP has cut this HyperX Omen Max 16 gaming laptop down to $2,099.99 right now, or slightly more if you fancy the OLED, giving you a $600 saving in the process.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Helium Health gets $2.5m Google.org grant to deploy AI in maternal healthcare - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian e-health startup Helium Health has received a US$2.5 million grant from Google.org to roll out artificial intelligence (AI) solutions that improve maternal healthcare delivery in the country.
Founded in 2016, Helium Health takes hospitals and clinics instantly digital with its flagship Electronic Medical Records/Hospital Management Information System (EMR/HMIS) product, the most widely used such solution in West Africa.
The company is among 15 global recipients of the US$30 million Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. The initiative backs organisations that work with governments to improve public service delivery.
The funding will support the deployment of clinical AI models through Helium Health’s maternal health initiative, HeliumMum, across the Lagos, Delta, Kano and Oyo states. Lagos will serve as the main launchpad. Helium Health will also join a dedicated Google.org Accelerator programme, where it will receive technical support from Google engineers and AI product experts.
Through HeliumMum, Helium Health will deploy AI tools that help pregnant women identify potential complications early and connect them with appropriate healthcare providers. The platform links women to facilities equipped with electronic medical records and AI-powered clinical decision support systems, so healthcare professionals can make better-informed decisions. It will also give governments actionable data to strengthen maternal health services and identify gaps in care.
The startup aims to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality. Helium Health has already reached more than 3.5 million women through its maternal health initiatives over the past decade.
“Nigeria accounts for nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths globally. Behind every maternal death is a woman whose family expected her to come home,” said Dr Shona Oluwatola, head of public health at Helium Health.
“By equipping the 15 selected organisations with funding and pro bono support from Google’s own AI experts, we are empowering the people closest to the problem to show what is truly possible,” said Maggie Johnson, global head of Google.org.

articles.title: Windows 11 27H2 pourrait être la mise à jour majeure que vous attendez tous
articles.text:
La prochaine mise à jour majeure du système d’exploitation de Microsoft ne sera encore pas Windows 12. Si la prochaine version majeure du système d’exploitation de Microsoft fait parler d’elle depuis 2023, son arrivée sur votre PC n’est a priori pas prévue pour tout de suite. Microsoft aurait en effet pour projet de se concentrer encore un peu sur l’amélioration de Windows 11. Et pour la prochaine mise à jour majeure du système d’exploitation, 27H2, dont la sortie devrait être prévue pour l’automne 2027, Microsoft partirait d’une feuille blanche.
Alors que tout le monde s’attendait à voir arriver Windows 12 en 2024, Microsoft a adopté à la place un cycle de publication de mises à jour étalées sur trois ans. Ce cycle arrivant à échéance en 2027, Microsoft prépare l’arrivée de la prochaine mise à jour majeure de son système d’exploitation. Et il ne s’agira visiblement toujours pas de Windows 12. La firme de Redmond semble vouloir tenir sa promesse d’améliorer Windows 11 plutôt que de lancer une nouvelle version de son OS accompagnée de nouvelles fonctionnalités.
Un remplacement complet du système
Contrairement aux mises à jour 25H2 et 26H2 qui n’étaient que de simples paquets d’activation débloquant graduellement les nouvelles fonctionnalités, la mise à jour 27H2 devrait être une mise à niveau complète. La prochaine version de Windows 11 remplacerait visiblement de larges pans du système d’exploitation, comme cela a été le cas avec Windows 11 24H2. C’est en tout cas ce que rapporte The Verge qui cite des sources a priori bien informées sur les plans à venir de Microsoft.
Comme elle l’a déjà fait cette année avec la mise en place de Windows K2, son plan secret pour remettre Windows 11 à flot et regagner la confiance des utilisateurs, Microsoft aurait pour principal objectif de proposer une mise à jour améliorant les performances globales et résolvant surtout les problèmes de lourdeur de son OS.
Les changements à venir avec Windows 11 27H2 seraient d’ailleurs si importants que Microsoft prévoirait de lancer les tests de sa prochaine mise à jour bien plus tôt qu’à l’accoutumée auprès des Insiders.
Pour préparer ce changement, Microsoft aurait prévu de remplacer son emblématique fond d’écran bleu « Bloom » par de nouveaux visuels qui pourraient être dévoilés ce mois-ci lors de la conférence Ignite. Le changement de fond d’écran, qui pourrait par ailleurs varier en fonction des différentes versions de Windows (famille, pro, etc.) reprendrait un design similaire au fond d’écran « Bloom », mais avec une feuille colorée pliée et immergée dans des nuages.

articles.title: Chainalysis says breach exposed credentials for all customers
articles.text:
Blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis says a recent attack on its systems and internal tools has exposed credentials and live tokens for all customers.
Chainalysis provides blockchain analysis tools to trace cryptocurrency transactions and investigate crimes such as fraud, ransomware, and money laundering. Its customer list includes law enforcement, government agencies, financial institutions, insurance companies, and cryptocurrency businesses worldwide.
This follows the company's disclosure last Friday that attackers using AI tools accessed customers' names, email addresses, user IDs, and organizational role labels using what it described as "offensive agentic techniques."
While it initially said the impact was limited and the breach affected only non-sensitive identity metadata, later updates revealed that usernames and password hashes for all customers were exposed in an "on-path attack" (more commonly known as a Man-in-the-Middle or MITM attack).
However, the company found no evidence that the attackers accessed investigative graph data or altered its blockchain attribution repositories.
"On Monday, we discovered certain customer information including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed to a malicious actor," it said in a Wednesday update. "At this time we continue to have no evidence that any investigations data has been accessed or Chainalysis attribution data has been manipulated."
While the company locked Chainalysis accounts as a precaution after discovering that some customers' passwords had been exposed and asked users to reset their passwords before signing in again, it has now taken the login portal offline, together with Reactor and Data Solutions, the Know-Your-Transaction (KYT) user interface and API, and address screening products, after discovering further abnormal activity.
To ensure threat actors don't access affected accounts, Chainalysis asked customers to provide trusted IP addresses so they can regain access to the login portal once it is brought back online and reset their credentials.
"Contact support@chainalysis.com or your Chainalysis account team with trusted IP addresses for our allowlist. We will then grant access for users to reset their passwords and rotate API keys to register transactions. We are working around the clock to harden our systems and bring Reactor and Data Solutions back online. We will require additional protections to access accounts, including that every user will have to reset passwords and rotate API keys as appropriate," it added.
"Once access is granted, all users will be required to reset their passwords and rotate API keys, as applicable, before registering transactions," the company noted earlier today.
Chainalysis' disclosure follows several other security incidents affecting cryptocurrency companies in recent weeks. Ledger also asked Asian resellers and distributors last month to remove products from shelves and halt wallet sales while it is investigating multiple hardware implant incidents.
More recently, crypto exchange Binance revealed that North Korean hackers stole roughly $6.34 billion worth of cryptocurrency after compromising its wallet infrastructure by infecting an employee's laptop with malware during a fake job interview.

articles.title: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate
Organizations building applications powered by artificial intelligence (AI) face a recurring challenge: giving large language model (LLM) agents access to enterprise data lakes without duplicating integration logic across every agent and application. Most teams begin by wiring agents directly to databases and APIs, with no shared gateway such as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in between. Each new dataset demands custom code, and each agent reimplements its own access control. As the number of datasets or agents grows, permission enforcement drifts, and onboarding a new data source becomes a multi-day engineering effort.
Our team supports Amazon’s North America Sort Center (NASC) network, where planning teams rely on operational data to manage capacity, labor, and package flow. To give those teams conversational access to that data, we built a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to address this problem for planning teams in NASC. The server acts as a centralized, agent-agnostic gateway between AI agents and our enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON metadata file that the server discovers automatically on the next pipeline sync.
In this post, we describe the architecture, show how a metadata-driven approach removes the need for per-dataset integration code, and explain how the serverless infrastructure supports multiple agents and applications in a multi-tenant environment.
Problem statement and design goals
Two interrelated challenges shaped how we designed this system: fragmented data access patterns and an unsustainable onboarding model.
Integration challenge at scale
Our data lake contains thousands of datasets spanning operational metrics, business analytics, and domain-specific data. Multiple teams wanted AI assistants that could query this data conversationally, but each built its own integration from scratch. Each agent embedded its own SQL generation logic, schema knowledge, and connection handling, so a schema change meant patching every agent individually. Access control was fragmented, with no single audit point for data access decisions. Onboarding a new dataset required custom tool code, query validation, and redeployment, typically a multi-day effort per table.
Design goals
We established four requirements:
- Configuration-driven data lake access. Adding a dataset requires only a metadata file, not code.
- Agent-agnostic tool interfaces. Any MCP-compatible client can invoke the same tools.
- Centralized permission enforcement. Access control is enforced at the MCP server layer.
- Elastic infrastructure. The system scales with bursty AI workload patterns.
Solution overview
The architecture separates concerns into four layers (client, MCP server, tools, and knowledge-base refresh), each independently scalable and deployable. A metadata catalog underpins the tools layer, storing schema descriptions, column-level semantics, and table relationships that the AI agent references when generating SQL. Because the agent derives schema knowledge from the catalog at query time, there is no need to hardcode table structures or redeploy when schemas change. The knowledge-base refresh layer keeps that catalog current, indexing new dataset metadata as it arrives. The following sections describe each layer in detail.
Architecture walkthrough
The following diagram shows the request flow from user query to data layer across all four layers. A user submits a query from a client application (web chat, Slack, an IDE plugin, or an external agent). The request resolves through Amazon Route 53 for DNS and reaches an Application Load Balancer in a public subnet, configured with HTTPS and AWS WAF. The load balancer routes to Amazon Cognito, which authenticates the user and enriches the request. Authenticated traffic then enters the private subnet, where the client layer runs on Amazon ECS Fargate. This layer handles session state in Amazon DynamoDB and forwards requests through an internal Application Load Balancer to the MCP server layer, also on Amazon ECS Fargate. In the MCP server layer, an AI agent powered by Amazon Bedrock orchestrates tools built with FastMCP (a Python framework for building MCP servers). Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is applied to every model interaction. On the right, the data layer holds the tool backends. Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift run SQL queries against the data lake, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, the fully managed Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) capability, handles semantic search. Data ingestion into Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and the knowledge bases is handled by AWS Lambda. Each layer is described in detail in the sections that follow.
MCP client layer: Authentication and session management
A request flows from the client application through Amazon Route 53 for DNS resolution to an Application Load Balancer configured with HTTPS and AWS WAF. The load balancer forwards traffic to the Amazon ECS Fargate client service, which integrates with Amazon Cognito for JSON Web Token (JWT) authentication and Amazon DynamoDB for session storage.
A context mapping configuration drives this enrichment, scoping each query to only the relevant tables. In our testing, this scoping keeps end-to-end interaction latency in the 15–20 second range. The following example shows a context mapping configuration:
When a context specifies tables, the MCP server narrows its search of the metadata catalog to those tables, reducing noise and improving SQL generation accuracy. Adding a new business domain requires only adding an entry to this mapping.
MCP server layer: Stateless execution with conversation state
The MCP server runs on its own ECS Fargate cluster, isolated from the client layer. Requests reach it through Amazon Route 53 and an internal Application Load Balancer in a private subnet. The server handles full orchestration including query analysis, tool selection, execution, and response generation. Through the MCP protocol endpoint (/mcp), a FastMCP-powered JSON-RPC interface, external MCP-compatible clients such as Amazon Q Developer or IDE extensions can discover and invoke tools directly.
Fargate tasks are stateless with conversation state persisted in DynamoDB, so tasks can be replaced or scaled without data loss. When a request arrives, the agent retrieves session history, analyzes user intent using Amazon Bedrock, discovers and invokes appropriate tools, and streams results back to the user.
Tools layer and metadata-driven data lake access
Each tool is registered with FastMCP and discoverable at runtime:
| Sr.no | Tool | Backend | Purpose | 
| 1 | SQL query tools | Amazon Athena Amazon Redshift | SQL queries against any configured dataset in the data lake and Redshift | 
| 2 | Document and metadata search | Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases | Semantic search over internal documentation, table metadata and team wikis | 
| 3 | Policy search | Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases | Search operational policies and standard procedures | 
The Athena query tools are the primary interface to the data lake. The agent first queries the metadata catalog to understand available schemas, generates an optimized SQL query through Amazon Bedrock, validates and auto-corrects the SQL for Athena compatibility, then executes it. Results flow back to the orchestrating agent for natural language synthesis.
Responsible AI controls
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is applied to all LLM interactions and is designed to filter harmful content, enforce grounding checks, and help block prompt injection attempts. These guardrails operate as production controls at the MCP server layer, so every connected agent benefits from the same content safety policies regardless of how it connects. The Athena query tools enforce SELECT-only queries, rejecting write operations at the tool level before they reach the data lake.
Knowledge base refresh layer: Dataset onboarding with a single JSON file
The entire system is built around configuration-driven extensibility. Adding a new dataset requires a metadata JSON file describing the table and an optional context mapping entry. The file captures the table’s schema, business context, and column-level semantics. It serves as the single source of truth that the AI agent uses to understand and query the dataset:
The business_description_for_the_table field carries engine-specific query hints, such as “always use date() to wrap string literals,” that reduce SQL validation failures. The column_details field pairs each column_name [type] with a natural language description and sample values, giving the agent both schema awareness and business semantics. The sample_values field matters for accurate WHERE clause generation because the agent learns real data patterns, for instance that warehouse_id holds codes like FC-EAST-07 rather than spelled-out names like “East region facility.”
The pipeline picks up metadata files, generates vector embeddings with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings, and indexes them into Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Once indexed, the table is discoverable by all connected agents without manual re-indexing or server restarts.
To improve accuracy for specific applications, an engineer can optionally associate the dataset with a business context. This narrows the search scope, so the agent prioritizes the right tables. The following example shows a context mapping entry:
If no context is specified, the agent searches across all indexed tables. The context mapping reduces latency and improves SQL accuracy by limiting the search space. This scoping is optional and can be added at any time without modifying the metadata files themselves.
Putting it together: A query in action
When a user asks, “What were our top 10 highest-value orders last month?”, the client enriches the request with business context to narrow scope. The agent converts the question into a vector embedding, searches the metadata catalog for matching schemas, and selects the most relevant table via a lightweight LLM call.
Using the selected schema, column descriptions, and engine-specific query hints, the agent generates a SQL statement such as:
The SQL is validated and auto-corrected for engine compatibility, then executed against Amazon Athena. The agent formats the results into a natural language response and streams it back to the user. In our testing, this end-to-end flow completes within 15–20 seconds.
The same orchestration extends beyond pure SQL. Because document search is registered as another tool on the same server, the agent can answer questions that span structured and unstructured sources in a single turn, such as “What was our return rate for Q4, and what does the product team’s analysis say about the root causes?” For that request, the agent runs an Athena query for the return-rate figure and a Knowledge Bases document search for the analysis, then combines both into one response.
Security and multi-tenant access
That single-turn orchestration works only because every tool call passes through the same controlled gateway. The architecture uses layered security rather than a single enforcement point. The MCP server runs in private subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer and is not reachable from the internet. Only the client layer, which sits behind a public-facing Application Load Balancer with AWS WAF, can route requests to it. Amazon Cognito validates user identity at the client layer, and only authenticated, token-bearing requests are forwarded downstream. At the tool level, the Athena query tools enforce SELECT-only queries, rejecting write operations before they reach the data lake. All tool invocations are logged to Amazon CloudWatch with structured JSON, which gives security teams a single audit point for data access across every agent and application. This architecture is available in the AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases are available.
This centralized design is also what makes the server multi-tenant. Because the standardized /mcp endpoint accepts any MCP-compatible client regardless of which LLM or orchestration framework it uses, multiple agents share the same tools and the same access controls. Adding a new agent requires only pointing it at the server endpoint, so onboarding another team extends the system without weakening or duplicating the security model.
Serverless infrastructure and scaling
Each layer scales through a mechanism suited to its workload pattern:
| Layer | Scaling mechanism | Trigger | 
| Client (ECS Fargate) | ECS Service Auto Scaling | CPU utilization (50% threshold) | 
| MCP Server (ECS Fargate) | ECS Service Auto Scaling | CPU/Memory utilization | 
| Athena | Serverless (automatic) | Query concurrency | 
| Amazon Bedrock | Managed service scaling | Inference requests | 
Amazon ECS Fargate provides serverless compute with no EC2 instances to manage. Downstream services (Athena, Bedrock) scale automatically, so the system handles a single query or hundreds of concurrent queries without configuration changes.
Use cases and extensions
This architecture supports several patterns beyond basic question-answering. Enterprise knowledge assistants can combine data lake queries with document search to answer complex questions spanning both structured data and unstructured knowledge, such as “What’s our return rate for Q4, and what does the product team’s analysis say about the root causes?” Internal analytics copilots let business users query the data lake conversationally without writing SQL, relying on the metadata descriptions and query hints to guide the agent toward accurate, performant query patterns.
The standardized /mcp endpoint also supports multi-agent workflows. Multiple specialized agents for data analysis, document retrieval, and operational alerting can share the same MCP server, each accessing the full tool suite through a common protocol. Onboarding a new team’s data follows the same configuration-driven pattern. They add a metadata JSON file, and within one pipeline sync cycle their dataset is discoverable by every connected agent and application.
Conclusion
A centralized MCP server on Amazon ECS Fargate provides a scalable, secure gateway between AI agents and enterprise data lakes. The metadata-driven approach removes the need for per-dataset integration code, and the Model Context Protocol standard means any MCP-compatible client can connect without custom adapters.
The key architectural decision is separating the tool layer from the agent layer. Agents evolve rapidly, but data access patterns should outlive any single agent implementation. Treating extensibility as a configuration problem rather than a code problem accelerates onboarding.
To learn more, see Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate, Amazon Bedrock, the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases user guide, Amazon Athena, and the Model Context Protocol specification.
Next steps
We are extending this architecture in two directions. First, finer-grained access control where table owners can mark sensitive columns as restricted per permission group, and the agent automatically excludes those columns from generated SQL without prompt-level changes.
Second, closing the feedback loop so that when queries fail or produce low-confidence results, the system captures the failure pattern and surfaces targeted suggestions for improving column descriptions, adding query hints.

articles.title: Kubernetes, mark II? Why Google's giving away gVisor, a code sandbox used by Anthropic and OpenAI
articles.text:
Kubernetes, mark II? Why Google’s giving away gVisor, a code sandbox used by Anthropic and OpenAI
Google wants to emulate one of its biggest ever open-source success stories, donating three core AI agent infrastructure projects to a neutral foundation in the hope they become industry standards, just as Kubernetes did for containers.
In a blog post published on Thursday, Drew Bradstock, VP of product management, Kubernetes and orchestration at Google, confirmed that the company is donating gVisor, Agent Substrate, and OpenRL to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).
The move comes amid growing concerns about the security of autonomous AI agents, particularly their ability to execute code and interact with external systems. In July, models undergoing a cybersecurity evaluation at OpenAI escaped their restricted environment and breached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure, highlighting the challenges of keeping increasingly capable agents contained.
“We believe that these donations will accelerate the development and adoption of agentic workloads through these projects similarly to what we saw with Kubernetes.”
Bradstock, for his part, argues that addressing such security risks, while making agents more economical to run and train, requires closer cooperation across the various facets of the underlying software and hardware infrastructure. And he believes that putting its technologies under neutral governance could encourage the kind of industry-wide participation that helped Kubernetes become ubiquitous.
“We believe that these donations will accelerate the development and adoption of agentic workloads through these projects similarly to what we saw with Kubernetes,” Bradstock writes.
Why Google’s giving away gVisor
By way of a brief recap, Google open-sourced gVisor in 2018 to improve container security. As The New Stack explained later that year, the technology uses a lightweight kernel running in user space to intercept application system calls, providing an additional layer of isolation between containers and the underlying host operating system. This makes it particularly useful for running untrusted code, including code generated by AI agents.
The technology is used by major AI companies, including Anthropic, which runs code generated by Claude inside gVisor containers on its web platform; and OpenAI, which uses it to isolate code execution. In a security report published just on Wednesday, OpenAI cited sandboxes such as gVisor and Firecracker as important for limiting the damage from exploited Linux kernel vulnerabilities.
The donation itself has been in the works for several weeks. The CNCF accepted gVisor’s application in late September, with Google publicly announcing its plans a few days later. The project’s onboarding process began last week, ahead of Thursday’s broader announcement incorporating all three projects.
In its original October announcement, gVisor contributors and Google software engineers Etienne Perot and Jing Chen sought to reassure users that the company remained committed to the technology. With demand for affordable, secure sandboxes growing, they argued that independent governance could encourage wider participation and adoption, both within Google and beyond.
“We (the gVisor contributors at Google) have been pushing for this move internally with the expectation that this will accelerate gVisor’s growth and adoption both within and outside of Google, in a similar manner as what has happened with Kubernetes,” they wrote at the time.
“We have been pushing for this move internally with the expectation that this will accelerate gVisor’s growth and adoption both within and outside of Google.”
Agent Substrate addresses a different challenge: how to run large numbers of autonomous agents without wasting computing resources while they sit idle. As The New Stack reported in July, the project introduces an additional runtime layer on top of Kubernetes, allowing agents to be suspended when inactive and resumed when needed, without repeatedly creating and destroying Kubernetes Pods. It does this by separating an agent’s persistent state from the computing resources executing it, with gVisor providing one of the available options for securely isolating that execution.
As part of the announcement this week, Google officially released Agent Substrate 1.0 and made it generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
OpenRL, meanwhile, focuses on reinforcement learning, allowing developers to fine-tune AI models on their own Kubernetes infrastructure. Publicly introduced in June, the project coordinates the training and evaluation processes used to improve models. It also integrates with Agent Substrate, allowing training exercises to run inside isolated environments that can be secured using gVisor.
Collectively, the three projects address the execution, security and training requirements of autonomous AI agents.
Going vendor neutral
The move to CNCF governance should also change how gVisor is developed and maintained. In their October announcement, Perot and Chen outlined plans to move the project’s development and testing infrastructure outside Google, give external maintainers permission to merge code, and introduce a governance model that prevents any single company from exercising unilateral control.
Notably, in the project’s CNCF application submitted through GitHub in September, Perot identified a divide among gVisor’s existing adopters. At one end are major technology companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI, which can invest in adapting the technology to their needs; at the other are specialist startups whose businesses depend heavily on secure code execution. The opportunity, Perot suggested, lies in reaching the much broader market between those two camps.
Such companies “don’t have the resources to invest specifically into security but would happily adopt an off-the-shelf, widely-available sandboxing runtime,” Perot wrote in the application.
There’s also the question of why more cloud providers haven’t integrated gVisor into their commercial offerings. In their October announcement, Perot and Chen noted that Google, DigitalOcean and Modal were among the few providers selling general-purpose computing services powered by gVisor, despite evidence that customers were already installing the technology themselves on competing cloud platforms. The engineers suggested that concerns about Google’s control of the project could explain the discrepancy.
“The remaining explanation of the lack of direct integration is likely the project’s (pre-donation) governance risk,” they wrote.
But perhaps the most interesting obstacle concerns the Linux kernel itself. Google and other companies using gVisor maintain their own kernel modifications to improve its performance, particularly for I/O-intensive applications. Those improvements aren’t universally available, potentially leaving other users with slower execution environments.
Bradstock attributes the difficulty in getting those improvements incorporated into the mainline Linux kernel to gVisor’s hitherto Google-centric credentials.
“Upstream Linux maintainers declined to merge them while the project was owned by a single vendor.”
“Upstream Linux maintainers declined to merge them while the project was owned by a single vendor,” Bradstock writes.
There is also documented resistance to at least one earlier gVisor-related kernel proposal on technical grounds. As LWN reported in 2022, Linux kernel maintainers raised security and design concerns about a proposed performance improvement, including questions about its usefulness beyond gVisor.
While such interactions don’t focus on Google’s ownership as a reason for the objections, it’s clear that moving to CNCF governance should go some distance toward addressing concerns about single-vendor control.
And for Google, that effort now extends beyond gVisor. With Agent Substrate and OpenRL also moving to the CNCF, the company is hoping to establish a common foundation for autonomous agents.
“Vendor-neutral ownership lets cloud providers, hardware vendors, and independent software companies participate in the future growth of agentic workloads equally,” Bradstock writes.

articles.title: Le marché du vélo sort-il enfin du gouffre ? Le signal positif et inattendu envoyé par le géant Shimano
articles.text:
Depuis la fin du boom du Covid, le marché du vélo vit une période très délicate avec une baisse de la demande, du surstockage et de l’inflation. Les faillites ont ainsi été nombreuses, à l’image d’Accell Group, le géant néerlandais qui se voit progressivement racheter ses différentes filiales.
Des indicateurs au vert
Shimano, le fabricant japonais de transmission, freins et autres composants, qui vend aussi du matériel de pêche, a lui aussi encaissé le choc. Pour autant, ses comptes de janvier à septembre 2026, publiés le 27 octobre et détaillés par Cycling Industry News, montrent une division vélo de nouveau en hausse : 278,4 milliards de yens de ventes, soit environ 1,57 milliard d’euros, en progression de 4,6 % sur un an. Shimano fait office d’indicateur dans le secteur du vélo : suivre ses résultats permet de mieux comprendre certaines tendances et dynamiques du marché.
Plus précisément, le résultat d’exploitation de la division a augmenté de 10,9 % pour atteindre 33,4 milliards de yens, soit environ 189 millions d’euros. L’essentiel de la hausse s’est joué au troisième trimestre : d’après les chiffres trimestriels de Shimano, les ventes de composants ont grimpé de 14,3 % entre juillet et septembre, à 97 milliards de yens, et le bénéfice d’exploitation du vélo est passé de 6,5 à 13,4 milliards de yens sur la période.
Côté produits, Shimano cite le bon accueil du XTR, le fleuron de sa gamme VTT renouvelée, des séries Deore XT et Deore.
Ramené aux ventes, le vélo dégage une marge d’exploitation de 13,8 % sur le trimestre, contre 7,7 % un an plus tôt. Shimano reste tout de même loin de ses années Covid : le groupe prévoit une marge de 11,5 % sur l’ensemble de 2026 pour le vélo, soit moins de la moitié des 28 % atteints en 2021 et 2022.
Un bénéfice net multiplié par 2,5, en grande partie grâce au change
En ajoutant la pêche et les autres activités, le chiffre d’affaires du groupe atteint 375,2 milliards de yens, soit environ 2,12 milliards d’euros, en hausse de 6,9 %. Le vélo pèse donc à lui seul près des trois quarts des ventes. Le résultat d’exploitation du groupe progresse de 21,8 % à 44,5 milliards de yens, et le résultat courant, qui intègre les gains et pertes financiers, s’envole de 71,5 % à 51,9 milliards de yens, en partie grâce aux variations de change.
Enfin, le résultat net attribuable aux actionnaires bondit de 148,5 % à 40 milliards de yens, soit environ 226 millions d’euros. Ce dernier chiffre profite surtout d’une base de comparaison faible : sur les neuf premiers mois de 2025, Shimano avait enregistré une perte de change de 18,4 milliards de yens, contre 1,7 milliard cette année.
L’Europe tient
Dans l’ensemble, Shimano estime que les ventes de vélos complets en magasin sont restées globalement solides malgré l’inflation, et que les stocks du marché se sont écoulés petit à petit.
Le groupe replace par ailleurs ces chiffres dans un contexte plus large : « Au cours des neuf premiers mois de l’exercice 2026, l’économie mondiale a globalement conservé sa solidité, soutenue par l’augmentation des investissements dans les semi-conducteurs et l’intelligence artificielle et par un environnement de l’emploi dynamique. Cependant, les perspectives économiques sont restées incertaines en raison de facteurs tels que l’évolution des politiques commerciales et monétaires de divers pays et la hausse des prix de l’énergie dans un contexte de tensions croissantes au Moyen-Orient. »
En Europe, les ventes de vélos sont restées solides et les stocks se sont améliorés, notamment en Allemagne, principal marché de Shimano dans l’Union européenne. Shimano note qu’« en Europe, malgré une consommation des ménages atone due à la hausse des prix et à d’autres facteurs, le marché de l’emploi est resté solide et l’économie a montré des signes de reprise. »
En Amérique du Nord, en revanche, les ventes de vélos sont restées faibles, avec des perspectives économiques incertaines et des prix tirés vers le haut par les droits de douane. Les stocks y sont tout de même restés à un niveau approprié. Le contexte économique y est pourtant meilleur, selon Shimano : « Aux États-Unis, malgré les inquiétudes liées à la hausse des prix et aux variations des taux d’intérêt, l’économie a affiché une performance solide, soutenue par une expansion des investissements de capitaux, principalement liés à l’IA, et par un environnement de l’emploi favorable. »
Un marché asiatique en difficulté
En Asie et en Amérique centrale et du Sud, les ventes montrent des signes de reprise, mais les stocks restent assez élevés. En Chine, les VTT se sont mal vendus, notamment à cause de la météo, et la demande de vélos de route est restée faible, même si l’écoulement des stocks avance. « En Chine, l’économie a continué d’afficher de faibles performances en raison du repli du secteur immobilier et de la faible croissance de la consommation des ménages, dans un contexte de marché de l’emploi morose. »
Au Japon, enfin, les ventes au détail sont restées faibles face à des vélos toujours chers et à la hausse générale des prix, avec des stocks maintenus à des niveaux appropriés. Le groupe écrit pourtant qu’« au Japon, malgré l’impact de la hausse des prix dans un contexte de tensions croissantes au Moyen-Orient et d’évolution des taux de change, l’économie a maintenu sa reprise modérée grâce à une consommation des ménages solide, soutenue par l’amélioration des revenus. »
Pour les cyclistes, ce rebond de Shimano ne fait pas baisser les prix pour autant. Shimano applique depuis le 1er août une surtaxe temporaire de 3 % sur toutes ses commandes livrées jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026, de quoi peser sur la facture des vélos, mécaniques comme électriques, dans les prochains mois.
Malgré des marchés contrastés selon les régions, Shimano a relevé ses prévisions pour l’année 2026, qui se termine le 31 décembre. Le groupe vise désormais 495,5 milliards de yens de ventes, soit environ 2,8 milliards d’euros et 0,9 % de plus que sa précédente estimation. Il relève aussi de 15,5 % son objectif de résultat d’exploitation, à 54,3 milliards de yens, et de 9,3 % celui de résultat net.

articles.title: Écrire en boucle sans flancher : les nouvelles cartes mémoire de SanDisk visent l'endurance ultime
articles.text:
À force de filmer non stop, les caméras finissent par user leur carte mémoire. Sandisk mise sur l’endurance avec ses nouvelles microSD Guardian alors que ses SSD pour NAS et ses modèles Pokémon et Crayola complètent son offre avant les fêtes.
Le jour où l’on a besoin des images d’une dashcam suite à un accident de la circulation, mieux vaut que la carte mémoire ait tenu le coup. C’est tout l’intérêt des Guardian Series, découvertes cette semaine lors d’une journée portes ouvertes de Sandisk, qui doivent supporter les enregistrements répétés ou en continu d’une caméra embarquée ou domestique.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Filmer en boucle met la mémoire à l’épreuve
C’est une constante. En mode d’enregistrement en boucle, la caméra remplace les séquences les plus anciennes lorsque la carte mémoire est pleine. Ces cycles usent les cellules de mémoire flash, ce qui rend l’endurance aussi importante que la vitesse d’enregistrement ou de lecture. Les nouvelles cartes microSD Guardian de la marque prolongent ainsi le principe des cartes High Endurance que proposait déjà Sandisk à la vente.
La Dash Cam Card vise les caméras embarquées dans les voitures avec une résistance annoncée à la chaleur et à l’humidité. La Security Cam Card cible la surveillance domestique, notamment les caméras extérieures, avec une protection contre les températures extrêmes, l’humidité, la pluie et la poussière. Toutes deux ont des capacités de stockage qui vont de 32 à 512 Go avec jusqu’à 100 Mo/s en lecture et 40 Mo/s en écriture.
Sur la Dash Cam Card de 512 Go, Sandisk annonce jusqu’à 40 000 heures d’enregistrement en Full HD, contre 2 500 heures en 32 Go. Ces chiffres mesurent la durée cumulée supportée au fil des réécritures, d’après des tests internes.
Avec une caméra capable d’enregistrer de manière autonome, le stockage local permet aussi de garder les séquences capturées ou de continuer à filmer même quand il n’y a plus de Wi-Fi. Les prix conseillés débutent à 26 euros pour la Security Cam Card et 27 euros pour la Dash Cam Card.
Des SSD pour les NAS qui travaillent sans relâche
L’endurance compte aussi dans les NAS, ces petits serveurs, généralement domestiques, qui stockent et partagent des fichiers sur un réseau. Sandisk leur destine le NAS 600, un SSD SATA de 2,5 pouces allant jusqu’à 4 To et 560 Mo/s en lecture.
Le NAS 800 adopte lui le M.2 NVMe PCIe 5.0 et monte à 7,68 To. Disponible en quatre capacités de stockage (de 960 Go à 7,68 To), il offre des performances en lecture allant jusqu’à 14 900 Mo/s. L’endurance atteint, sur le modèle 7,68 To, 14 pétaoctets écrits, soit 14 000 To cumulés. Dans un NAS compatible, il pourra aussi bien servir de stockage principal que de disque système ou de cache pour accélérer l’accès aux données.
Pokémon et Crayola s’invitent sous le sapin
Le stockage se fait plus ludique avec la collection lancée en août pour les 30 ans de Pokémon. Mew habille une clé USB-C allant jusqu’à 128 Go, tandis que Mewtwo prête ses traits à un SSD portable de 500 Go ou 1 To, annoncé jusqu’à 1 000 Mo/s en lecture.
Au moment de la rédaction, nous n’avons pas trouvé un seul cybermarchand avec du stock dans la base de données de notre partenaire Affilizz (l’entreprise qui nous permet de réaliser nos tableaux de prix). Une bonne idée de cadeau de Noël donc, à condition de pouvoir mettre la main sur l’un de ces SSD Pokémon d’ici au 25 décembre prochain.
Enfin, les clés USB-C Crayola, sorties l’année dernière, restent également au catalogue de Sandisk avec leurs coques en forme de crayon, leurs quatre couleurs et leurs capacités de 64 à 256 Go. De quoi offrir du stockage sans avoir à expliquer, au pied du sapin et le verre à la main, ce qu’est le PCIe 5.0 à ses proches.

articles.title: Sonnensystem: Warum das Ende laut Caltech-Studie viel früher kommt
articles.text:
Caltech-Studie: Zerfällt unser Sonnensystem in nur 1 Mrd. Jahren?
Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.
Ein Team von Forscher:innen um den Astronomen Konstantin Batygin am California Institute of Technology (Caltech) im US-amerikanischen Pasadena kommt nach neuen Analysen jedoch zu einem vollkommen anderen Ergebnis. Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen
Bisherige Computermodelle gingen davon aus, dass unsere Sonne ihre äußere Hülle in der Endphase gleichmäßig abstoßen wird, wodurch sich die Umlaufbahnen der äußeren Planeten zwar ausdehnen, aber stabil bleiben. Die wahre Ursache für die nun berechnete beschleunigte Destabilisierung liegt jedoch in eben jener Art und Weise, wie der sterbende Stern seine Masse verliert.
Beobachtungen an anderen Weißen Zwergen deuten auf ein abweichendes Verhalten hin, bei dem Sterne in dieser Endphase ihre Materie oftmals asymmetrisch in Schüben abstoßen, wie Scinexx einordnet. Jeder dieser Auswürfe erzeugt einen leichten Rückstoß, der den Stern physisch bewegt, wodurch sich dieser stochastische, solare Massenverlust deutlich auf die Gravitationsverhältnisse im gesamten Sternensystem auswirkt.
Stochastische Rückstöße sorgen für Chaos
Die Forscher:innen um Batygin simulierten die zukünftigen Entwicklungen und nahmen für ein plausibles Szenario an, dass die Sonne ihre Hülle in rund 4.600 einzelnen Auswürfen abstößt. Jeder einzelne Auswurf entspricht in der Simulation dabei einem Verlust von etwa einem Zehntausendstel der ursprünglichen Sonnenmasse.
Die dadurch entstehenden Rückstöße von typischerweise sieben Metern pro Sekunde summieren sich über die Zeit und verändern die Planetenbahnen minimal, aber kontinuierlich, wie AAS Nova berichtet. Um die langfristigen Konsequenzen dieser fortlaufenden Impulse zu evaluieren, führte das Team des Caltech insgesamt 672 Simulationen mit unterschiedlichen Auswurfgrößen durch.
Instabilität beginnt schon im Riesenstadium
Diese vielen kleinen Störungen führen laut den Berechnungen der Forscher:innen dazu, dass sich die Bahnen der äußeren Planeten massiv verschieben. Bei Modellen, die Auswürfe während der gesamten Riesenphase der Sonne berücksichtigten, kam es in 37 von 48 Durchläufen bereits zu Bahnkreuzungen, bevor der Weiße Zwerg überhaupt entstanden war.
Rund 40 Prozent dieser Simulationen zeigten schon zu diesem frühen Zeitpunkt massive Zerrüttungen, durch die das Sternensystem seine bisherige Ordnung verliert. So wurde Saturn in einigen Durchläufen komplett aus dem Sonnensystem geschleudert, während in anderen Berechnungen Uranus und Neptun schlichtweg ihre Positionen tauschten.
Auch bei moderaten Auswurfmassen zeigte sich ein dynamisches Bild, bei dem den Daten zufolge eine Wahrscheinlichkeit von etwa 20 Prozent besteht, dass Jupiter und Saturn sowie Uranus und Neptun in sogenannte Bahnresonanzen eintreten. In diesen Zuständen stehen die Umlaufzeiten der Planeten in einem bestimmten Verhältnis zueinander.
Den Berechnungen zufolge schützen solche Resonanzen die Planeten jedoch nicht vor dem endgültigen Zerfall, da rund drei Milliarden Jahre nach der Entstehung des Weißen Zwergs nahezu 90 Prozent der simulierten Modellverläufe instabile Eigenschaften aufwiesen. Das bisherige Zeitfenster für ein geordnetes Ende korrigiert sich auf Basis der wahrscheinlichsten Berechnung damit von bis zu 100 Milliarden auf lediglich rund eine Milliarde Jahre.
Unsicherheiten im physikalischen Modell
Diese Zahlen stellen allerdings keine absoluten Prognosen, sondern lediglich bedingte Wahrscheinlichkeiten auf der Basis eines physikalischen Modells dar, dessen Ausgang stark von der Masse der tatsächlichen solaren Schübe abhängt. In Simulationen mit sehr geringen Auswurfmassen blieben beispielsweise mehr als 98 Prozent der Systeme dauerhaft stabil.
Ob die Sonne jene Asymmetrien entwickelt, die in den drastischeren Modellen angenommen werden, lässt sich aus den aktuellen Daten noch nicht abschließend beweisen. Beobachtungen der zukünftigen Sonne sind naturgemäß unmöglich, weshalb die Parameter auf Messungen an anderen Sternen basieren und weitere Validierungen durch astronomische Beobachtungen erfordern.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 10.10.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Máximo, 26 años: "Me vuelvo a España después de vivir 3 años en Australia, he trabajado en sitios que nunca imaginé"
articles.text:
Cuando Máximo decidió marcharse a Australia con 23 años, pensaba que solo estaría allí unos meses, pero lo que iba a ser una estancia temporal se convirtió en casi tres años lejos de España. Durante ese tiempo, trabajó en lugares que nunca imaginó y conoció a personas que le acompañaron durante una aventura que, tras cumplir 26 años, dejará atrás al volver a casa reconociendo que regresa siendo alguien muy diferente.
El joven compartió su experiencia en su cuenta de TikTok (@maximobilbao). Allí explica cómo ha cambiado su vida durante este tiempo, y asegura que la persona que se fue con 23 años no es la misma que regresa con 26, pero por desgracia no todo han sido buenos momentos. Máximo también habla de las dificultades de vivir tan lejos de casa y de lo que ha supuesto tener que adaptarse a situaciones completamente nuevas. Según explica, la experiencia le enseñó tres conceptos fundamentales: confiar más en sí mismo, cometer errores y empezar de cero en más de una ocasión.
Volver a España después de tres años en Australia ha sido una decisión personal
Aunque muchas personas deciden emigrar para encontrar mejores oportunidades laborales, Máximo defiende que su regreso no responde a ninguna obligación: "No vuelvo porque tenga que volver, vuelvo porque quiero", tal y como explicó en su vídeo. Además, también reconoce que siente que ha llegado el momento de empezar otra etapa y este es uno de sus aprendizajes principales, ya que ahora ha descubierto qué quiere hacer con su vida tras casi un lustro fuera.
Su experiencia coincide con un momento de cambios para quienes buscan trabajar en Australia. En agosto de 2026, el Gobierno australiano suspendió temporalmente nuevas solicitudes del visado Work and Holiday para ciudadanos de varios países, entre ellos España. Sin embargo, las solicitudes para españoles vuelven a estar abiertas, según la información oficial de inmigración, y el programa mantiene un cupo anual de 3.400 primeras visas para España.
Máximo, por su parte, afronta su regreso con ganas de descubrir qué le espera ahora. Como recoge El Español en su publicación sobre el joven, considera que estos tres años le han ayudado a conocerse mejor y a decidir qué quiere hacer a partir de ahora. Para él, regresar a casa no significa dar un paso atrás, sino comenzar otra etapa con todo lo aprendido en Australia.
