articles.title: Shure’s popular podcasting and streaming mic is almost $50 off
articles.text:
While the Shure Mv7 Plus is popular with streamers and podcasters, it’s equally good at impressing your friends and coworkers on meetings and Discord calls. It’s currently marked down to $255 at various retailers, including Amazon, Guitar Center, and directly from Shure. That’s almost $50 lower than its usual price, and just a few dollars off Amazon’s all-time low. If you don’t already have a stand, both Amazon and Shure are offering a bundle that includes the mic and a desktop stand for $269, and the white model is also discounted at Amazon.
Shure’s popular podcasting and streaming mic is almost $50 off
This Verge-favorite microphone for podcasting is discounted, along with other audio products.
Shure MV7 Plus
Shure’s MV7 Plus is an updated version of its popular USB microphone. The new version features a USB-C port, a customizable LED light panel, and several additional features available in the Motiv Mix app.
When our team shared some of our favorite audio gear in late 2024, we noted that the Mv7 Plus was the mic we send to podcast guests for remote interviews. It’s known for its crisp and clean audio quality, with auto-leveling and denoising, so you can use it without touching an equalizer.
The MV7’s unique shape and sonic profile is inspired by the Shure SM7B (also discounted), a microphone that’s often used in professional recording. This version is meant as a more budget-friendly variant for content creators looking for a simpler setup, with both an XLR output and USB-C, letting you wire into an audio interface or directly to a computer.

articles.title: IA soberana: la apuesta de las grandes empresas para ocultar sus datos a los tecnoligarcas estadounidenses
articles.text:
IA soberana: la apuesta de las grandes empresas para ocultar sus datos a los tecnoligarcas estadounidenses
Compañías europeas como Airbus, TotalEnergies y BMW buscan inteligencias artificiales privadas para esconderse de la vista de las tecnológicas
Desde la Comisión Europea se rema por impulsar una soberanía tecnológica que brilla por su ausencia. En los últimos años este movimiento se ha intensificado con la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial (IA) como un elefante en una cacharrería. La UE ha redoblado sus esfuerzos para intentar fabricar chips avanzados, al tiempo que promociona la construcción de centros de datos y el desarrollo de una IA propia.
Aumenta la premura, pero no tanto las opciones. En realidad es imposible tener una IA exclusivamente con tecnología hecha en Europa. Solo con los chips, de la empresa estadounidense Nvidia, ya se trunca cualquier aspiración en ese sentido. Pero en la soberanía tecnológica, como en todo, hay grados. Y uno de los más críticos es el sistema donde se introducen los datos.
El uso creciente de la inteligencia artificial en las empresas hace que los datos internos cobren cada vez mayor importancia. Y algunas compañías se muestran reticentes a que su información viaje a los servidores de OpenAI, Anthropic, Google o Microsoft para poder utilizar su inteligencia artificial.
Recurrir a los servicios de estas compañías directamente implica enviar datos confidenciales del negocio de la empresa a la nube. “La gente ha empezado a reaccionar negativamente ante estos modelos de IA. Les generan preocupación porque las empresas pierden control de sus datos, que abandonan su perímetro, ya sea este tecnológico o geográfico”, explica Charles Sansbury, director ejecutivo de la multinacional estadounidense Cloudera.
La compañía de Sansbury cubre la trastienda de las empresas, allá donde los sistemas informáticos almacenan los datos y tratan de exprimirlos. A día de hoy, parte de su negocio pasa por facilitar la aplicación de la IA a estos grandes volúmenes de información interna. Durante el evento EVOLVE 2026, organizado por Cloudera el 27 de octubre en Nueva York y al que EL PAÍS acudió invitado, la firma destacó cómo las empresas son cada vez más celosas de sus datos. Muchas de ellas prefieren ejecutar los modelos de IA en una nube privada o en sus servidores locales.
Algunas empresas llegan al extremo de aplicar esta IA a su información en equipos sin conexión a internet, para reforzar la protección de este activo tan valioso, el llamado oro del siglo XXI. “El término IA soberana tiene un matiz más geopolítico”, comenta Sansbury. “Pero en realidad se trata de controlar hacia dónde van tus datos, quién los procesa y con qué sistemas se procesan. Al final se trata de dar a los clientes las herramientas para que operen cualquier aplicación en un contexto de control que han definido previamente”.
La desconfianza creciente entre ambos lados del Atlántico y la voluntad europea de sacudirse el dominio digital de las grandes tecnológicas estadounidenses han tensado el escenario geopolítico. Y de esto se nutren las ambiciones de IA soberana. Una de las compañías mejor colocadas para aprovechar esta necesidad es la francesa Mistral.
“Es absolutamente esencial para las empresas inyectar sus datos, protegidos con su propiedad intelectual, en modelos de IA. Hay una correlación directa entre hacer esto y obtener valor de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial. Hay señales claras de que si no enriqueces los modelos con tu propiedad intelectual pierdes una ventaja competitiva respecto a otras empresas”, apunta Marjorie Janiewicz, directora de Ingresos de Mistral.
La empresa emergente francesa, asociada recientemente con Cloudera ―que ofrece sus modelos en su sistema de gestión de datos―, trabaja con grandes paladines empresariales europeos. La holandesa ASML, TotalEnergies o Airbus se cuentan entre las compañías que han introducido su información en los modelos de Mistral. Todas ellas operan en sectores altamente regulados, donde la protección de la información es aún más crítica.
Garantizar que los datos se queden en casa
La Comisión Europea ha diseñado específicamente una hoja de ruta para la digitalización y la introducción de IA en el sector energético. Este ámbito, sometido a una exhaustiva regulación, ha adquirido cada vez más importancia estratégica ante la guerra de Ucrania y el creciente aumento de los precios de la electricidad. La UE no quiere dejar la implementación de la inteligencia artificial en este sector en manos extranjeras.
Algo similar ocurre en otros ámbitos, también considerados críticos para el funcionamiento de un Estado. “Para las empresas en sectores regulados de Europa, ya sea en España, Francia, Alemania o los países escandinavos, están surgiendo normativas nacionales que previenen la salida de datos del perímetro geográfico del país”, apunta Sansbury, cuya compañía trabaja en España con gran parte del sector bancario y de telecomunicaciones.
En este escenario, para garantizar que los datos no salen de los sistemas propios de una compañía, se impone el uso de los llamados modelos de pesos abiertos. Se denominan así porque se pueden descargar —a diferencia de los de OpenAI o Anthropic— y modificar algunos de sus parámetros. Así, las empresas crean una IA ajustada a su contexto y a sus necesidades.
Pero para las compañías europeas no existen tantas opciones. “Si necesitas un modelo de IA [abierto] de calidad y necesitas que se ejecute en tus servidores, puedes recurrir a los modelos de Nvidia, pero son de Estados Unidos. Y la mitad de los modelos [abiertos] disponibles en el mercado son chinos, por lo que acarrean sus propios resquemores a nivel geopolítico”, señala Sansbury.
Es irónico que Cloudera, una compañía estadounidense aunque con presencia global, actúe como llave para impulsar la IA soberana entre las empresas europeas. Sus sistemas, basados en una estructura de código abierto, permiten introducir datos de forma privada y procesarlos con modelos de IA de diferentes proveedores. Aunque la opción preferida son los sistemas de Mistral, especialmente de cara al territorio de la UE.
Janiewicz, de la compañía francesa, ilustra con un ejemplo la utilidad de sus sistemas para las empresas: “Aplicar la inteligencia artificial es hoy muy diferente a cómo era hace solo unos años. Hoy podemos tener listos casos de uso reales en tres meses. Trabajando en pruebas de accidentes con BMW construimos muy rápido un modelo de pruebas con el que BMW acelera la evaluación de sus vehículos”.
En este caso, los datos que BMW utiliza para generar este modelo de pruebas de accidentes son demasiado valiosos como para volcarlos en los servidores de un OpenAI o Anthropic. Por muchas garantías que las políticas de estas compañías concedan sobre el papel, siempre queda un poso de inquietud. ¿Terminarán por filtrarse datos confidenciales?, ¿servirán para entrenar nuevos modelos de IA?, ¿qué ocurre si las condiciones del servicio cambian y, por tanto, el tratamiento de los datos?
Las empresas buscan evitar este tipo de incertidumbres cuando ejecutan los modelos de IA en sus propios sistemas, sin que la información viaje a la nube. Un informe de Cloudera, basado en encuestas a más de 1.500 responsables de departamentos de estas tecnologías a nivel global, indica que casi la mitad de las empresas ya ha trasladado parte de sus procesos a sistemas privados.
“Un banco, que tiene sus datos de transacciones, de depósitos y de inversiones de todos sus clientes, no quiere subir toda esta información a un sistema en la nube. No quiere poner todos esos datos, que son suyos, en un sitio fuera de su terreno”, explica Sansbury. “Lo que podemos hacer con nuestras herramientas y los modelos de IA a los que damos acceso es permitir que las empresas construyan su IA en un entorno que controlan, sin que la información salga de su perímetro de seguridad”.
En realidad, tener una IA soberana no es otra cosa que tener una IA privada. En el contexto europeo, se ha impuesto el primer término, pero el concepto alude a una preocupación básica entre las empresas: evitar el riesgo de que su información confidencial pase por manos ajenas.

articles.title: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?
articles.text:
How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?
Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos
Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.
NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA
The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.
This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.
“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”
Why Phobos Is Such a Strange Moon
Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.
The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA
Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.
More than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.
Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA
MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.
If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.
The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images
“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.
How MMX Will Orbit Phobos
An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images
Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.
“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.
From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.
Martian Maneuvers
To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.
Chris Philpot
The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.
During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.
Idefix Rover: The First Penguin
Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.
MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA
It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.
Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.
The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR
“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.
A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR
Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.
The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”
The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR
The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.
Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.
With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy
Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”
What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.
How MMX Will Land and Collect Samples
Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.
The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.
The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”
Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.
MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA
The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.
One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.
That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.
After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA
During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.
Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.
MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA
Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.
“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.
“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

articles.title: Microsoft s'attaque enfin aux lenteurs de l'application Xbox sur PC : jusqu'à 60 % de gain annoncé
articles.text:
Microsoft déploie une refonte de son application Xbox sur PC, avec un lancement annoncé jusqu’à 60 % plus rapide et une navigation repensée pour la manette. Les membres du programme Xbox Insider peuvent l’essayer dès maintenant.
Cette nouvelle appli Xbox sur PC s’attaque à ses défauts les plus connus : lenteur, interface hybride souris/manette, social noyé dans les menus. Reste à savoir si les chiffres de Microsoft tiendront hors de ses laboratoires, car ils proviennent de ses propres tests.
Des gains de vitesse chiffrés, mais « jusqu’à »
Selon Windows Central, Jason Beaumont, vice-président Xbox Experiences, a présenté cette version sur Xbox Wire. Le lancement de l’appli gagne jusqu’à 60 %, les pages Home, Store et Game Pass chargent jusqu’à 50 % plus vite, et les fenêtres internes s’ouvrent jusqu'à 65 % plus vite.
Ces valeurs viennent des tests internes de Microsoft, qui précise que les résultats varient selon la machine, la connexion et la configuration. Autrement dit, « jusqu’à » désigne le meilleur cas. Côté retours de terrain, les testeurs qui utilisent l’appli depuis quelques semaines, la jugent nettement plus rapide sur plusieurs appareils. Windows Central affirme que les à-coups ont quasiment disparu sur des machines comme la ROG Ally X, tout en rappelant que l’application reste une application web.
Bibliothèque, amis et recherche : le ménage est complet
La bibliothèque reçoit une navigation simplifiée, de nouveaux filtres et davantage d’options pour organiser les jeux installés. Les amis passent dans le menu principal, avec accès direct au chat, aux parties et à ce que jouent vos contacts.
La recherche couvre désormais jeux, titres installés, add-ons et joueurs depuis un seul endroit. Les fiches de jeux, l’accueil, les réglages et les animations sont aussi refaits. Le but affiché : une appli qui ne donne plus l’impression d’être pensée pour la souris quand vous tenez une manette.
Seul bémol relevé : la Game Bar sur consoles portables paraît désormais un peu décalée face à ce nouveau design. Microsoft prévoirait de l’harmoniser dans les prochains mois.
Comment la tester, et ce qui arrive ensuite
Pour y accéder, il faut s’inscrire au programme Xbox Insider via l’application Xbox Insider Hub du Microsoft Store. Windows Central détaille la marche à suivre : section Previews, puis « PC gaming », clic sur « Join », attente de 10 à 15 minutes jusqu’à l’affichage de « Manage », redémarrage, puis mise à jour de l’appli Xbox et du Store.
Aucune date n’est donnée pour le déploiement général sur PC. Le cloud gaming suit la même cure : la version web, testée par les Insiders plus tôt dans l’année, arrive automatiquement chez davantage de joueurs dans les semaines à venir, ou immédiatement sur play.xbox.com. Elle ajoute un onglet Bibliothèque, un mode bureau et cinq options de contraste élevé. Les applications pour téléviseurs et casques VR commencent aussi à recevoir ce nouveau visuel, sans calendrier précis.
Plus rapide, c’est bien. Mais face à Steam, qui garde une avance sur les outils communautaires et les mods, la vitesse seule ne suffira pas à convaincre les joueurs hors écosystème Xbox.

articles.title: Cybercab statt Cybertruck: Elon Musk zieht E-Pickup-Truck den Stecker
articles.text:
Cybercab statt Cybertruck: Elon Musk kündigt Aus für den E-Pickup-Truck in Texas an
Eine Million Vorbestellungen und eine eigens ausgebaute Fabrik, in der jährlich bis zu 250.000 Fahrzeuge vom Band rollen sollten – Teslas Pläne für den Cybertruck waren mindestens so voluminös wie der E-Pickup-Truck. Allerdings entwickelte sich der Cybertruck nicht zum Verkaufsschlager, sondern zum größten Flop der Autogeschichte.
Cybertruck bleibt Flop
In den drei Jahren nach dem Verkaufsstart soll Tesla insgesamt nur 70.000 bis 80.000 Exemplare des Modells verkauft haben. Einen guten Teil davon machten Verkäufe an Schwesterunternehmen wie SpaceX aus. Jetzt hat Tesla-CEO Elon Musk die Reißleine gezogen und per X ein Produktionsaus für den Cybertruck in der Gigafactory in Texas angekündigt.
Ab Mitte 2027 will Tesla demnach dort dann vermehrt Cybercab-Robotaxis herstellen. Ob er die Cybertruck-Produktion damit ganz auslaufen oder in einer anderen Fabrik weiterlaufen lassen will, ließ Musk in seinem Posting offen. Ob sich der enorme Aufwand eines Umzugs angesichts der geringen Nachfrage lohnt, ist allerdings zu bezweifeln.
Keine EU-Zulassung
Zumal der Cybertruck auf dem wichtigen E-Automarkt EU wegen Verstößen gegen Sicherheitsvorschriften bisher nicht offiziell zugelassen ist. Zudem müssten Fahrer:innen des E-Pickup-Trucks mit seinem Gesamtgewicht jenseits von 3,5 Tonnen hierzulande einen Lkw-Führerschein haben, wie es bei Golem heißt.
An der Börse gab es jedenfalls ein leichtes Aufatmen über die Musk-Pläne. Der Kurs der Tesla-Aktie, der im Anschluss an die Midterms in den USA allerdings zuvor auch stark eingebrochen war, legte nach der Ankündigung um knapp sechs Prozent zu.
Cybercab statt Cybertruck
Die noch stärkere Hinwendung zu den Cybercabs erscheint den Börsianer:innen jedenfalls vielversprechender zu sein als das Festhalten an dem unpopulären E-Pickup-Truck. In der Gigafactory in Texas sind die ersten Cybercabs ohnehin schon im April 2026 vom Band gerollt. Im Juli 2026 hatte Tesla die Produktion der Robotaxis ohne Pedale und Lenkrad weiter ausgebaut.
Derweil sind die Einsatzmöglichkeiten der autonom fahrenden Taxis aber noch auf einige wenige Städte in Texas und Florida begrenzt. An Privatpersonen darf Tesla das Fahrzeug bisher nicht verkaufen.

articles.title: GIF animés et images plus rapides : ChatGPT passe la seconde avec Images 2.6
articles.text:
OpenAI a commencé le 4 novembre à déployer Images 2.6, sa nouvelle version du générateur d’images de ChatGPT, sur le web comme dans les applications de bureau et mobiles. Au programme, des GIF animés créés depuis une simple phrase ou une photo, et une génération annoncée 50 % plus rapide par l’entreprise, qui ne précise ni la référence ni les usages mesurés. Codex, l’outil des développeurs, est servi dans la même vague.
 https://t.co/kcuOhTipYR
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) November 4, 2026
Un GIF en une phrase, retouchable image par image
La recette reprend celle des images fixes : on décrit la scène, « un chat qui danse » pour reprendre l’exemple maison, ou on téléverse une photo, et ChatGPT en tire une animation en boucle. La vitesse de lecture se règle après coup, chaque image de la séquence peut être inspectée puis corrigée individuellement, et le résultat se partage dans la foulée.
Le modèle conserve aussi des images de référence, votre visage, votre animal de compagnie ou un personnage récurrent, pour les resservir sans nouvel envoi. L’annonce ajoute aussi le balisage des images pour guider les retouches, ainsi qu’un export au format SVG. Le déploiement s’étale toutefois sur plusieurs jours : tous les comptes ne voient pas encore ces options, et OpenAI annonce la fonction pour l’ensemble des utilisateurs sans détailler d’éventuelles limites côté comptes gratuits.
Quatre milliards d’images par semaine, et la régie en embuscade
Images 2.0 ouvrait la série en avril, Images 2.5 suivait le 8 septembre : la 2.6 boucle trois versions majeures en sept mois. Dans l’intervalle, la production revendiquée est passée de 3 à plus de 4 milliards d’images par semaine, API comprise, soit un milliard gagné en moins de deux mois. OpenAI y voit la preuve d’un usage de masse, à défaut de détailler la part des différents formats dans le total.
Depuis octobre, OpenAI déploie par ailleurs aux États-Unis des publicités visuelles affichées à côté des images générées, fournies par un premier groupe d’annonceurs test et présentées comme clairement étiquetées. Le mouvement prolonge une offensive publicitaire engagée plus tôt dans l’année, puis étendue chez nous à la fin de l’été. Refuser la publicité sans payer reviendra bientôt à perdre la génération d’images, l’abonnement Plus à 20 euros par mois restant la porte de sortie officielle.

articles.title: 18,1 milliards d'euros : le cyclotourisme pèse désormais très lourd en Allemagne
articles.text:
Le Deutscher Tourismusverband (DTV), l’association qui représente le secteur du tourisme en Allemagne, a publié début novembre un rapport court qui présente les premiers résultats d’une nouvelle étude de référence, financée par le ministère fédéral des Transports (BMV). On y apprend que cyclotourisme a généré 18,1 milliards d’euros en 2026, soit environ 216 euros par habitant.
Des chiffres encourageants
Ce chiffre repose sur 319,3 millions de journées de cyclotourisme recensées en 2025. Une excursion à vélo compte pour une journée, et un voyage à vélo pour autant de journées qu’il dure. Les excursions à la journée représentent 70 % du total, contre 30 % pour les séjours avec nuitée. L’étude compte aussi les touristes qui qui font du vélo pendant un séjour culturel. Avec ce périmètre, le vélo représente environ 15 % de toutes les journées de séjour avec nuitée passées en Allemagne, et près de 7 % des journées d’excursion.
Ces dépenses ont crée 8,4 milliards d’euros de valeur ajoutée, c’est-à-dire la richesse réellement produite une fois retirés les achats intermédiaires. Les entreprises qui encaissent directement l’argent des cyclotourismes en génèrent 5,2 milliards, et leurs fournisseurs les 3,2 milliards restants. L’hôtellerie-restauration capte 51,6 % du chiffre d’affaires, contre 27,8 % pour le commerce de détail et 20,6 % pour les services comme la location de vélos ou les loisirs.
L’étude chiffre aussi les recettes fiscales à 1,7 milliard d’euros. Ces revenus équivalent au revenu moyen d’environ 244 000 personnes.
La France, deuxième destination mondiale du tourisme à vélo, estime les retombées économiques directes du cyclotourisme à 4,6 milliards d’euros en 2023, d’après une étude de la Direction générale des entreprises (DGE).
Deux fois plus d’itinéraires qu’en 2009
À noter qu’une autre étude de référence datant de 2009 ne comptait que les voyageurs dont le vélo était la raison principale du déplacement. Seule cette partie de l’activité peut donc être comparée. Elle est passée de 175 millions de journées en 2009 à un peu plus de 218 millions en 2025, soit une hausse d’environ 25 %.
Sur la même période, les dépenses quotidiennes des utilisateurs ont plus que doublé, de 16 euros à 35,70 euros, et celles des touristes qui dorment sur place ont augmenté d’environ 63 %, d’environ 64 euros à 105,30 euros. L’offre a suivi elle aussi : selon la synthèse des conclusions publiée par le DTV, le nombre d’itinéraires cyclables proposés aux touristes est passé d’environ 150 à 320. Leur longueur cumulée a doublé, d’environ 50 000 à plus de 100 000 kilomètres.
Tout n’a cependant pas progressé au même rythme. Le nombre d’hébergements certifiés Bett+Bike par l’ADFC, le club cycliste allemand, est passé d’environ 4 800 à près de 4 200, même si 20 000 à 30 000 établissements se présentent aujourd’hui comme accueillants pour les cyclistes. Surtout, l’étude relève que 84 des 96 programmes d’aide recensés financent la construction de pistes, alors que les communes manquent souvent d’argent et de personnel pour les entretenir ensuite.
27,8 millions d’intéressés
En Allemagne, 27,8 millions de personnes âgées de 14 à 74 ans se disent fortement intéressées par le vélo ou le VTT pendant leurs vacances, soit 45 % de cette tranche d’âge. Pourtant, une partie seulement passent le cap, surtout pour les longs voyages : sur les deux dernières années, 13,5 millions de personnes ont fait une excursion à vélo, 4 millions sur un court séjour et seulement 1,1 million sur un voyage plus long.
Le DTV attend surtout de nouveaux clients chez les jeunes, les familles et les citadins, mais vise aussi les seniors et les touristes étrangers : l’étude classe la France parmi ses cinq marchés prioritaires, avec les Pays-Bas, le Royaume-Uni, l’Autriche et la Suisse. Selon l’étude, les vélos électriques ont élargi le public et les distances parcourues : le pays en compte plus de 17 millions sur plus de 90 millions de vélos, et ils représentent 53 % des vélos neufs vendus.
Des meilleures infrastructures à prévoir
Reinhard Meyer, président du DTV, estime qu’il faut d’abord améliorer les conditions cyclables. Dans le communiqué du DTV, repris par le site spécialisé Pedelecs und E-Bikes, il réclame des pistes cyclables bien entretenues, de meilleures correspondances avec les bus et les trains, ainsi que des offres simples à préparer et à réserver.

articles.title: CBN sets $744,000 capital rule for crypto firms
articles.text:
Cryptocurrency companies licenced by Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will need separate central bank approval and at least ₦1 billion ($744,000) in additional capital to offer certain stablecoin payment, remittance, and custody services under new regulations.
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) will oversee stablecoins used as payment instruments, transfers, foreign exchange (FX) conversion, and settlement. The SEC retains authority over crypto trading, investments, and digital assets classified as securities, according to new regulations released Thursday evening.
The framework draws a clearer regulatory boundary for crypto businesses that combine trading with payments, requiring companies operating across both markets to secure authorisation from each regulator. It also raises compliance costs, prohibiting firms from counting the same capital toward their CBN and SEC requirements.
The division follows years of overlapping regulatory mandates and comes nearly four months after Nigeria’s President Bola Tinubu established a Virtual Asset Council to coordinate oversight of Nigeria’s cryptocurrency industry.
Under the rules, an SEC licence that permits a company to trade or hold cryptocurrencies will not automatically authorise it to use those assets to process payments or remittances. Companies seeking to offer such services must apply to the CBN for an additional authorisation specifying the activities they can undertake.
“A licence, registration or approval granted by the SEC shall not, by itself, authorise the holder to provide services [covered by the CBN’s framework],” the regulator said.
One business, two regulators
The separation of oversight could affect crypto exchanges and fintechs that combine digital asset trading with cross-border payments, merchant acceptance or stablecoin settlement.
For example, a company authorised by the SEC to facilitate cryptocurrency trading would need separate CBN approval to process stablecoin-powered cross-border or remittance payments.
The SEC has not yet issued a full operating licence to any cryptocurrency company, with 14 companies, including crypto exchanges Busha and Quidax and digital investment platforms such as GetEquity, currently participating in its Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme (ARIP). The companies are operating under approvals in principle as they work toward full registration.
The SEC has also raised the minimum capital requirement for digital asset exchanges from ₦500 million ($372,000) to ₦2 billion ($1.5 million). The rules also require new applicants to meet the higher threshold; existing operators have until June 30, 2027, to comply.
The CBN’s ₦1 billion ($744,000) capital requirement will apply to the additional services digital asset firms may provide, even where a company already meets the SEC’s minimum capital threshold. The central bank may also impose higher capital or liquidity requirements based on the scale and risks of an operator’s business.
SEC-regulated crypto exchanges seeking to offer digital asset-based payment services may need at least ₦3 billion ($2.23 million) in regulatory capital for both functions. Companies cannot count the same capital toward both requirements.
However, not every cryptocurrency transaction will require dual approval. Wallets and custody services used solely for trading, brokerage, or investment purposes will remain under the SEC. The CBN will regulate custody arrangements involving stablecoins held or transferred for payment purposes.
The regulations also establish a pathway for both regulators to cooperate, including information sharing, joint examinations, and coordinated licencing assessments. The CBN may rely on the SEC’s existing checks on a company’s governance, management, and anti-money-laundering (AML) controls when reviewing applications for additional authorisation.
The new arrangement gives crypto firms a clearer distinction between trading and payments, but also places additional regulatory and financial obligations on companies whose services extend across both activities.
It could shape how Nigerian exchanges and fintechs develop stablecoin products, particularly as digital assets play an emerging role in cross-border settlements, merchant payments, and access to FX liquidity.

articles.title: IA e automação avançam nas empresas. Mas quem está medindo o ROI?
articles.text:
Em 2024, a Gartner apontou que a hiperautomação já era disciplina central para 90% das grandes empresas, mas que menos de 20% delas dominavam a mensuração dessas iniciativas. Dois anos depois, com IA generativa e agentes no topo da agenda, vejo essa distância aumentar.
A pesquisa State of the CIO 2026, com 662 líderes de TI, mostra que só 19% consideram que suas iniciativas de IA atingiram as metas de negócio. Menos da metade (47%) tem KPIs formais, e 32% apontam métricas de ROI mal definidas como barreira para escalar. Além disso, a Gartner projeta que mais de 40% dos projetos de IA agêntica serão cancelados até 2027 por custos crescentes, valor pouco claro ou controles de risco insuficientes.
Minha leitura é que automatizar uma tarefa e comprovar seu benefício são etapas diferentes. Um sistema pode processar documentos em segundos e preencher cadastros sem intervenção humana. A pergunta que o conselho faz ao CIO é outra: o prazo de atendimento caiu? A operação ficou mais barata? Os erros diminuíram?
A hiperautomação combina IA, RPA e integração de sistemas para automatizar processos inteiros, não apenas tarefas. A avaliação precisa seguir a mesma lógica.
Uma tarefa mais rápida pode esconder um processo lento
Imagine uma empresa que automatiza a conferência de documentos: o que levava duas horas passa a levar minutos. Mas o pedido continua parado três dias à espera de aprovação. A conferência acelerou; o atendimento, quase nada.
Por isso desconfio de painéis que contam tarefas automatizadas. Quem mede apenas a etapa que recebeu tecnologia deixa de ver o gargalo que mais afeta o cliente. O indicador que importa é o tempo entre a entrada da solicitação e sua conclusão, com filas, aprovações e devoluções. É ele que mostra se o próximo avanço depende de outra automação ou de redesenhar o fluxo.
O que vale acompanhar
Os indicadores nascem do problema que motivou o projeto. Automação criada para reduzir erros se avalia pela qualidade; para acelerar o atendimento, pelo prazo de resolução. A própria Gartner resume o valor da IA agêntica em custo, qualidade, velocidade e escala. Trabalho com quatro medidas equivalentes:
Tempo: quanto leva uma demanda, da entrada à entrega?
Qualidade: quantos casos têm erro ou retrabalho?
Custo: quanto custa cada demanda concluída, incluindo a operação da tecnologia?
Capacidade: quantas solicitações a equipe atende com os recursos atuais?
Elas só fazem sentido juntas. Mais volume com mais retrabalho não é ganho; encurtar uma etapa pouco vale se a fila só muda de lugar.
Outro erro comum está no cálculo de produtividade. Uma automação que libera 100 horas por mês cria capacidade, não necessariamente economia. Esse tempo pode virar mais clientes atendidos, menos pendências ou mais análise humana, benefícios reais desde que comprovados após a implantação. Converter toda hora liberada em economia infla a expectativa de retorno; mas redução de custo só existe quando uma despesa efetivamente cai.
A conta precisa incluir licenças, integrações, manutenção, consumo de nuvem e de modelos e tratamento de exceções. Um levantamento da Gartner com 353 líderes de dados e IA mostra que só 44% das organizações adotaram práticas de FinOps ou limites financeiros para IA. Solução que exige correções manuais frequentes consome parte do ganho que prometia.
A medição começa antes da tecnologia
Não há comparação sem linha de base. Antes de automatizar, é preciso registrar quanto o processo leva, quanto custa e com que frequência falha. Depois, os mesmos indicadores mostram o que mudou e revelam perdas causadas por novas regras, aumento de demanda ou mudanças nos sistemas.
Esse trabalho é compartilhado. A TI acompanha a execução da solução; a área dona do processo verifica o efeito nas entregas; finanças valida o retorno quando a meta é financeira. Defendo que cada iniciativa tenha um patrocinador técnico e outro de negócio, corresponsáveis pelo resultado.
Ampliar uma automação deve ser decisão baseada em evidência. Prefiro financiar resultados, não entregas, com revisões em marcos como 90, 180 e 270 dias. Se o prazo caiu, a qualidade subiu e o custo por demanda diminuiu, há base para escalar. Se o ganho ficou restrito a uma etapa, o trabalho não terminou: é preciso descobrir o que ainda trava o processo.
Tiago Amor é CEO da Lecom, plataforma pioneira em hiperautomação de processos. Especialista em Gestão de Projetos (FGV) e formado em Sistemas da Informação (UNESP).

articles.title: He probado el Lepas L6 PHEV en China: ¿va a reventar el mercado este nuevo SUV?
articles.text:
En el reciente viaje que hice a China para cubrir el Chery User Summit tuve la ocasión de probar muchas de sus novedades. Vimos el Lepas Aura como parte de la Lepas Elegance Week y, también, pudimos conducir el Lepas L6 PHEV. Un vehículo de unos 4,5 metros de longitud que la marca ha confirmado que llegará a España próximamente.
Lepas, para los que aún no la tengan correctamente ubicada, es la nueva marca del grupo Chery (Omoda, Jaecoo y, en cierto porcentaje, también Ebro) en desembarcar en nuestro país. La red de concesionarios está en plena expansión y, en estos momentos, ya comercializan el Lepas L8, un SUV también híbrido enchufable que trata de diferenciarse de sus hermanos, sobre todo, por su diseño y puesta a punto más europea.
El Lepas L6 toma esa misma dirección pero en un formato algo más compacto y, también, más económico. El vehículo llegará tanto en versiones eléctricas como en híbrida enchufable. Nosotros, por el momento, solo hemos podido probar la enchufable por las carreteras de China. Y este es un vehículo interesante porque, en el mercado español, los SUVs de estas dimensiones e híbridos enchufables están ganando mucha cuota de mercado.
La elegancia y refinamiento, el factor diferencial de Lepas L6
Ya cuando probamos el Lepas L8 nos dimos cuenta de ese carácter algo diferente a otros hermanos del grupo Chery. Detalles como la suspensión, algo más europeizada, o las líneas de diseño, que en ciertos aspectos recuerda a lo que vienen haciendo marcas europeas de primer nivel.
En el caso del Lepas L6, esa sensación se repite. Las líneas son más curvas y menos angulosas que en otros modelos de Chery en Europa. También tiene rasgos, como los faros afilados, que tratan de dar ese carácter “felino” que buscan sus diseñadores.
En el interior también se desmarca de otros modelos del grupo Chery, si bien hay elementos claramente comunes. Tenemos una pantalla central de 13,2 pulgadas bastante buena en comportamiento –lleva chip de Qualcomm detrás– que se “fusiona” con la zona del climatizador, los cargadores, el reposabrazos, etc. Frente al conductor, una pantalla de 8,8 pulgadas que actúa como cuadro de mandos. No es inmensa, aunque tampoco lo considero necesario. Muchas marcas chinas se empeñan en poner pantallas inmensas en el cuadro de mandos que no siempre se aprovechan a nivel de software o incluso quedan “tapadas” por partes del volante. Eso sí: en la del Lepas L6 creo que algunos elementos del cuadro deberían ser algo más grandes y otros, en cambio, más pequeños o desaparecer. Pero eso es ir muy al detalle, soy consciente.
Volviendo a la zona central, un par de detalles del Lepas L6 muy bienvenidos son la botonera bajo la pantalla para controlar el climatizador de manera rápida, así como la integración de un cargador inalámbrico con rejilla de ventilación. Esto último para mi es fundamental. De nada sirve tener un cargador de este tipo si el teléfono se termina calentando en exceso y, por consiguiente, se interrumpe la recarga o el funcionamiento de sistemas como Android Auto o Apple CarPlay.
En cuanto a comportamiento dinámico, se repiten las sensaciones que tuvimos con el Lepas L8. Lo principal: la suspensión y dirección son algo más duras y ágiles que en otros vehículos chinos. Eso no significa que sea un coche incómodo o de corte deportivo. No deja de ser un SUV cuyo principal enfoque es la comodidad durante viajes o trayectos diarios. Pero sí responde mejor en una amplia variedad de situaciones.
Una combinación conocida
En cuanto a la unidad de potencia del Lepas L6, encontramos una combinación clásica en Chery. Un motor de combustión interna de 1.5 litros turboalimentado acompañado de un sistema eléctrico que entrega un total de 279 CV, promete una autonomía eléctrica de unos 90 KM y una autonomía total combinada de unos 1.100 KM.
Este sistema puede funcionar en diferentes modos: solo en eléctrico, con la parte eléctrica asistiendo al motor de combustión interna, solo en modo de combustión, con el motor de combustión actuando como generador para recargar la batería... El vehículo, eso sí, alterna de manera automática e inteligente entre todos ellos en función de lo que le estemos pidiendo (velocidad, pendiente, aceleración, etc.) y el modo de conducción seleccionado. Podemos cambiar algunos parámetros, pero el grueso de la gestión la hace de manera autónoma e invisible al usuario.
En cuanto a la respuesta, es más que correcta para el tamaño del vehículo. Ágil en incorporaciones, silencioso en la mayoría de momentos y con una autonomía eléctrica que, a falta de probarlo en profundidad, parece más que suficiente para cubrir los trayectos diarios sin gastar ni un ápice de gasolina.
Respecto a los consumos, poco podemos aportar más allá de las cifras del fabricante sobre el Lepas L6. Si bien tuvimos ocasión de probarlo en ciudad, autovía y carreteras rurales, sería necesario un test más prolongado para poder determinar su rendimiento en este sentido.
Para finalizar, en lo que respecta a espacio interior, se trata de un vehículo amplio en el que pueden viajar cuatro adultos de manera holgada y cinco de manera algo más ajustada. Su maletero es de 435 litros. No es un maletero de referencia en su segmento, pero sí es suficiente para realizar viajes.
Lepas L6: precio y disponibilidad
El Lepas L6 llegará a España en 2027 tanto en versiones híbridas enchufables como en eléctricas. La compañía no ha confirmado aún los precios, pero, considerando que el Lepas L8 se vende por 33.000€ contando todas las ayudas y descuentos posibles, cabe la posibilidad de que este se sitúe justo por debajo de los 30.000 euros contando también con todas las promociones y descuentos posibles.
Un precio parejo al de vehículos del grupo Chery como el Omoda 7, y también a propuestas de Kia, Volkswagen, etc. Eso sí: el Lepas llega bastante bien equipado de serie, sobre todo si se compara con propuestas europeas.

articles.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
articles.text:
HBM smuggling routes into China; Nvidia H200s held in Hong Kong; Micron pauses Taiwan fab work; Samsung expands HBM base-die capacity; Oracle-Tencent AI chip deal collapses; Bosch builds out semiconductors; S. Korea boosts AI and chip spending; Marvell-Lumentum deal draws scrutiny; more acquisitions, market reports and earnings.
HBM from Samsung and SK hynix is reportedly reaching Chinese AI chip developers through smuggling operations that exploit U.S. export-control loopholes. According to The Information, intermediaries package HBM with low-performance server processors, ship the combined components to China, and then remove the memory for resale, including to customers of Huawei.
Approximately 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are being held in Hong Kong awaiting approval for shipment to mainland China, according to Reuters. Beijing has limited imports in an effort to reduce reliance on U.S. technology and encourage adoption of domestically developed processors.
Micron reportedly paused construction of a $4.5B memory-chip plant in Taiwan due to a prolonged labor dispute, according to Bloomberg. Micron has not confirmed the suspension, and the effect on its longer-term Taiwan manufacturing plans remains unclear.
Samsung Electronics is reportedly planning to expand advanced foundry capacity for HBM base dies at two locations.
Separately, Samsung reportedly secured orders from AMD and Nvidia for 2nm HBM base dies to be produced at a proposed second foundry in Taylor, Texas, with mass production targeted for 2030. Note: Samsung has not confirmed the reported Giheung investment or Taylor customer orders.
Oraclereportedly canceled a 5-year agreement worth an estimated $7B to provide Tencent access to up to 100,000 advanced AI chips through data centers in Southeast Asia, following pressure from the Trump administration, according to the Financial Times. U.S. officials raised concerns about Chinese companies accessing advanced processors through overseas cloud services, while officials in China’s Guangdong province urged Tencent to use domestically developed chips.
Bosch plans to establish a dedicated semiconductor division in January 2028, expanding its foundry business and opening more manufacturing capacity to external customers. The company is targeting €5B in semiconductor sales by 2030 and plans to expand its semiconductor test center in Penang, Malaysia, by the mid-2030s.
Marvell‘s pending acquisition of Lumentum, initially valued at $115B, is drawing mixed reactions, with analysts seeing opportunities to challenge Broadcom in AI optical interconnects, but also raising concerns about supplier concentration and customer relationships. Questions about the purchase price and regulatory approval have added to investor concerns.
U.S. election results raised concerns about tighter restrictions on data center development, particularly in major markets such as Texas and Ohio, as well as increased congressional oversight of AI, including AI safety, cybersecurity, and industry practices. Restrictions that delay or reduce data center construction could weaken demand for AI accelerators, HBM, and networking chips, and increased regulatory scrutiny could create additional uncertainty for AI infrastructure investment. (See chip stock impacts here.)
More acquisitions and deals
Onsemiconfirmed it plans to acquireFerric, developer of integrated voltage regulators, for $600M in cash, plus up to $175M in milestone payments.
EntegrisacquiredAdvanced Abrasives and announced plans for a new SiC materials manufacturing line in Taiwan. The company also partnered with Element Six to develop diamond-based thermal-management materials for advanced packaging and expanded its deal with Kioxia on BiCS Flash 3D flash memory.
Supermicro is initially planning to use 10,000 SambaNova SN50 RDUs for its new AI disaggregated inference systems as part of a strategic collaboration.
AI data centers are moving toward 800 VDC power distribution as rack power rises toward megawatt levels, with Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and other industry participants working through OCP on common architectures and interfaces.
Events and Webinars— ACM/IEEE ICCAD, Electronica & SEMICON Europe. Webinars on shift left, verification, and debug of high-power motor controllers.
Global
Americas
UC San Diego and Qualcomm launched a $750K AI-driven chip-design research initiative, funded by a $500K Qualcomm gift and $250K in UCSD matching funds, focused on AI methods for SoC design, processor architectures, hardware accelerators, memory systems, and interconnects.
CSIS examines Albany NanoTech as a model for semiconductor technology clusters, highlighting shared R&D infrastructure, industry partnerships, and workforce development supporting sub-2nm technologies, advanced packaging, photonics, and quantum systems.
The OCPFoundation is opening nominations for project leads across all 12 top-level OCP Projects, ranging from hardware management to the AI computing continuum.
Europe
The European Semiconductor Industry Association (ESIA) called for dedicated semiconductor funding under the EU’s 2028–2034 budget, including support for R&D, pilot production, advanced packaging, and industrial deployment. The association urged policymakers to coordinate national and EU funding, preserve the Chips Joint Undertaking’s cross-sector role, and ease restrictions on intellectual property transfers within multinational companies.
Synopsys and the EU Chips JU signed a deal to expand access to its EDA software for semiconductor startups and research teams through the EuroCDP.
Asia
South Korea reaffirmed plans to spend ₩21.3T (US$16B) on AI and major initiatives covering semiconductors, physical AI, and data centers, in its proposed 2027 budget, nearly doubling this year’s allocation.
Panasonic Industry plans to invest about ¥92B ($583M) to expand AI-related materials production and R&D, including circuit-board materials, capacitors and semiconductor packaging materials.
Two workers were killed and five injured in an explosion and fire at Panasonic Industrial Devices Materials‘ factory in Hsinchu, Taiwan. The facility produces PCB and semiconductor packaging materials. The cause and production impact have not been determined yet.
South Korea’s Techwing plans to invest approximately ₩52.6B ($39M) in a new semiconductor equipment factory in Cheonan to expand production of memory test handlers and HBM cube probers.
Infineon introduced its first automotive MCU platform based on the RISC-V architecture, adding hardware-based physical protection and crypto agility, with support planned for post-quantum security requirements.
Infineon and Qualcomm are collaborating on a microcontroller-based subsystem for Snapdragon Ride reference platforms used in central car computers for automated driving and digital cockpit applications.
STMicro announced a new microcontroller portfolio covering industrial, automotive, and physical AI applications.
Test, measurement
Keysight released XR3, a low-profile 14-bit oscilloscope designed to increase measurement capacity in rack-based test systems.
Siemens introduced an automated component model extraction solution developed with Bosch that cuts frequency-response-function measurement time by up to 93% and produces ISO 20270-compliant models for virtual NVH development.
Cerabyte completed S3 integration testing of its ceramic data storage within established object-storage workflows, in collaboration with CERN openlab.
Design
Arteris exceeded 1,000 customer silicon design starts using its interconnect IP, and released a report showing the evolution of SoC, ASIC, FPGA, and MCU designs across key markets.
Research
MCL, PVA TePla and ASE researchers developed an AI-based image-enhancement method for detecting flip-chip interconnect defects. By improving scanning acoustic microscopy images, the method increased detection of cracks and delamination in extreme-low-k dielectric layers from 5.2% to 100% in tests involving 19 defects across three packages.
TU Munich, Applied Materials et al. evaluated cryogenic 2nm GAA transistors and superconducting interconnects for energy-efficient AI computing. Using a calibrated chip-design flow, they reported a 3x performance increase and 7.7x improvement in energy efficiency for a modeled AI accelerator’s compute fabric, excluding memory, data movement, and refrigeration power.
ETH Zurich-led researchers benchmarked 10 commercial sub-watt edge AI devices, comparing inference performance and energy consumption across convolutional neural networks and small vision transformers. The study found that memory traffic, rather than computational workload, was the primary factor determining latency on the tested neural-network accelerators, highlighting the importance of data movement in low-power AI hardware design.
HUST and PolyU researchers developed annealing-free ferroelectric transistors with ultrathin oxide-semiconductor channels for NVM and neuromorphic computing. The devices achieved a memory window of up to 20.6V, endurance of 10⁶ cycles, and stable 6-bit operation across 64 states. A neuromorphic network evaluation achieved 93.02% recognition accuracy.
AMD issued security bulletins covering a newly discovered EDK II PXE driver vulnerability that can allow pre-boot code execution and a contention-based side-channel technique for exploiting known vulnerabilities in AMD CPUs.
Dell issued BIOS updates for a critical Qualcomm chipset vulnerability affecting five Latitude, Inspiron, and XPS systems. The flaw can cause memory corruption when a malformed RSA key is imported into Qualcomm’s Keystore.
Google banned Videostrong Technology from making certified Android devices after its security researchers determined that the company was responsible for creating an XCPE backdoor that enrolled 1.3 million set-top boxes into a criminal botnet.
Vietnam has its first-ever homegrown security chip after government-backed Viettel Group successfully integrated a domestically developed cryptographic algorithm into silicon.
u-blox announced that it will integrate Kudelski Labs’ embedded security IP into its future chipsets.
Chinese tech giant Tencent released Hy4, its powerful new open-source AI model. Amid growing concerns about agentic hacking, the company said it limited the model’s cybersecurity training data to defensive material only.
Security technical papers
NC State and Princeton researchers proposed a 3D-stacked hardware shield to protect post-quantum cryptography accelerators from side-channel attacks. The design stacks a guard layer above the cryptographic hardware, using decoy-key activity and physical shielding to obscure power leakage from NTT computations.
Accelerating Plug-And-Play Prototyping In Chiplet-Based Designs: Purna Mohanty, CEO of SignatureIP, talks about the impact of chiplets and shared memory resources, the challenges of version control across multiple flavors of I/O, and the challenges engineering teams face when hardware-accelerated tools are running at different speeds than the actual design.
Quantum Hardware
New launches
Universal Quantum launched its iQPU quantum processor, combining a large trapped-ion compute surface, ultra-low-noise integrated control electronics, and chip-to-chip interfaces designed to scale quantum computing systems. The processor is manufactured on a commercial 200mm semiconductor production line.
IBM, ORNL, and AMD opened a new co-design platform for quantum error correction at IBM’s quantum facility in New York, co-locating the 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk with ORNL’s Umbra HPC system.
Fig. 1: ORNL’s Umbra HPC system. Source: Oak Ridge National Lab
Advances
Researchers from Quantum Motion, UCL, and others demonstrated a superconducting circuit element fabricated using a commercial CMOS process. The titanium-nitride device functions as a compact superinductor and was integrated with a silicon quantum dot to enable sensitive RF charge detection, potentially supporting more compact readout hardware for semiconductor spin qubits.
University of Regensburg-led researchers demonstrated a real-time feedback technique that reduced superconducting-qubit operation errors by approximately 54%, from 0.14% to 0.065%. The approach identifies changes in qubit resonance frequency associated with material defects and adjusts control signals to improve reliability.
Alice & Bob reported extended bit-flip lifetimes in superconducting cat qubits, averaging 44 minutes on a single-qubit test device and reaching 189 to 252 minutes on selected qubits in its 12-qubit Helium 2 processor. The preliminary results demonstrate strong suppression of bit-flip errors during idle operation, with performance during error-correction operations still to be validated.
Workforce, Education
The U.S. Department of Labor opened applications for a $40M apprenticeship incentive fund that includes semiconductor fabrication among several high-growth sectors. Registered apprenticeship sponsors can receive up to $6K per eligible new apprentice.
UCLA named the first 10 doctoral fellows in its Semiconductor Hub, with research spanning 3D ICs, advanced packaging, silicon photonics, compute-in-memory, and AI hardware. Fellows will also intern with one of the Hub’s industry partners, including Synopsys, GlobalFoundries, and others.
In a new Semiconductor Engineering roundtable, industry experts discuss how AI is changing expectations for new engineering graduates. Demand for electrical engineers remains strong, but AI agents are taking over some traditional junior-level tasks, raising expectations for practical experience, AI fluency, and the ability to tackle higher-level engineering work earlier in their careers.
U.S. community colleges are expanding semiconductor technician training programs as the industry faces a potential shortage of 157,000 workers by 2030, according to the Associated Press. More than 200 colleges and universities are coordinating with semiconductor manufacturers, including TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and SK hynix, to develop hands-on training programs supporting new U.S. fabs.

articles.title: Assez rapides pour faire Paris-New York en 10 minutes : les sondes Escapade foncent enfin vers Mars
articles.text:
Pour propulser un vaisseau jusqu’à Mars, il ne suffit pas de l’envoyer dans la bonne direction et de le laisser filer en ligne droite. Afin de réaliser des économies de carburant, les satellites qui quittent la Terre vont suivre un parcours sinueux et contre-intuitif qui va leur permettre de gagner de la vitesse progressivement en profitant de la force gravitationnelle des planètes.
C’est comme ça qu’a fonctionné Escapade. Composée de deux sondes jumelles, la mission Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers a décollé il y a presque un an, le 13 novembre 2025, à bord de la fusée New Glenn de Blue Origin. Mais à ce moment-là, la Terre et Mars se trouvaient de part et d’autre du Soleil, la pire position pour partir vers la planète rouge. Les deux sondes ont donc décrit une grande boucle en forme de haricot autour du point de Lagrange L2 du système Soleil-Terre, situé à 1,5 million de kilomètres de la Terre, là où se trouvent aussi les télescopes James Webb et Euclid.
Vers Mars à Mach 31
Dans un communiqué publié ce lundi 2 novembre, la Nasa annonce que la Terre et Mars sont enfin bien placées pour que les deux sondes partent vers Mars. Le premier passera ce samedi 7 novembre vers 11 heures (heure de Paris), le second le lundi 9 novembre vers midi. Les deux vaisseaux vont entamer une manœuvre de mécanique orbitale connue sous le nom de TMI, ou en français « injection trans-martienne ».
L’idée est d’attendre que les vaisseaux passent au plus près de la Terre, entre 970 et 1 770 kilomètres d’altitude. C’est là que la gravité terrestre les fait filer le plus vite, et c’est à ce moment qu’un allumage du moteur leur fait gagner le plus de vitesse. Une fois ce point atteint, leurs moteurs s’allumeront pendant environ neuf minutes afin de les propulser vers la planète rouge.
Les vaisseaux vont ainsi gagner plus de 1 600 km/h et passer d’environ 10,1 à 10,8 km/s, de quoi relier Paris à New York en un peu moins de dix minutes. Lancés à environ Mach 31, les deux vaisseaux Escapade suivront pendant dix mois une trajectoire courbe autour du Soleil, corrigée en route par plusieurs manœuvres, avant d’arriver sur Mars les 7 et 9 septembre 2027.
Des jumeaux observateurs de plasma
Une fois là-bas, leur périple ne sera pas terminé. Les deux sondes devront passer plusieurs mois à abaisser et synchroniser leurs orbites, avec une coupure des communications pendant la conjonction solaire de la fin 2027, quand le Soleil se trouvera entre la Terre et Mars. Leurs observations scientifiques ne commenceront qu’à la mi-2028.
Pourquoi ne pas avoir fait partir Escapade lorsque la Terre et Mars étaient bien alignées ? Cette fenêtre de tir ne s’ouvre que quelques semaines tous les 26 mois. Escapade devait partir pendant celle de l’automne 2024, sur le tout premier vol de New Glenn. En septembre 2024, la Nasa a retiré ses sondes de ce vol, car la fusée de Blue Origin ne serait pas prête avant la fermeture de la fenêtre, fin octobre. L’équipe a alors conçu une trajectoire inédite pour partir sur le deuxième vol de la fusée. Ce départ anticipé a aussi permis aux sondes de traverser une région lointaine de la magnétoqueue, la partie du champ magnétique terrestre étirée par le vent solaire, qu’aucun engin n’avait encore explorée directement. L’équipe scientifique doit publier ses résultats prochainement.
Une fois autour de Mars, les deux vaisseaux pourront analyser le plasma de l’environnement martien d’une nouvelle manière. En se suivant sur la même orbite, à quelques minutes d’intervalle, les deux sondes pourront voir comment la structure et la composition de ce plasma changent d’un instant à l’autre. Aucune mission n’avait encore fait voler deux engins coordonnés autour de Mars.
